13:20.race_name: Tally Ho Stud Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners.comment: Brother to Group-placed 1m1f 2yo winner Endorsement; Moore's pick
runners.name: Sergei Diaghilev
runners.owner: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith
runners.spotlight: Wootton Bassett colt; second foal; brother to Group-placed 1m1f 2yo winner Endorsement (RPR 107), also Group-placed over 1m2f at 3 in 2026; dam unraced sister to winners Johannes Vermeer (7f 2yo Group 1; runner-up in Melbourne Cup) and Elizabeth Browning (1m1f Group 2); trip looks on the short side on his breeding but Ballydoyle first-choice on jockey bookings.

runners.comment: Blue Point colt related to some decent 2yos; yard in top form so has to be respected
runners.name: Folsom Blues
runners.spotlight: Blue Point colt is closely related to 7f AW 2yo winner Greek Mythology (RPR 99), half-brother to 7f/1m winner Atlantic Coast (inc 2yo Group 3/Australia; 104); dam Group-placed 9.5f winner (95), half-sister to useful 1m2f winner Groundbreaking; yard in top form so newcomer has to be respected.

runners.comment: Brother to 5f/6f 2yo winner First Approach
runners.name: Bold Commander
runners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
runners.spotlight: No Nay Never brother to 5f/6f 2yo winner First Approach (RPR 89), half-brother to winners Lisboa (1m2f; 84) and Sound It Out (Australian 7f-1m); dam Group-placed 6f winner (109), closely related to useful 7f/1m winner Aerion Power; seemingly Ballydoyle second-choice but don't rule out.

runners.comment: Kodiac colt, out of a Galileo half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Besharah
runners.name: Switching Sides
runners.spotlight: Kodiac colt bought back for 52,000euros as a yearling; dam placed 1m3f/1m4f (RPR 76), half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Besharah; needs checking in the market on debut.

runners.comment: Debutant respected from a yard with a decent recent 2yo winner
runners.name: Winnies Wish
runners.spotlight: Coulsty colt a 10,000euros foal and 35,000euros yearling; brother to 7f 2yo winner Madbadanddangerous (RPR 86), half-brother to winners Marvelosa (10.4f; 84) and Mulsanne (US 1m turf); dam unraced sister to 1m4f Listed winner, closely related to Gold Cup winner Courage Mon Ami; debutant respected from a yard with a decent recent 2yo winner.

runners.comment: Half-brother to 2yo Group 2 winner High Definition
runners.name: South Dakota
runners.owner: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
runners.spotlight: St Mark's Basilica half-brother to winners High Definition (1m 2yo inc Group 2, RPR 120), Innisfree (1m Group 3/7f 2yo; 110) and Royal Aide (1m3f/11.7f Flat, 86; 3m/3m1f hurdle); dam 1m and 8.4f (Listed) winner (104); seemingly the Ballydoyle third-choice but worth a look for future reference.

runners.comment: Speedily bred sort but this likely a strong maiden
runners.name: I Ready
runners.spotlight: Invincible Army gelding; 10,000 yearling; second foal; dam runner-up 6f 2yo (RPR 74), half-sister to winners Insignia Of Rank (1m Listed) and Mayleaf Shine (useful 5f inc 2yo); speedily bred sort but this likely a strong maiden.

runners.comment: Never recovered from bad start on recent Navan debut; best watched for now
runners.name: Dhikola
runners.owner: Walerc Limited/M J Wasylocha/Tony Cantwell/Paul J Nolan
runners.spotlight: Ardad colt cost 45,000GBP as a yearling; third foal; closely related to Spanish 1m winner Running Hot, half-brother to 6f turf 2yo/1m AW winner Priapos (RPR 84); dam 5.7f winner (76), half-sister to winners Global Applause (5f Listed inc 2yo) and Auditor (useful 5f-7f inc 2yo); never recovered from bad start on recent Navan debut; best watched for now.

13:55.race_name: Sherry FitzGerald Country Homes Orby Stakes (Listed Race)

runners.comment: Smart last year and promises to make an even better 4yo upped to this trip; big player
runners.name: Purview

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Navigation Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: He works very well, I probably rode Purview with too much confidence at Leopardstown and the ground last time at Deauville was much quicker than the description. Today, with the ease in the ground he showed what he's capable of. Hopefully he'll keep progressing - Colin Keane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Smart, lightly raced 4yo; never quite fulfilled Leopardstown's Derby Trial second this time last year although did end the campaign on a winning note in 1m2f Cork Listed in September in ready fashion; looks the type to make an even better 4yo upped to this trip; very interesting player.

runners.comment: Ex-German trained filly; Group 1-placed in Italy; choice of Joseph O'Brien's four
runners.name: Nyra
runners.spotlight: German import, having been bought for 875,000euros at Arqana in December; 1-9 for previous yard, winning Group 3 in Hamburg over 1m3f (good) and better form when beaten a neck in Group 2 at Baden-Baden and final start when third in 1m4f Group 1 Gran Premio del Jockey Club in Milan; McMonagle's choice of Joseph O'Brien's quartet so has to be respected.

stable_tour.quote: She was placed in the German Oaks last year and has some nice form lines. We like what we see of her and we're aiming to start her around the second half of May. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Last year's winner well below best on recent return; entitled to improve for that
runners.name: Trustyourinstinct

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai International Stakes In Honour Of Kevin Prendergast (Group 3)
quotes.quote: You can set your clock by Trustyourinstinct. He turns up and runs his race everyday. He is a multiple stakes winner and he loves the Curragh. He won at the track on Guineas weekend and he backed it up here up in class and down in trip with a penalty. It wasn't an easy task today. I thought he was impressive and I think that run is right up there with his best. When he won the last day he needed to fight  out the finish but today he showed a turn of foot off the turn and Dylan [Browne McMonagle, jockey] said he felt really sharp off the bend. It was a smart performance and he is going the right way.   I imagine the horse will travel somewhere in the Autumn whether it is to Kentucky for the mile and half, million and half dollar race or to Australia. To be quite honest a horse like him has loads of options for good pots and he's a gelding so we will be looking all the big prize money options in the Autumn. He won over hurdles but he wasn't the most natural jumper. He has really found his niche now - Joseph O'Brient, trainer.

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Orby Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Trustyourinstinct is a lovely horse, very consistent and loves it here at the Curragh. I'm delighted to have a nice winner for JP. He's a home-bred of JP and Noreen's and everybody will get an extra kick out of that. He always turns up and runs his race. He was behind Los Angeles here the last day, it was a very credible run, and dropping down into Listed class today he's won impressively. He's well enough handicapped over hurdles but he doesn't really jump with great fluency. He'll probably stick to the Flat. He's a very solid Listed/Group 3 horse and he pays his way every year. We've ran him internationally a few times as well and we might look at that again at a later date. He particularly loves the Curragh and it's not a bad place to have a rapport with. - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Tonybet "We're Here To Play" Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We weren't sure about the mile-and-a-half trip as his best runs had been at ten but Trustyourinstinct really got the trip well. He qualifies for a lot of big pots around the world as we get into the autumn so he could potentially end up in a race internationally - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Ballyduff Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Trustyourinstinct was a classy enough horse on the flat and it's probably taken him a while to get his act together over hurdles. It was a weak race and so we just kept it simple - Simon Torrens, rider

quotes.race: Bet Builder At Novibet Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Trustyourinstinct looks a nice horse. We thought he'd run well and he'll have learned a lot. He was green in the middle of the race there but I thought he went to the line well. It was a good performance on debut - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Good form early last season, recording back-to-back wins here in today's event and Group 3 International Stakes over 1m2f; subsequent Leopardstown efforts were below best below best, as was last month's seasonal return here in 1m2f Group 3 Alleged Stakes dominated by two stablemates; entitled to come on for that.

stable_tour.quote: He showed some really good form last year, winning a Group 3 at Leopardstown over a mile and a half and just touched off in a Group 2 in Italy in October. We were happy with his run when third in the Devoy Stakes, but the set-up of the race wasn't ideal for him. Depending on ground, he could go for the Mooresbridge next. 24-04-25
He won two races on the Flat for us and he will start off in the next month in a juvenile hurdle. We're looking forward to getting him out over hurdles and his schooling has been good. 27-11-23

runners.comment: Two narrow defeats at this level recently; this looks a much deeper race though
runners.name: Snapretend
runners.spotlight: Very useful filly has returned this term with 0.5l defeats by Moody at Listed level at both Cork (1m4f) and Gowran (1m6f), each time forcing it; this a much deeper race than those however so will do well to sneak a place.

runners.comment: Recent maiden hurdle winner; cheekpieces fitted for Flat return and bit to find on ratings
runners.name: Arouet
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced last year at 3, winning minor Roscommon contest and chased home a very smart type in Leopardstown Listed over this trip; recently landed odds in Cork 4yo maiden hurdle, an unusual prep for one from this yard; cheekpieces fitted for Flat return and bit to find on ratings.

runners.comment: Possible fitness edge on some of these but ideally wants further at this stage
runners.name: Emit

quotes.race: Qatar Prix Chaudenay (Group 2) (3yo) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Emit ran a smashing race, too. It was great to see him run so well - Kevin Blake, trainer's representative.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: He was game and tough. Emit was unlucky in the Curragh in that group race where he came out the worst of it and Ascot didn't really go to plan. We decided to come here up in distance and he seemed to really enjoy it. He fought really well. Dylan (Browne McMonagle) said he'd even go a 1m6f. I suppose he's into group races now - Joseph O'Brien, trainer

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Emit is a grand horse. He didn't get the message to go past but when he did he was snug at the line. He's a lovely staying colt - Declan McDonogh, rider.

runners.spotlight: Consistent last season, going close in 1m2f Group 3 Gallinule Stakes on this weekend and later in year twice runner-up in Longchamp Group contests over 1m7f; both runs this term at 1m6f, latest when respectable third to Scandinavia in Navan Listed; possible fitness edge on some of these.

stable_tour.quote: He finished off last year well and he'll probably go down the staying route. It was a nice run when he was fourth on his comeback and I expect him to step forward nicely from that. We're looking at going to Navan or Chester next. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Absent since 1m Listed win in September; this trip stretches him
runners.name: Cristal Clere

prev_owners.owner: G & M Roberts Green Savidge & Whittal-Williams

quotes.race: Edmund & Josie Whelan Memorial Listowel Stakes (Listed)
quotes.quote: If ever a horse deserved to win a Listed race, it was Cristal Clere as he's been knocking on the door. He got stuck a bit in the ground yesterday and just isn't as competitive with a lot of horses around him - he likes to have his own way. For a horse we bought to go point-to-pointing at Belharbour, he's turned out all right and has been lucky for us - John Nallen, trainer.

quotes.race: SHEIN Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Cristal Clere had great runs last summer and is a really consistent horse. He took off on the soft ground the other day and again today - John Nallen, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Third career win came on final start last season in 1m Listowel Listed in testing conditions under a positive ride (just a day after being well beaten in handicap); balance of form is over shorter than this so others preferred on seasonal return.

runners.comment: Last year's Lingfield Derby Trial winner didn't progress;  tried in tongue-tie
runners.name: Puppet Master

prev_owners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

quotes.race: William Hill Lingfield Derby Trial Stakes (Listed Race) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Puppet Master is a nice horse and has always been held in high regard. He's done well because running downhill on this ground probably wasn't ideal for him. Stay True is a lovely horse also and will be going forward. I'd be happy with both of them. They're all very good horses and there's nobody like Aidan to train a horse, so I'm very lucky - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Money Back If 2nd To SP Fav Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Puppet Master is a lovely colt. He had a lovely run at Killarney, running green but finishing out well. Today he was very professional. He jumped, travelled, and I thought he quickened up well. He had a look when he got there but he went to the line well and he has a bit of class - Wayne Lordan, rider.

runners.spotlight: Ex Ballydoyle-trained; won Lingfield Derby Trial last year but well held in both Irish Derby and Irish St Leger; bought for 78,000gns and soundly beaten on yard debut in Grade 2 Leopardstown hurdle at Christmas; tried in a tongue-tie here and plenty on his plate in what looks a hot Listed race.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good staying colt who showed he was tough and hardy when winning the Lingfield Derby Trial. Ryan liked him that day and the plan was always to come here next. He seems well and seems to stay well. 13-06-25

runners.breeder: Robert Ryan Brendan Quinn & Joan Quinn
runners.comment: Fairly useful handicapper over shorter trips; big jump in trip here and out of her depth
runners.name: Lady Lilac

quotes.race: QuinnBet Spring Fillies Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Lady Lilac is improving and with another year under her belt she will be a nice filly - Joseph Murphy, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Fairly useful handicapper over shorter trips; big jump in trip here and out of her depth.

runners.comment: Better than ever last year; runs well fresh but ideally wants it softer
runners.name: Chally Chute

quotes.race: William Hill Extra Place Races Daily Handicap
quotes.quote: He's a pleasure to train, Chally Chute is improving steadily and we are having great fun with him. A couple of opportunities we had to pass because we felt the ground was too quick for him so I was keen to run him this week. The whole idea was to see how he stays and plan the rest of the season for him, the Irish Cesarewitch was in the back of my head for a long time. He won at Galway last autumn so the plan will be to go back, we might give him an entry in the 2m early in the week and then the 1m4f on the Friday - Michael Halford, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Hollywoodbets.ie Handicap
quotes.quote: Chally Chute is getting better with racing. He had a setback as a three-year-old and we just had to wait for him - he's improving all the time. He handled Dundalk well when he won up there, but I wasn't too worried about this ground with him being by Fast Company. It was a nice race and a nice track for him. Jamie was very cool on him. The plan wasn't to be that far back on him but he rode him for luck and it happened for them - Mick Halford, trainer.

runners.spotlight: In the form of his life last year, winning 1m4f Roscommon Listed on seasonal debut and better again upped to 2m at this venue, unlucky narrow defeat in Irish Cesarewitch and ready winner of Group 3 Loughbrown Stakes in November on heavy; ideally wants it softer and this looks a tough enough task on seasonal return but has to be respected.

runners.comment: Now 11lb higher than for C&D win in March, has maintained progress with a win over hurdles
runners.name: Fiver Friday

quotes.race: Boardsmill Stud Mares Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'd say there is a good chance of Fiver Friday mixing and matching the Flat and hurdles, we would be thinking of coming back here for the festival in July for the 50,000euros grand handicap hurdle. We might try and go back to the Flat in between. She jumps really well too, so we wouldn't rule out a chase either - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: 1xBet.ie Emerald Cup Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: It's a wonderful pot to win and Fiver Friday got a lovely run down the inside and won snugly. She'll have plenty of options over the summer and we'll see her over jumps again, possibly at Punchestown - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

quotes.race: TRM Speedxcell Multi Vitamin And Mineral Tonic Handicap
quotes.quote: Fiver Friday handled the course here from her maiden form  and for her to get her head in front in Ireland is brilliant. They went plenty hard early on and set it up for her - Paul Traynor, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Now 11lb higher than for C&D win in March, an emphatic success gained at the main expense of the Irish Lincoln winner Ribee; has maintained progress with a wide-margin win in a handicap hurdle at Bellewstown; strong contender.

runners.comment: Has shown enough in Listed races to suggest she could go close, talented apprentice booked
runners.name: Iowa City
runners.spotlight: Joined this yard for E210,000 after showing useful form in France; won a rated race over the extended mile at the Galway festival (soft); fair third of seven in a Listed race at Cork on final start last year; fourth at the same level at Naas on return; talented apprentice booked; may prove the pick of stable's three runners; leading chance.

runners.comment: Consistent last season, ended with C&D second, sharpened by a hurdles run at Punchestown
runners.name: In My Teens
runners.spotlight: Consistent last season; ended with C&D second behind today's rival Retracement on handicap debut; jumping let her down in juvenile hurdles; sharpened for return to the Flat by a handicap run at the Punchestown festival.

stable_tour.quote: She's run well in four starts on the Flat and will go juvenile hurdling. She's done a good bit of schooling and jumps well. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Has shown a liking for this track, suited by soft ground, would benefit from any easing
runners.name: Perry Mason

quotes.race: Feel The Rush With 1xBet.ie Handicap
quotes.quote: Perry Mason was probably a bit too far back in the Lincoln, we were a bit disappointed, but it probably crowned him for today. We'll probably step him up now into a better class. He might come back for the mile-and-a-quarter race here next Friday - Maurice Andrew Ahern, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Has shown a liking for this track, gained a second 1m success here in March; suited by soft ground; holding his form well on the evidence of Cork third; would benefit from any easing.

runners.comment: Found 1m inadequate here on seasonal debut. much better at Cork, could be in the mix
runners.name: Iron Fist

quotes.race: Knocklofty Handicap
quotes.quote: Iron Fist loved that ground, he gets through it well, but he absolutely hated the track, to be honest. He hung and never came down the hill. He'll be a nice horse next year - Shane Foley, rider, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Two soft ground wins last term; found 1m inadequate here on seasonal debut; much better when second at Cork, with Apercu back in fourth; could be in the mix.

stable_tour.quote: He ran an absolute cracker when second at Cork on Friday. He seemed to really enjoy stepping up to a mile and a quarter and it looks a really nice trip for him. There should be some good races in him through the summer. He showed on Friday that he doesn't mind that bit of nicer ground, which opens up plenty of options. 27-04-26

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khans Studs S C
runners.comment: Ex-Dermot Weld, won her first two starts last season, interesting recruit to this yard
runners.name: Deressa

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

quotes.race: @gowranpark1 On Twitter Fillies Race
quotes.quote: It took me all of last year to get to know how to ride Deressa, she enjoys a nice pace and to be coming at them. I would be happy enough with that trip but she'll get further in time. She enjoyed that ground, she's a filly that is improving away, a typical Aga Khan pedigree - Chris Hayes, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.spotlight: Ex-Dermot Weld, won her first two starts last season, both at Gowran over a slightly shorter trip than this; highly tried later in the season; interesting recruit to this yard.

runners.comment: Should be suited by this return to a longer trip after two seconds over 1m, good claimer
runners.name: Fixation
runners.spotlight: Won over the extended version of this trip at Dundalk last November on stable debut; should be suited by this return to a longer trip after two seconds over 1m; good claimer aboard.

runners.comment: Winner of three of her six races for Ralph Beckett, obvious chance with yard in super form
runners.name: Perfect Your Craft

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Perfect Your Craft toughed it out in the ground and the dream would be black type, although she could also go to the December sales - Anthony Ramsden, owners' representative.

runners.spotlight: Winner of three of her six races for Ralph Beckett; clear chance on best form, though issue complicated by the fact that she is one of three runners for a stable in superb form.

stable_tour.quote: She's done well over the winter and will probably go for a trial. The ground will be important as she wants a bit of juice. Her win on her debut at Salisbury came on heavy and she learned plenty that day. She'll stay very well. 28-04-25

runners.comment: C&D winner on penultimate start last season, final outing over 1m4f was too bad to be true
runners.name: Retracement

quotes.race: DNG Handicap
quotes.quote: Retracement is a horse with a lot of ability, but he's a little bit tricky. He's starting to settle into the place now. I thought coming today he was in good shape and he was after growing up. He's in the mile and a half handicap [at Leopardstown] on Sunday and we'll see how he is - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Fifth behind Apercu in this event 12 months ago; C&D winner on penultimate start last season, beating subsequent improver Fiver Friday; final outing over 1m4f was too bad to be true.

runners.comment: Back from a spell in Bahrain, five-time winner, generally reliable performer at 1m2f/1m4f
runners.name: Cloud Seeker

quotes.race: Leopardstown Golf And Driving Range Handicap
quotes.quote: Cloud Seeker won four last year and had a blow in Tipperary, he just needed the run. We'll give him an entry at Royal Ascot or he could be one for something like the Ragusa at the Curragh. He jumps hurdles well so he has that option as well in the future - Andrew Slattery, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Five-time winner, beaten a short head by Apercu in this race last season; back from a spell in Bahrain; generally reliable performer at 1m2f/1m4f.

runners.comment: Not far behind Iron Fist at Cork, out of her comfort zone in a Listed race last time
runners.name: Apercu

quotes.race: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Apercu is a tough mare, she's improving and Billy knows her well. He gave her a great ride. She seems to go everywhere he wants her. She got it handy up front and he said himself that he probably got there a bit earlier than he thought. She was enjoying herself and was going sweetly. She battles and when the horse came back at her she just kept finding. She was tough out, she's a great filly to watch because she wears her heart on his sleeve. Barry Irwin, CEO of Team Valor, has been a great supporter of mine over the years. We have a few together as well at the moment. It's an exciting venture. This filly has done nothing but improve. She's been very easy to train and has given everybody a lot of fun - Andy Oliver, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Four turf wins, including this race last year, beating Cloud Seeker by a short head; not far behind Iron Fist on seasonal debut at Cork; out of her comfort zone in a Listed race at Gowran last time; respected now on the same mark as 12 months ago.

stable_tour.quote: She will probably go for the Northfields Handicap. She won nicely at Naas and she stepped up to a mile and half at the Curragh and finished sixth, which I was a bit disappointed with as I thought she had a great chance. I'm not quite sure she got the trip, so we're bringing her back in distance. She'll be near the bottom of the handicap but she has a fair chance of getting in. 11-09-24

runners.comment: Group 2 course winner at 2m, fine second in last year's Cesarewitch, inadequate trip here
runners.name: Dawn Rising

prev_owners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

quotes.race: Comer Group International Loughbrown Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Dawn Rising came on the bridle with me from about halfway and he was loving it. I was able to mooch away down the centre in the straight. It took him a while to get to Gavin but he was finding plenty for me and I knew I was always going to get there - Dylan Browne McMonagle, rider

quotes.race: Queen Alexandra Stakes (Conditions Race)
quotes.quote: Joseph had Dawn Rising beautifully prepared for today. He has been jumping and won a graded race over jumps during the winter, and today he just got himself into a nice spot and I just gradually built along. I hadn't really asked him for everything and he was always finding plenty. Joseph's horses can do that - Ryan Moore, rider, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: John J. Galvin Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Dawn Rising learned a bit from Galway and came on plenty for the run. It was a good performance. He bumped into a good horse in Galway but came forward plenty. He's taken to hurdling well. We'll go down the novice route I'd imagine and see how we go - Frank Berry, racing manager to owner JP McManus.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: He's a lovely, big, staying horse who had a very good run at the Curragh the last day. He was very idle in front and I know we won by 12 lengths, but you never know when there's something coming from behind you and the way he was rolling around, I just wanted to keep the revs up. He won with plenty in hand at the end. He looked at the stalls in the straight, they were pulled in and he copped them and ran out in the middle - Wayne Lordan, rider of Dawn Rising

runners.spotlight: No wins last season but strong form in defeat in big staying handicaps; fourth in the amateur handicap at Galway, fifth in the Irish Cesarewitch and signed off with a fine second in the Cesarewitch; runs over an inadequate trip here on second start of the season.

stable_tour.quote: He needs to find his form again but I think it usually takes him a few runs, so hopefully he might bounce back at Ascot.  13-06-25
He had a nice run at Leopardstown in the Saval Beg and wasn't beaten far, so hopefully he'll run a nice race in the Queen Alexandra Stakes. 16-06-23

runners.comment: Fair form at 7f/1m in Britain, appeared not to stay this trip at Newcastle in January
runners.name: Flame Of Forest
runners.spotlight: Fair form at 7f/1m in Britain; appeared not to stay this trip at Newcastle in January; tough task against that background.

runners.comment: Ended last season with a 1m1f maiden win, may step up from his 1m run here in March
runners.name: Playin Cool
runners.spotlight: Ended last season with a 1m1f maiden win on heavy ground at Leopardstown; may step up from his 1m run here in March; needs to reverse form with Perry Mason; finished in front of Calm The Jets and Iron Fist.

runners.comment: Third place in 2024 Dante is becoming a distant memory, plenty to prove at this stage
runners.name: War Rooms

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dante Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: That was what I expected at Sandown. We were disappointed there but nothing went to plan there and Jim was quick to say put a line through that. I was more favouring going to Newbury on Saturday but fair play to the owners, they were rewarded. The winner looks really smart but we were beaten not far by a Group 1 winner last year. War Rooms won't go to Epsom and we'll keep him for Royal Ascot for the Hampton Court. He's still learning and Jim said we might do more harm than good for the future if we were to go to Epsom - Owen Burrows, trainer.

quotes.race: Simon Piggott Memorial Race EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: War Rooms gave me a good feel. They went a strong pace on the ground and he stayed well. He'll have learnt plenty and has got a good mind on him. He's rangy and will be a lovely horse for next year. Over a mile and a quarter he'll be quite smart - Jim Crowley, jockey, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Third in the 2024 Dante and generally kept good company on the Flat in Britain; started brightly in Ireland last spring; has become disappointing; plenty to prove at this stage.

runners.comment: 1m AW winner, fair run over 1m here on turf debut, needs to settle better than at Cork
runners.name: Calm The Jets
runners.spotlight: Landed a 1m maiden at Dundalk on debut early last year; did not appear last turf season; fair run over 1m here on turf debut; needs to settle better than at Cork a month ago.

runners.comment: No hint so far of the form that brought him eight wins in France, headgear tried now
runners.name: Dar Toungi
runners.spotlight: No hint so far of the form that brought him eight wins in France, including a Listed race over this trip two seasons ago; has beaten only one opponent in each of his two Irish starts; headgear tried now.

runners.comment: Towards the rear in three outings this season, 6lb out of the handicap, can be ruled out
runners.name: Dutch Gold
runners.owner: Albert Dravins & Exors of the Late Eamonn Scanlon

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden
quotes.quote: Dylan Browne McMonagle rode DUTCH GOLD last time over a mile and we were thinking about going back to 7f but he said he needs a trip. I was worried about the ground but he seemed to like the ground and the trip. He had some very good runs as a two-year-old and we were getting a little bit frustrated so that was nice to get. I had a notion we were going to geld him after today's race but we might leave him now as he settled well - Noel Meade, trainer.

runners.spotlight: A long time since he showed his best form; the most recent of his two wins was in 2023; towards the rear in three outings this season; 6lb out of the handicap, can be ruled out.

runners.comment: Struck form last autumn, progress not maintained in two subsequent outings, cheekpieces on
runners.name: Railwayview Lady

quotes.race: Lynn Lodge Stud Maiden
quotes.quote: Railwayview Lady's first run was educational and on her second run she just got held up and into all sorts of trouble at Leopardstown at the bend. We knew coming here she was still a bit green, she has her own way of doing things. We knew the ability was there and we were hoping that this track would suit her - Andrew Oliver, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Sprang 125-1 shock in a 1m2f Navan maiden last September, proved that was no fluke later in the month when going down narrowly on handicap debut over 1m5f at Down Royal; progress not maintained in two subsequent outings; cheekpieces on now.

runners.comment: Course 1m4f winner during a solid 2025 campaign, below his best in two outings this term
runners.name: Pillar Of Hope

quotes.race: Fitzpatrick's Mercedes-Benz Apprentice Derby Handicap
quotes.quote: I bought Pillar Of Hope two years ago at Tattersalls [18,000gns]. I ran him at Leopardstown recently when I thought the 1m1f trip was too short for him, he was finishing out the race well. The longer trip worked, young Patrick [McGettigan] from Donegal used to ride out for me in Letterkenny so a real Donegal experience so it is - Patrick Sweeney, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

runners.spotlight: Five turf wins include a 1m4f course success during a solid 2025 campaign; below his best in two outings this term; mid-field behind today's Perry Mason on the first occasion.

runners.comment: French import who stays considerably further than this, no luck in running on Irish debut
runners.name: Yulia
runners.spotlight: Two wins in France (on soft and AW); has won over 1m7f, and had never raced at under 1m4f until recent Irish debut at Sligo; unplaced favourite after starting slowly and meeting trouble in running; trip is a concern, but unwise to discount.

runners.comment: Won Ascot Group 1 at 200-1, little mileage on the clock, fascinating prospect this term
runners.name: Powerful Glory

quotes.race: Qipco British Champions Sprint Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: I always felt Powerful Glory was going to get there if that makes sense. It's fantastic. It was the plan all year, genuinely. We had a blip halfway through and we had to stop with him, and we were running out of races. Did I think he would come here and win? I thought he would need to be at his very best because he's still an immature horse because he's only had four runs. It was a Spencer special. I thought Jamie would suit him well, just get him to switch [off,] relax and leave him alone - Richard Fahey, trainer,I'm lost for words. Powerful Glory is a good horse and we obviously travelled nicely. I thought I was going to be placed and then all of a sudden, I thought 'I've got a chance'' He jinked a little bit left and I've put my whip away and we've held on. I'm just shocked really - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

quotes.race: Dubai Duty Free Mill Reef Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I thought I was in a bit of trouble. It's not easy out there but ability can get them through most ground, and I think he's got plenty of it. Everything Powerful Glory has shown has been speed but he's big and scopey as well and, if learns to relax and race right, there's no reason why he can't get further. At home there's nothing really we have to gallop with him, so I think he's pretty smart - Oisin Orr, rider.

quotes.race: Cure Leukaemia EBF "Newcomers" Maiden Stakes (For horses which have never run) (GBB/IRE Incentive)
quotes.quote: We do like Powerful Glory. He was my favourite breeze-up horse this year and I'm just delighted Sheikh Rashid bought him. You're a bit nervous when you've got a nice one and I thought they weren't quick enough to lead him. That was grand. He's a big, scopey lad. We gave him a little flick to see if we thought Ascot would be for him but he's still on the leg, he's still weak. Fair dos to Sheikh Rashid, he said do whatever you want with him and I said I'd give him a bit of time. He's in the Mill Reef Stakes and that's his target. He might go for the 5f race at Ayr as well, he's a very fast horse - Richard Fahey, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Looked smart when landing the Group 2 Mill Reef Stakes at Newbury (6f, heavy) on final juvenile start; beat only one rival in his first two races last term; produced massive shock (200-1) when beating the favourite Lazaat in 6f Group 1 at Ascot last October (good); wind-surgery evidently the key to that success; little mileage on the clock, fascinating prospect for this season.

runners.comment: Late-maturing type won the Group 1 Sprint Cup at Haydock in 2024, not at best in 2025
runners.name: Montassib

quotes.race: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: I thought Unequal Love might run well but I wasn't expecting Montassib to enjoy that ground and I thought they were both drawn away from the real action. We relied on Bucanero Fuerte going forward, which he did, and Unequal Love was always travelling well, whereas Cieren [Fallon] had to get after Montassib. On softer ground they come back to him and that would suit him better, but he's the most genuine horse at home and Cieren always thinks there's more to come. The Champions Sprint was always the race I was looking forward to. You would think the race would suit him, but he'll now be one of the favourites and things are different when you're expected to win - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Jenningsbet Nun Street Newcastle Open Now Chipchase Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: I'm not sure where we'll go now, but Montassib won't go to Goodwood for the Stewards' Cup. He'd have to carry a Group-race penalty now. I think we'll stick to stakes races and go wherever we can get a bit of dig in the ground - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I do believe I should have won the Ayr Gold Cup on Montassib, he reversed the form at York and he's improving all the time. He's got so much quicker - Cieren Fallon, rider.

quotes.race: Coral Sprint Trophy Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: "It's only taken us three years to find Montassib's right trip, but we got there in the end. He had a bit more luck than he did at Ayr. He really is a lovely horse and one of those nice ones to have around. He was a good two-year-old then had a problem with his heart, and had the whole three-year-old campaign off. He's still got a few miles on the clock and lots of racing left in him. There isn't much left for him unless something comes up at Doncaster, but that might be it for the year. He's definitely stepped up his last two runs" - Maureen Haggas, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Aspall Blush Cyder Handicap
quotes.quote: Montassib found the ground quick enough but I wanted to make the most of him by setting him alight two and a half furlongs out. It's nice that he could get his head back in front - Cieren Fallon, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Pick Your Places Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought Montassib was certain not to cope with conditions and told everyone he'd dislike the ground, but he coped with them. Most Exceed And Excels don't like that ground, but he won nicely and I don't know what we'll do, but the Buckingham Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot would seem an obvious target - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: It was probably as you'd have hoped from Montassib. Four-runner races can get a bit muddly but he travelled into the race and duly put his head in front. He's had a good experience, the ground is plenty quick enough and he handled that fine. It's good to have him back on the racecourse. He looks like he belongs in a Newbury or Ascot paddock and hopefully he'll be ending up at those racetracks in the near future - Tom Marquand, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Late-maturing type won the Group 1 Sprint Cup at Haydock (good) in 2024; did not appear last year until September and failed to recapture his best form in three runs, only fifth behind Spycatcher when favourite at Doncaster on last of them; reversed that form (and had James's Delight behind) when fourth in a 6f Listed race at the same venue eight weeks ago.

runners.comment: Group 1-winning juvenile over C&D, Group 1-placed here last season, fair chance if on song
runners.name: Bucanero Fuerte
runners.owner: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar

prev_owners.owner: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar

quotes.race: FBD Hotels And Resorts Phoenix Sprint Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: A lot of credit to Adrian (Murray) and Robson (Aguiar) for the training performance there and David gave Bucanero Fuerte an unbelievable ride, just the way he likes to be ridden. I'm glad to see him back happy on the track. We're definitely not taking him out of Ireland now for a while - Kia Joorabchian, owner.

quotes.race: Sole Power Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: It was great for us to see Bucanero Fuerte coming back but I suppose from a breeding point of view it was disappointing. We were on a fact finding mission today to see whether he was going to train on and he was brilliant. He's only back six or eight weeks with us and you'd never think he was away at stud. He's so cool and calm, we even said to David [Egan, jockey] going out to wake him up a little bit because he's so relaxed. He finished out the race well, he galloped right to the line. He put plenty of daylight between them. There is a race in Cork in three weeks time and he'll be entered for the Nunthorpe. He's not in Ascot. We'll see after a couple of days how he comes out of the race and then make a plan from there - Adrian Murray, trainer.

quotes.race: Goffs Lacken Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Bucanero Fuerte is unbelievable and had to tough it out today. We had to come here because we'd as much done at home as we could and that run is going to bring him on plenty. He had a lot left in the tank. He did a spectacular piece of work at the Curragh last Sunday. It's on now to Ascot and we'll probably go for the Commonwealth Cup. We're really looking forward to it - Adrian Murray, trainer.

quotes.race: Keeneland Phoenix Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: I think Bucanero Fuerte is a serious horse. That's three runs and three wins here, he's the horse of a lifetime. I'd say it'll be the National Stakes for him now and I don't think he'll have any problem stepping up to 7f. He would prefer an ease in the ground but he has won on good ground. The ground today would be a bit easier than the last day. He was very impressive in his maiden here on heavy ground but it's not an issue for him as he's won on quick ground as well - Adrian Murray, trainer.

quotes.race: GAIN Railway Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I knew Bucanero Fuerte would battle because he needs every yard of 6f. He's a tough horse, really tough. He's a beautiful-looking horse too and, you know what, he's going to improve again. When he won his maiden in April he was only a shell of a horse. He is twice the horse now than he was then. Please God, we will be back here again for the Phoenix Stakes - Adrian Murray, trainer

runners.spotlight: Group 1-winning juvenile over C&D; returned from aborted stud career last year and won a 5f Listed race at Naas (good) and a C&D Group 3 (6f, good); fine third in the Group 1 Flying Five before failing to run to expectations at the Breeders' Cup; well below best on soft on seasonal debut at Cork; better over 5f at Naas, but needs more to make an impact here.

runners.comment: Useful form at 7m/1m last season, hard to be sure he has the speed to match some of these
runners.name: Comanche Brave

prev_owners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & Mrs A M OBrien

quotes.race: Jersey Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Comanche Brave ran okay, I don't think he had any excuses, the first two pulled well clear. This is a tough place, any time you hit the board its not a bad result - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Useful form at 7m/1m last season, fifth in the Irish 2,000 Guineas, third in the Jersey Stakes, odds-on for 7f Naas win; kept on for third in 7f Group 2 in Saudi Arabia in February; ran as well as could have been expected when fifth of eight behind the spectacular Ka Ying Rising at Sha Tin last month; trip possibly a little sharp for him.

runners.comment: Failed to uphold previous form with Montassib at Doncaster on seasonal debut, likes soft
runners.name: Spycatcher

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Wentworth Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: That was brilliant. I just managed to watch it here in Germany and I was delighted. He's a Group 1 horse on that ground, Spycatcher absolutely ploughs through it. If we managed to get him into a Group 1 and it comes up that ground he'd run a big one somewhere next season. We were going to put him away after his last run but with the ground the way it is, and him bouncing out of that race so well, we said we'd roll the dice - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Cammidge Trophy Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: The jockeys came in after the first two races and said it's safe, dead ground so we let Spycatcher take his chance. But I said to James he's a scrabbly old mover, he's had plenty of little issues in his career, ride him to finish and if it's happening great but don't knock him around if it's not. He gave him a peach of a ride. It was a great performance - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Barriere Prix de Meautry (Group 3) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with Spycatcher. He looked like his old self today and was given a great ride by Clifford [Lee]. He loves that soft ground, that's key to him, he looked in great shape and travelled over well. We'll aim for Champions Day again but he'll have entries in a few races and if the ground comes up heavy between then and now, he'll probably turn up - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Arc Prix Maurice de Gheest (Group 1) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Spycatcher was on the box, heading for retirement last year. He had an issue but Duncan Moir, the vet, said he'd seen the x-ray and he thought we could put this horse back together again if we did everything right. Karl and Duncan and everyone have got him to win a Group 3 and come within a whisker of winning a Group 1. It's a remarkable training performance and all credit to everyone involved with him. It was a terrific run. He was travelling so well and Maxime Guyon had to go, there was no choice. The agony is that the other horse has come to him, passed him and then he's come back and got him just past the post. He's a fabulous horse and, ground allowing, we'll hopefully look at the Haydock Sprint Cup. He must have this easy ground - Harry Herbert, owner's Chairman and Managing Director.

quotes.race: Prix de Ris-Orangis (Group 3) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Spycatcher ran a brilliant race at Newcastle and today he's loved this ground. I liked the way he travelled into it and quickened away. It does take a lot of doing. Some horses you can't really do that with but he's a tough horse to turn around and win - Clifford Lee, jockey.

quotes.race: 1895 Duke Of York Clipper Logistics Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted, Spycatcher has run a great race. He's suffered with his feet a little bit and to come and do it that grade gives us a lot of hope for the future. He's in a Group 2 at the Curragh a week on Sunday, but I'd imagine that will come too quick. We're not in at Ascot and ground with a bit of juice in it will be key to him with his feet - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Novice Stakes (Div I)
quotes.quote: Spycatcher showed last year he had a lot of ability. He was a lot more relaxed today and we might think about the Greenham, otherwise he'd be running in handicaps with big weights - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won a 6f Listed at Doncaster early last season (good to soft); ended 2025 in top form with convincing wins in Group 3 at Chantilly (very soft) and a Listed race at Doncaster (Montassib fifth); failed to uphold form with Montassib at the same venue on seasonal debut.

stable_tour.quote: He's a great old horse who loves running fresh and he did it nicely in the Cammidge Trophy on his return. I'm not sure where we'll go next because the higher the grade the softer he needs the ground. Realistically he's a Group 3 horse but on heavy ground who knows what he might achieve. 11-04-25

He's a horse I have always liked and after suffering a mid-summer injury we had him gelded and I brought him back at Thirsk last month, expecting him to come on for the run, so it was a pleasant surprise to see him romp home from the useful Mount Athos. We had planned to turn him around quickly at Haydock on Saturday but the ground was a bit quick for him. He will not run on any ground with the word ‘firm' in the going description. He is a nice horse who has more good races in him now he has matured. Prior to his last run he had never seen the 7f out, as he was too keen, but the long break and the cut have seen him come back a more mature horse and that trip looks more to his liking now. 07-05-23

runners.comment: Won this event on good ground last 12 months ago, this is a deeper race than last year's
runners.name: Jamess Delight

quotes.race: Barriere Prix de Meautry (Group 3) (3yo+) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: James's Delight enjoys the soft ground and we have an entry in the Champions Day Sprint. We're forecast some hotter temperatures so we'll play our cards accordingly - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: Churchill Tyres Supporting Macmillan Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: That was wonderful, I'm so pleased. It was a very confident ride from Ryan, as always. The way that he changed gear there today fills me full of excitement. James's Delight does appreciate the ground, although he won on good ground on Guineas day at Newmarket he prefers this end of the scale.  We'll see how he comes back before we think of the Wokingham but winning today means he'll have a penalty and that will be on top of a mark of 102 so we'll see. But he's clearly a three-year-old going places - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Bet In-Running Handicap
quotes.quote: James's Delight did that well. Last time over seven furlongs was a bit of a non event and he enjoyed this trip of six furlongs a lot better - Richard Kingscote, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Won this event on good ground last year, battling well to beat another British challenger, with Big Gossey a little unlucky in a close third; struggled in two Group 1s in the autumn, including the Ascot event won by Powerful Glory; out of the money, along with the shorter-priced Spycatcher, on seasonal debut at Doncaster in March; this is a deeper race than last year's.

stable_tour.quote: We were thrilled with his Group 2 success in the Greenlands Stakes at the Curragh. I'm delighted how he's been able to move through the ranks and he's come back really fresh and well. If we had any rain in the meantime it would be in his favour. 10-06-25

He put up a pleasing performance to win at Newbury last month on his debut in the colours of Paul and Clare Rooney, who we've had some great days with in the past. James's Delight is out of a Pivotal mare and I thought that may count on his debut where the ground was on the soft side. He showed a great attitude and I was impressed with his positive response in the closing stages. He has qualified for the Goffs sales race at Naas in Ireland later on and we will obviously seriously consider that option. He is a horse to look forward to. 02-08-23

runners.comment: Durable course specialist, twice placed in this race, asking a lot now in a strong edition
runners.name: Big Gossey

quotes.race: 1xBet.ie Supports Irish Racing Gladness Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't really expecting that. Coming here last year I thought Big Gossey had a good chance. Today I thought there were a few in there that probably had a bit more class than him, but you can't beat honesty. The longer I hang around this game, attitude is more important than an awful lot of things. If you look at his programme for the last seven or eight years, it's going to be pretty much the same. He couldn't be any easier to deal with at this stage, he's an old pro - Charles O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Lester Piggott Gladness Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I thought seven furlongs might find Big Gossey out, if it was six furlongs I think he would have won easy. Billy said he was just hanging on desperately. An eight-year-old on that ground against three-year-olds, it doesn't matter how much weight they are giving away, it's very hard for young horses to take on a battle-hardened horse like him. Gary O'Brien, who leads him up, does 90 per cent of the work with him and he just occasionally gives him a pipe opener and lunges him and doesn't have to do much with him. When he arrived in the door, I never thought he'd be doing this! A Gutaifan that couldn't be sold without much of a pedigree. Apparently he might come back here! Today was his 40th start at the track - Charles O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Cavalor Equine Nutrition Race
quotes.quote: Big Gossey got in well at the conditions and it's a perfect sort of race for him. He is in terrific form and we might find a race for him at Dundalk before next year - Charles O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: David Power Memorial Premier Handicap
quotes.quote: Big Gossey has been great for my career. I was delighted to see the rain as he thrives with a bit of an ease. He just loves it here. I would have loved something to bring me a bit further but I wanted to get rolling on him and not let something get first run - Robert Whearty, rider.

quotes.race: Sheehy Motors Volkswagen Race
quotes.quote: Big Gossey has been a great horse to me this season, he's a legend. He hit the line well when he won the Bold Lad, and over that ground and trip, I didn't think the seven would be a problem - Robert Whearty, rider

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF "Bold Lad" Sprint Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Big Gossey was a bit unlucky the last day when he missed the break. I travelled into it lovely and got a lovely run up the rail. He had a bit of a look when he got there but he stayed going - Robert Whearty, rider.

quotes.race: AK Bets "Higher Limits, Better Prices" Handicap
quotes.quote: Big Gossey is getting better as the year goes on and he loves it up the Curragh. I'm delighted that he's after getting his head in front today. I always thought six was his ideal trip but a fast run five like that suits him down to the ground - Danny Sheehy, rider.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF "Bold Lad" Sprint Handicap (Premier Handicap)
quotes.quote: Big Gossey travelled throughout and picked up well. I was probably there a bit early but he saw it out. He has plenty of speed and did everything right - Michael Hussey, jockey.

quotes.race: Join Us On Instagram @dundalk_stadium Handicap
quotes.quote: Big Gossey came on from the last run. They went a good strong gallop which suited him and he settled lovely. When I gave him a squeeze he picked up really well. He toughed it out to the line so I'm very happy with him - Danny Sheehy, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Big Gossey is a horse that's improving every week and there's more improvement in him again. He's an out-and-out sprinter - Mick Hussey, rider

runners.spotlight: Splendid veteran showed he retained enthusiasm when winning the 7f Gladness Stakes in March, his ninth Curragh win on his 50th visit; found 5f too sharp at Naas last time; runs in this event for the fourth consecutive year, second at 25-1 in 2023, ninth in 2024, third behind James Delight at 33-1 last season; asking a lot now in a strong edition.

runners.comment: All three wins have come at 1m, back after a spell in the Emirates, trip looks inadequate
runners.name: Chicago Critic

quotes.race: Porsche In Support Of Breast Cancer Ireland Amethyst Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Chicago Critic has been up and down in trip, from six furlongs to a mile. I think a mile on fast ground is his ideal trip. They didn't go quick and I had a nice turn of foot towards the end so it's nice to get his head in front again. His best form is over a mile and he feels good at that trip - Ben Coen, jockey.

quotes.race: Jersey Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We're absolutely delighted - that was fantastic. We came over because we thought we had a nice horse on our hands, but when you look at the strength of the race, it was a very, very good race and Chicago Critic ran his heart out. Ben gave him a great ride. We got excited up there for a couple of seconds - we thought he was coming, but he just couldn't get there. No fault of the horse, he ran brilliantly. Today was the plan, and now we know we have a horse of this level, we will think about what's next. He'll stay at seven or a mile - I think he'll get a mile no problem - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

quotes.race: Royal Ascot Trials At Naas Handicap
quotes.quote: Chicago Critic has been gelded since his last run so maybe that and the good ground both helped. I'm delighted with that and he could be a horse to go to Ascot for the Britannia Handicap - Johnny Murtagh, trainer

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Ben (Coen, jockey) said Chicago Critic is very professional, very genuine and should get a mile and a quarter next year - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

runners.spotlight: All three wins have come at 1m; back after a spell in the Emirates; not far off best when touched off by Elnajmm in the 7f Group 2 Al Fahidi Fort in January; beaten 3l in fourth behind the same horse in a Group 3 last time; blinkered first time now; not appealing at this trip.

runners.comment: Found wanting in two stakes races last year, same over 7f in a Group 3 on seasonal debut
runners.name: Fregada

quotes.race: Bermingham Cameras EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Fregada got a touch of sore shins six or seven weeks ago and we backed off her. She did that very well, was impressive. She gallops all over anything we have at home. When she gets a bit of racing she will be really good - Johnny Feane, trainer.

runners.spotlight: C&D maiden winner at two; found wanting in two stakes races last year; same over 7f in a Group 3 at Leopardstown on seasonal debut.

runners.comment: Norfolk Stakes winner in 2023, five AW wins, out of his depth here judged on recent form
runners.name: Valiant Force
runners.owner: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar

prev_owners.owner: Amo Racing/Mrs R OCallaghan/G De Aguiar
Amo Racing/Mrs R OCallaghan/G De Aguiar

quotes.race: William Hill Proper Betting Race
quotes.quote: The drop in class has probably done Valiant Force's confidence the world of good more than anything. I kind of kidded him along rather than being aggressive because he hasn't really been finishing his races. He disappointed on dirt in the States early this year but hopefully he's getting back on track now - David Egan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Norfolk Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: To be fair to the lads, they were confident Valiant Force would run a big race. If you took away his last run at the Curragh, when he was on his own, he ran a stormer first time up in a Listed race, that's how much they thought of him. He's bred well, he's bred to be a sprinter, and he's something else to look at. He jumped well, did everything right. When I took the lead inside the two I was always in a rhythm and I probably could have won further if someone had come at me with a run. But he got the job done - Rossa Ryan, jockey, speaking to ITV.

runners.spotlight: Sole win on turf in the 2023 Norfolk Stakes; has won five conditions races at Dundalk since, the most recent over 5f in February; has struggled since then, most recently last Sunday at Naas; out of his depth here.

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.name: Marvelman

quotes.race: Betfred Park Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Marvelman is a very smart horse with lots to look forward to. He'll probably go to the Challenge Stakes with a penalty. There is the Foret but we've got all of next year as well. He should have a good four-year-old campaign - Andrew Balding, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Non-runner

runners.comment: Crowned last season with Breeders' Cup win, can uphold Newmarket form with Distant Storm
runners.name: Gstaad
runners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

prev_owners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

quotes.race: Betfred 2000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: I am pleased with Gstaad and that was a great run. Ryan [Moore] was very happy today and he has done everything right. It was his first run of the year, and you can see he's a big horse. It was great to get him started. I think there were two lengths between us and the winner (it was actually two and three-quarter lengths) and eight lengths back to the third. We couldn't be happier really. He's a big, powerful horse and that type of horse can only progress. We used today as a start off and tried to do our best to win on his first start as a three-year-old. We are still delighted with how he has run. We always thought that he could go further, although I don't know where we would go from here. The Irish Guineas would be the logical step, and I imagine that's what the lads would be thinking about - Aidan O'Brien.

quotes.race: Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf (Grade 1) (2yo Colts & Geldings) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I didn't do anything really, I think Gstaad is just good. He's been a little bit unlucky in Europe on his last few starts, we should've won one of them. He jumped a bit slow today, but he was travelling very well in the first part of the race. When I saw there was a gap in the back straight to try to go forward and let him sit behind the pace, I made the move and I was cruising the whole way. I knew when I came out of the turn that I'd win. It's very rare to see amazing horses winning a Breeders' Cup hands and heels like that - Christophe Soumillon, jockey.

quotes.race: Darley Dewhurst Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: Next year Gstaad will be older and stronger, but he ran a good race and you have to be very happy with him. I think the race worked out lovely. He would be one for an English or Irish 2,000 Guineas - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix Morny (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Gstaad ran a great race, we're delighted. It's a long time since he ran but we're over the moon. We had it in our head he could go back to the National Stakes, so that's where he could go next. He'd have no problem with seven furlongs - Aidan O'Brien, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Coventry Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Gstaad looks a very good horse, doesn't he? We've always loved him. He had only had the one run. He has always worked like a good horse. He's big, he's scopey, he has a good stride and is very genuine; he goes with his head down and he has loads of speed. He looks like he will get further than six [furlongs] - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.Gstaad was very impressive. I thought he travelled beautifully, and we got to the front a long way from home. He's a tall horse and is obviously improving with each run and that was a very good performance - Ryan Moore, jockey.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: He was a little bit babyish going down but Gstaad was a pro in the race. When Wayne (Lordan) kicked he got a bit disorganised but from the furlong pole I always thought I was going to get there. I'll think he'll sharpen up for it, he'll get another furlong - Chris Hayes, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.spotlight: Beat stablemate True Love on debut before landing the Coventry Stakes; second in three consecutive Group 1 races, including the National Stakes and the Dewhurst; ended the campaign by overcoming a wide trip in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf at Del Mar (1m, firm); has evidently trained on and can go one better than in the 2,000 Guineas by upholding form with Distant Storm.

stable_tour.quote: He was always a hardy horse and won the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf on his final start of the season. When he finished second in the Dewhurst, Christophe made the decision to take him back after he jumped, and was caught in the middle of two. When he came back, they all came back and there ended up being no pace. We felt there was more to come from him after that and he went and won in America, coasting around and not doing a lot when he got there. I wouldn't be afraid to let him flow because he isn't a keen horse but has a long stride and a big action. He's being trained for a Guineas. Ryan rode him at the Curragh on Sunday and he had it in his head he could be one for Newmarket. But we'll see how Puerto Rico and Albert Einstein are over the next few weeks. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Not far off Gstaad in the Dewhurst, 8l behind him in the 2,000 Guineas, likely second-best
runners.name: Distant Storm

quotes.race: Betfred 2000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: Distant Storm ran a good race and Will [Buick] feels that he will come forward a bit for that as well. We were a bit further behind the second Gstaad than we were in the Dewhurst, but Will was pleased and felt that he got a lovely run. Full credit to the winner - he routed them and they were going good honest fractions I felt. There is room for improvement there. The ground has been tight over the past couple of days but everyone had to go on it and I think it was a usual first run of the season, not that you would ideally come into a Guineas needing a run, which he will naturally come forward from - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Darley Dewhurst Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: After Distant Storm was beaten in the Acomb by today's winner, we thought we'd give him one more run and put him away, and then when he won the Group 3 here last time as he did we were drawn into the Dewhurst. William [Buick] said he rode like a horse who will be better with some time over winter to develop. He felt that the immaturity was coming out in him today, but he's lost nothing in defeat as we see him as a Guineas horse next year. Whether he runs in the Craven Stakes or has a racecourse gallop before that, we'll have to see - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Stakes (Registered As The Somerville Tattersall Stakes) (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: It's not the first time I've got one beat in the Acomb but it was my mistake. William was keen to get a pitch on Distant Storm early on and, to do that, he asked him from the gate and the only other time I've seen him be keen was when he was on the lead at home. We were adamant today to drop him in and let the race develop in front of him and in doing so we've seen his acceleration. I think we've seen a nice horse in the making. William was impressed and, with the way this season is stacking up with two-year-olds, my initial impression is to look at the Dewhurst. If it were sound ground conditions I'd be happy to take them on. He's definitely up there - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive)
quotes.quote: Distant Storm is one of the nicest breeze-up horses I've seen with an eye to the future, we always felt this is a horse for next year and we'll give him a bit of time. He's still very unfurnished. He's a nice-looking horse, but still needs to strengthen before you go up a level ? if you pitch them in too soon, you'll go quickly backwards. There will be races in the autumn we can dip our toe in and allow him to progress. If he ticks the next box we can look at the Group 1 target we have pencilled in. He could be an Acomb horse - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

runners.spotlight: E1,900,000 breeze-up purchase last spring; very smart juvenile form, aside from when pulling too hard in the Acomb; impressed in winning a 1m Group 3 event at Newmarket in September before a fine third placing (1 1/2l behind Gstaad) in the Dewhurst; now has an 8l deficit to overturn in another clash with Gstaad following his distant 2,000 Guineas third; first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Ran with credit the 2,000 Guineas despite pulling too hard, place chance if settling well
runners.name: Thesecretadversary
runners.owner: Cayton Park Stud & Mrs John Magnier

quotes.race: Ballylinch Stud Red Rocks Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: The only bit of a setback we had with Thesecretadversary was at Ayr last year. He was a bit unlucky in Canada last time. He's in everything so we'll see where we go. He stays well. He's been working well. He ran a good race at Ascot last year and won well at Tipperary, where he beat the horse who was second in the Middle Park [Brussels], so it was a fair bit of form. He's in every Guineas bar the Italian, and I entered him in a $1 million race in the US the same day as the English Guineas. We'll talk to the owners - Fozzy Stack, trainer.

quotes.race: Chesham Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Thesecretadversary ran a great race. It's annoying we didn't get there, but he ran a great race. He's been very straightforward, he's always looked a bit above average from the minute we started doing a bit with him. I know he's quite colourful, but he's actually a very good model. Seamie was delighted with him, he said he has the pace of a good horse, he feels he will mature in time - Fozzy Stack, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Chesham Stakes runner-up and Listed winner at Tipperary before a respectable effort in a 1m Canadian Grade 1 on final 2yo start; won going away from Power Blue (gave 3lb) in Group 3 at Leopardstown (7f, good to yielding) on reappearance; pulled very hard in the 2,000 Guineas; fifth was a decent outcome in the circumstances; can make his presence felt if settling better.

runners.comment: Reversed Dewhurst form with Zavateri in the Greenham, needs to do likewise with Gstaad
runners.name: Alparslan

quotes.race: Watership Down Stud Too Darn Hot Greenham Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Alparslan is a high-class horse, and I'm sure he'll turn up in one of the Guineas, but it's a case of which one we go for. We've got time to go to the English and Irish, but it's a nice problem to have and I'm really happy. He's been to Newmarket, and he didn't like the undulations of the track, although that could've been down to two-year-old immaturity. It's a question mark. Whether racing round a bend at Longchamp for the French Guineas would be his cup of tea, I don't know, but the Curragh would suit him well as he's obviously won there. The mile is the question, but when you look at the last 50 yards, he's not stopping. He's going away if anything. I thought we were coming here under the radar. He'd only run three times, and he's entitled to improve off those runs. He's been working very well, and he's got a great mind. He will definitely come on fitness-wise, and I'm sure there's another gear for him - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won Leicester novice event by 5l on debut and landed a valuable sales event over an extended 6f at this venue last September; finished 4l behind runner-up Gstaad when a 50-1 shot in the Dewhurst; reversed the form of that race with fourth-placed Zavateri when landing the Greenham at Newbury (7f, good) on reappearance; missed the 2,000 Guineas.

stable_tour.quote: A smart, strong-travelling horse who progressed nicely last year. He acquitted himself well in the Dewhurst as he didn't handle the undulations at Newmarket. He'll go to Newbury for a trial to see how he gets on with the trip and grade, and then we'll see about one of the Guineas. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Top-class 6f form at two, not disgraced in the 2,000 Guineas, more of a sprinting type
runners.name: Power Blue

quotes.race: Keeneland Phoenix Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: He has got bigger and stronger and Power Blue is improving throughout the year. Every time he turns up he never lets us down. A furlong out I was thinking the filly wasn't going to get to him - Adrian Murray, trainer, speaking to Racing TV

quotes.race: Castle Star At Capital Stud Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: It's a bit of a usual thing with Adrian [Murray] and his team winning this race! Power Blue was well prepared and he was the ultimate professional really. He showed a little bit of greenness but he really quickened up the last hundred yards and galloped out all the way to the boards so he'll be getting a bit further than five furlongs, that's for sure. Why not? [when asked whether he could emulate the achievements of previous recent winners of this race]. He won by a wider margin today than Arizona Blaze, who was a Breeders' Cup placed horse and Bucanero Fuerte probably won in similar fashion. He's a nice horse and there's sure to be plenty of improvement - David Egan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Productive juvenile campaign over sprint distances culminated in Group 1 win here from True Love in the 6f Phoenix Stakes (good); respectable second to Thesecretadversary (received 3lb), in 7f Group 3 at Leopardstown on reappearance; by no means a bad effort in the 2,000 Guineas on his first attempt at this trip, but probably more of a sprinting type.

stable_tour.quote: He's run some very good races, including when second to Albert Einstein last time, and we think he'll go very close in the Coventry. He and Arizona Blaze are probably our best chances. 13-06-25

runners.comment: Beaten favourite at Goodwood since Listed second in Meydan, supporting role now.
runners.name: Pacific Avenue
runners.spotlight: A useful 7f/1m winner last season; made the early running in the Dewhurst, runner-up in a 1m Listed event at Meydan in February; beaten favourite in a four-runner contest at Goodwood on return to Britain; supporting role now.

runners.comment: Maiden winner at Gowran, takes a massive rise in class for his first attempt at this trip.
runners.name: Go Just Do It
runners.spotlight: Made the frame in three races at this venue last season, all won by Ballydoyle-trained colts; most meaningful form when third of five in a 7f Group 2 won by Constitution River; odds-on for a comfortable maiden win at Gowran on reappearance; massive rise in class for his first attempt at this trip.

runners.comment: Trouble in running last time, 97-rated colt faces an unenviable task, tongue-tie fitted
runners.name: Take Charge Star

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Take Charge Star was a bit unlucky first time when he didn't get much of a run and we came back ten days later because we want to try to qualify him for the [Goffs] Million. That's his big target this year - Johnny Murtagh, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Maiden winner over 7f at Gowran last September and a creditable sixth of 30 in the Goffs Million; had no luck in running in the Tetrarch Stakes over C&D earlier in the month; 97-rated colt faces an unenviable task; tongue-tie fitted.

runners.comment: Beaten a neck on both maiden starts over 7f, can win races, this is highly ambitious.
runners.name: Bamako Beach
runners.spotlight: Beaten a neck on both maiden starts over 7f; can win races; this is highly ambitious.

runners.comment: Listed-placed twice at this venue this season, supporting role for Gstaad likely the plan
runners.name: Neolithic
runners.owner: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith
runners.spotlight: Won a 6f conditions race at Naas last season; Listed-placed twice at this venue this season, on either side of a Gowran win (7f, soft); supporting role here.

runners.comment: Can maintain the progression of this season's two wins on his first attempt at this trip
runners.name: Causeway
runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

quotes.race: Coolmore Stud Henry Longfellow Irish EBF Tetrarch Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: He got home very well. I'd imagine Causeway will have no trouble stepping up in trip when the time comes. We just didn't want to start him up (in trip) in bad ground. We just wanted to get a run into him for this. He's ready. He's done his prep for it now. He'd be very comfortable coming back here for the Guineas - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Racing Writers Association Madrid Handicap
quotes.quote: Causeway was tough and he learned a lot. He took a run last year, he was a little bit lazy. He'll obviously stay a lot further. Ryan was good on him. I think he'll be very comfortable going a mile and could get further. He's brave, he stuck his head out. He can go into a winners' race now and we'll go gentle with him and let him mature away -  Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Bermingham Cameras Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Causeway is a lovely, big, scopey horse who's laid-back. He had a lovely run at Gowran and was staying on well. Even though he was coming back a furlong, we thought the way the ground was today, up here, you'd have to stay well and he obliged. He went forward down past the two and then he felt like he parked a bit. There was something that came on the stands' side and he actually went forward again so I'd say it was company he was waiting for - Wayne Lordan, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Left Gowran debut effort behind to win a 7f maiden here last October on very soft ground; won the Madrid handicap at Naas (7f, soft) on seasonal return off 94; preferred by Ryan Moore to his higher-rated stablemate Neolithic in a 1m Listed race here 19 days ago; won comfortably and can continue on the upgrade; pedigree suggests this trip will be within his range.

stable_tour.quote: He won the Madrid Handicap on his return at Naas this month. He was tough and learned a lot from that. He took a run to find his form last year as he was a little bit lazy. I think he'll be very comfortable going a mile and could get further. He can go into a winners' race now and we'll go gentle with him and let him mature. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Impressed on debut, recent Group 3 defeat can be excused, remains a high-class prospect
runners.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

quotes.race: Aesop's Fables At Compas Stallions Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
quotes.quote: We're delighted with Drop Dead Gorgeous, she's a lovely big filly. She's still a baby and learned plenty today. She was very green when she got there but we're very happy. She'll stay further. She probably will [step into an Oaks trial], something like that I'd imagine. She's a quality, big mare. We'll see what comes up for her and how she comes out of it. It was just nice to get her started -  Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Regally-bred Dubawi filly; mentioned in positive terms by trainer before a smart debut win over 1m at Naas in March; combination of inexperience and trouble in running proved her undoing in a 1m fillies Group 3 here 19 days ago; remains a high-class prospect; this trip likely to suit.

stable_tour.quote: She's a lovely, big filly and it was nice to get her started this month at Naas, where she won a mile maiden.  She has an entry in the Park Express on Friday but it could come a bit soon. She's going to be an absolutely beautiful filly next year, she's big and strong, and she's a baby still. She'll work on Tuesday and that'll tell us if she could run on Friday. It's possible as she did take her race very well. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Looked useful when winning a C&D maiden, got upset in the stalls in the Derby Trial
runners.name: Shaihaan

quotes.race: Final Furlong Podcast At 1xBet.ie Maiden
quotes.quote: I thought it was a nice performance, Shaihaan travelled and picked up well. He was pretty fit for today but he's a huge horse and this trip was going to suit and he'll improve.
