He'll head for the Leopardstown Derby Trial, he won't be an Epsom horse but could be one for the Irish Derby - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Improved from his debut when chasing home Pierre Bonnard over 1m at Dundalk last August; found the competition too hot in the Group 2 Beresford Stakes; made a fine start to the season when beating two subsequent winners in a C&D maiden; got upset in the stalls when failing to build on that in the Derby Trial at Leopardstown.

runners.comment: Plenty to prove after failing to feature in the Ballysax at Leopardstown on reappearance
runners.name: Shosholoza
runners.owner: Rectory Road Hldgs Ltd/E Palmer/W Slattery/Mrs A M OBrien

prev_owners.owner: Rectory Road Hldgs Ltd/E Palmer/W Slattery/Mrs A M OBrien

runners.spotlight: Beat a subsequent winner by a wide margin on heavy ground at Tipperary on his debut last October; creditable fifth behind Pierre Bonnard in Group 1 at Saint-Cloud only three weeks later; plenty to prove now after failing to feature in the Ballysax at Leopardstown on reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: He had two very good runs last season, winning a maiden impressively and running well in a Group 1 in France. It was our plan to take our time with him on his return at Leopardstown but that didn't suit at all the way the race set up. We might look at the [Group 3] Gallinule back at the Curragh and give him a positive ride. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Course maiden winner over 7f, well beaten at Newmarket on return, outsider of stable trio
runners.name: Amadeus Mozart
runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
runners.spotlight: Made a winning debut in a 7f maiden here last June; no match for Godolphin's Maho Bay in a novice event at Newmarket last month; the winner was a beaten favourite in the Lingfield Derby Trial.

stable_tour.quote: He won his only race last year in a 7f maiden at the Curragh in June. He's out of a Galileo mare and is the type for a Derby trial. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Limitations revealed in two Group 3 Leopardstown events won by Ballydoyle's Christmas Day
runners.name: South Island

quotes.race: Tote 20K Euros Guaranteed Placepot Today Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: South Island has always worked like a very nice horse and we've been disappointed with him once or twice. I don't think he needs that far but I thought he'd be able to dictate against less experienced rivals over that track and trip. He looks like a nice horse going forward. They went slow, and it turned into a bit of a dash. What his trip will be next year I'm not sure but he's a fine, big, strong horse and what Al Riffa has done over a mile and six would make you think he should stay pretty well next year - Donnacha O'Brien, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Course 1m1f  maiden winner on the fourth of five starts at two; limitations revealed in two Group 3 Leopardstown events won by the Aidan O'Brien-trained Dante third Christmas Day.

runners.comment: Out of his depth in the Chester Vase and will need a clear career-best to make an impact
runners.name: Mr Vettori
runners.spotlight: Won a heavy-ground maiden at Gowran last October after 50-1 second to subsequent Group 1 winner Hawk Mountain at this venue; made a satisfactory return when second of four in a conditions event at Cork; out of his depth in the Chester Vase.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a great race when second at Cork on Friday. He took a blow inside the furlong pole but rallied back. He looks a nice horse going forward. We might step him up into black-type company and a mile and a quarter looks a nice trip for him at the moment. The Leopardstown Derby Trial might come up nicely for him or we could look at Chester. 27-04-26

runners.comment: Well held by Drop Dead Gorgeous on running in a Group 3 fillies' event here last time
runners.name: Alphecca

quotes.race: Irish EBF Auction Series Race Final
quotes.quote: That was great, a lovely pot to win for Alphecca. Ger [Kervick] gets his first homebred, so he's delighted. They took a chance running her back quickly from Killarney, but it paid dividends. She jumped, travelled and picked up and got to the line really strongly. A mile is probably her trip. She is a filly who I think will get black type next year. She is improving and I think there's more to come. When they beat her in Naas, she missed the break that day, but today she had the hang of the stalls and jumped well and she's very straightforward - Gary Carroll, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Useful form on easy ground last autumn; Killarney maiden winner in early October and won a valuable restricted contest over 7f at Naas six days later; unplaced in a handicap on her seasonal debut; conditions race at Cork last month; well held by Drop Dead Gorgeous on running in a Group 3 fillies' event here last time

runners.comment: Good winner of a conditions race at Cork last month, this is likely to prove too taxing
runners.name: Zia Zabel
runners.spotlight: Ran twice at two; has matured along the right lines, judged on his victory in a conditions race at Cork last month; however, this is likely to prove too taxing.

runners.comment: Won with plenty to spare at Roscommon on handicap debut, up 10lb, may remain competitive
runners.name: Substance

quotes.race: Athlone Handicap (Div II)
quotes.quote: Substance definitely enjoyed stepping up in trip and he was always going to improve from the Sligo run. He had a good draw and a nice pace to aim at, he relaxed really good and travelled well. It was a case of pushing the button but, in fairness, he quickened up well and hit the line. That'll give him a bit of confidence and hopefully he can build on it - Dylan Browne McMonagle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Similar level of form in trio of maidens at 6f-1m on varying ground; won with plenty to spare over slightly further than this at Roscommon on handicap debut; up 10lb, may remain competitive.

runners.comment: Beat dual Group 1 winner Precise on debut, again shaped well in a Listed sprint on return
runners.name: Quiet Mutiny
runners.spotlight: Beat dual Group 1 winner Precise on debut in a 7f maiden at Fairyhouse last June on her only juvenile start; looked in need of further when staying on into a distant second behind the impressive Royal Bay Cen in a Listed sprint at Cork early this month; potentially a cut above these rivals; Cork third Oh Cecilia now rated 101 after fine Group 3 second at Naas.

runners.comment: Two wins last season were over 6f, kept on over that trip at Naas on seasonal debut
runners.name: Gavoo

quotes.race: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Gavoo had the form. I was confident today. I didn't miss the break at the Curragh too bad last time, he was just a bit raw and babyish and to be honest we didn't give him a hard time of it. I followed Colin [Keane, rider of the runner-up] the whole way around today and he's a lovely relaxed horse. I would probably like to travel a bit better, I probably looked in a bit of trouble but I knew I had Colin covered and I got it done easy. He is a nice horse for down the line - Luke McAteer, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Two wins last season were over 6f; well beaten at Galway on his only attempt at 7f; kept on for fourth place over 6f at Naas on seasonal debut (Nakamura, seventh); worth another shot at the extra furlong on that evidence.

runners.comment: Not seen again after winning a 6f maiden at Navan last July, hard to assess, may need this
runners.name: Star Of Sapphire
runners.spotlight: Made a promising debut over 5f at Bellewstown last July; not seen again after winning a 6f maiden at Navan ten days later; hard to assess, and may need this.

runners.comment: Ran in good company in turf maidens before 7f Dundalk maiden win, lacks a recent outing
runners.name: Seoul Force
runners.spotlight: Ran in good company in Ballydoyle-dominated maidens at this venue before 7f Dundalk maiden win last November; lacks a recent outing, but stable's current form is a positive.

stable_tour.quote: He was very good in breaking his maiden at Dundalk. Seven furlongs looks a nice trip for him and we'll aim him for a three-year-olds-only handicap on Irish Guineas weekend. 27-04-26

runners.comment: Finished behind stablemate Nakamura in last year's Birdcatcher Nursery, others preferred
runners.name: Morehampton
runners.spotlight: Finished behind stablemate Nakamura in last year's Birdcatcher Nursery; likely to show the benefit of a run in a conditions race at Gowran last month but others have stronger claims.

runners.comment: One of the less exposed runners in the field, placed in three maidens, yard runs three
runners.name: Zenford
runners.spotlight: One of the less exposed runners in the field; placed in three maidens, the first of which was in a Leopardstown contest won by Unauthorized last October; has the advantage of race fitness over that rival now.

runners.comment: Winner of two 6f nurseries on easy ground, a bit high in the ratings since then
runners.name: Nakamura

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: - the headgear nearly worked too well for the first half of the race, Nakamura was tanking with me. The flat track suits him, he dug it out well, got a bit lonely in the final furlong and I let him drift onto the rail. He's an improving sort who likes a bit of give in the ground - Ben Coen, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.spotlight: Did plenty of racing at two; winner of two 6f nurseries on easy ground and ran well to take fourth in the Birdcatcher at Naas; a bit high in the ratings since then; needs to step up on the form of a recent Cork run.

runners.comment: Consistent performer at Dundalk, not without a chance if reproducing her AW winter form
runners.name: Glitter And Glory
runners.spotlight: Only poor run at two was when out of her depth in a valuable sales race at this venue; consistent performer at Dundalk, not without a chance if reproducing her AW winter form; trainer also runs another AW winner, Seoul Force.

She loves the surface, travels so well and stays, but she also shows plenty of speed over seven [furlongs]. She's in the December sale as it's the end of the syndicate and we've had two fabulous years with her. She's a wonderful filly and I'd love to keep her. We've had a great time and it would be nice if somebody bought her and maybe we could get her back - David Marnane, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Three wins include twice over C&D last October; promising C&D comeback second in March, stiffer task in Listed company last time; one to consider back in handicap company, especially given his record here.

stable_tour.quote: He'll probably come back for the Bold Lad Sprint Handicap on Sunday week at the Curragh. runners.comment: Absent since 2024 but this Group 1 winner won't need to be at her very best to win today
runners.name: Friendly Soul

quotes.race: Prix de l'Opera Longines (Group 1) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Her race record has been pretty spectacular this season and it really was push button stuff today. I thought we were going sensible on the front end and Friendly Soul had a wicked turn of foot when I needed it - Kieran Shoemark, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix Alec Head (Group 2) (3yo Fillies) (Round Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Friendly Soul has only got one blot on her copybook when we rode her wrong in the Musidora. She likes to use her stride. She doesn't have to be on the lead but she doesn't like to be restrained. I don't think she particularly found the ground to her liking, it's tacky and holding out there. If the ground is like last year the Opera would be an option, but not if it's tres souple [very soft]. A mile and three around Del Mar [ Breeders' Cup Filly and Mare Turf ] is like a mile and two in Europe, as it's not a demanding track. It's just the shortest straight in America. But she'll tell us if she wants to go -  John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Longines Valiant Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Friendly Soul was drawn nine in the Musidora and came out of the gates with the racecourse stables on her right and she cocked her jaw. She's a strong-willed lady and cocked her jaw all the way around there which explained that run. We gave her time afterwards, brought her back for this and she's done it in good style. She's the type of filly to get better as the year goes on and I think she's going to be a lovely filly next year - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Musidora Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Friendly Soul hung throughout the whole race. She's not done that with me before. I couldn't steer her - Kieran Shoemark, rider.

quotes.race: William Hill Pretty Polly Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: I think it was a good race. Our other filly (Strutting) was fourth - I think she is more of a staying filly. I was impressed with the second when she won here at the Craven meeting. I think it was a solid race today as the front two drew away from the field. Friendly Soul is a lovely filly and I think she is a mile and a quarter filly. She won't be an Epsom filly but we might make a visit to Chantilly (for the French Oaks) - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

runners.spotlight: She's won five of her six starts, the latest victory coming in the Group 1 Prix de l'Opera at Longchamp (1m2f, very soft) in October 2024; absent since and she needs to prove she retains her ability, but she probably won't need to be at her very best to come out on top in this line-up.

runners.comment: Disconcerting flop on last month's reappearance but leading player judged on 3yo form
runners.name: Wemightakedlongway

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Salsabil Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Wemightakedlongway is a good filly and I thought her last run, finishing behind Delacroix, was really good for a first run back. We were looking at going to Chester but when the drop of rain came, we decided to come here and she has won impressively. I have campaigned her aggressively and she ran against colts on both of her last two runs. She's a smart filly. The Pretty Polly at the Curragh is the race we're really building towards. She's out of a No Nay Never mare, so she just wouldn't be guaranteed to go a mile and a half. We'll see whether we look at Epsom or whether we look at something else before the Pretty Polly - Joseph O'Brien, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Last season's best performances came in Group 1s when runner-up in the Irish Oaks at the Curragh (1m4f, good) and very close fourth in the Prix de l'Opera at Longchamp (1m2f, very soft); flopped on last month's reappearance at Cork, which is disconcerting, but she's a leading player if leaving that performance behind in first-time cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: She was second in the Irish Oaks and made the frame in three other Group 1s, so winning a Group 1 is the aim this season. She was disappointing on her reappearance but we were happy enough we'd left something to work on and she'll come forward a lot. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Went close in Listed/Group 3 races last season; might be the type to improve with age
runners.name: Revoir
runners.spotlight: 0-7 since winning on 2yo debut in October 2024 but she finished close-up in a few Listed/Group 3 races last season (1m2f-1m4f, various ground) and she might be the type to improve with age; not ruled out on reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: It's staggering we didn't manage to win a race with her last year. She's talented and it's down to us to campaign her right in races over ten or 12 furlongs. The Daisy Warwick will probably come too soon, but there's the Hedge of Oak at Haydock next month. After that, the likes of the Lester Piggott and Lancashire Oaks could come into play. 27-04-26

runners.comment: Made it 3-4 in handicaps with impressive win at Musselburgh; up in grade but of interest
runners.name: Noche Clasica
runners.spotlight: Made it 3-4 in handicaps when winning on last month's reappearance at Musselburgh (1m1f, good); up in trip/grade today but she powered ahead once in the clear last time and it's hard to identify where the ceiling of her ability lies; has won on good to soft (unraced on softer); dam was two-time 1m4f Listed winner; interesting contender.

runners.comment: This is much tougher than Salisbury handicap but she could have plenty more to offer
runners.name: Dreamasar
runners.owner: Hot To Trot Racing 2 & J Fill
runners.spotlight: Made it 2-4 when scoring easily on this month's handicap and seasonal debut at Salisbury (1m2f, good to firm; unraced on slow ground); had just three rivals to beat and takes a steep rise in grade today, but this half-sister to her stable's Group 1 winner Dreamloper could have plenty more to offer.

stable_tour.quote: She's a lightly raced filly from a family we know well, as a half-sister to Dreamloper, and has progressed encouragingly. I hope she can climb the ladder in handicaps before hunting black type. I think she'll stay 1m2f. 22-04-26

runners.comment: 0-4 since easy debut win but possible she'll take sizeable step forward at some point
runners.name: Consecrated

quotes.race: Bridget "Confined" Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Newcomers' Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Consecrated is a beautifully bred filly and you hope they'd come out and do something like that. Cieren [Fallon, rider] couldn't pull her up and she's going to get further. We'll probably step her up to a mile next time, and we might look at the Listed Michael Seely at York - Maureen Haggas, trainer's assistant.

runners.spotlight: Impressive win on debut at Newbury (7f, good) last April; 0-4 since (including in two Listed races) and has something to find in today's company, but this lightly raced half-sister to connections' Group 2 winner Sacred is in top hands and may be able to take a sizeable step forward at some point.

runners.comment: Listed winner last July; perhaps unsuited by Newmarket's Rowley Mile on last two starts
runners.name: Sand Gazelle
runners.spotlight: Listed winner at York (1m2f, good) last July and runner-up in Group 3 at the Curragh (1m1f, good to yielding) in August; down the field on the Rowley Mile at Newmarket on both starts since, most recently her reappearance but that may not be her track; could bounce back with a bold show in first-time cheekpieces; unraced on ground slower than good to soft.

runners.comment: Group 3 winner at Ascot last July but tailed off on reappearance at Newmarket 3 weeks ago
runners.name: Cheshire Dancer

quotes.race: Longines Valiant Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: I said to the owners when Cheshire Dancer was third at the Royal meeting that we'll come back here for the Valiant. She ran massive in the Pipalong Stakes in between and sometimes these fillies can suddenly discover a rich vein of form. The funny thing is that she failed the vet for America after Ascot. We had her sold and had accepted an offer for considerably less than she's now worth. It's funny how it goes - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

quotes.race: Kensington Palace Stakes (Fillies' Handicap)
quotes.quote: Brilliant run from the filly. Cheshire Dancer has been tried over a mile and a quarter, and dropped back to a mile. She had a good run today, she seems to enjoy this track and ground - David Probert, jockey.

runners.spotlight: 22-1 winner of the Group 3 Valiant Stakes at Ascot (1m, good) last July and good fourth in US Grade 3 (1m, firm) next time; of interest on that form but tailed off in first-time cheekpieces (retained) on reappearance at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) three weeks ago; unraced on slow ground.

stable_tour.quote: The plan last year was to try to get her into the Sandringham, which we failed to do, as she went to Kempton and ran the only bad race of her life. This year the plan would be to head to the Kensington Palace Stakes, so she'll probably have one run before she goes there. She's a good-looking filly with a lovely pedigree, so I'd be hopeful we can get some black type with her. 09-04-25

She looked like she wanted further when running in Saturday's Sun Chariot. It was a Group 1 gallop from end-to-end and we weren't quite up to that grade on that occasion. Before that, she'd run a career-best every time this year, including when winning a Group 3 at Ascot. Her owners might keep her in training as a five-year-old, which would be great, as Group horses are hard to come by. If she was to get some Group 1 form that would enhance her paddock value - she's a very good-looking mare. She's a very special filly, owned by a syndicate of fairly normal racing fans. 08-10-25

runners.comment: Group 3 winner in France last October and might not be far away despite a 5lb penalty
runners.name: Sparks Fly

quotes.race: Prix Perth (Group 3) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I've been adamant for two seasons Sparks Fly is a Group 1 mare if she gets her conditions. She's had a tough year on the wrong ground and when she gets her conditions, she's unbeatable. She's a lot better around a left-handed track but soft ground is key. She'll race on again next year as a six-year-old and we'll try and win her a Group 1 - David Loughnane, trainer.

quotes.race: Princess Elizabeth Stakes (Sponsored By Oddschecker) (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares)
quotes.quote: Sparks Fly has run a blinder, she just didn't get out in time. She's handled the ground fine and that's the first time she's gone and got black type with good in the going description, I'm thrilled with the run. It was a real blinder and it opens up a few more options for her now. I've always thought she was a Group Three horse and she's proved it there. I thought she was the best horse in the race, but just got held up and didn't get there in time - David Loughnane, trainer.

quotes.race: Prix Isola Bella - Fonds Europeen de l'Elevage (Listed Race) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Turf)
quotes.quote: We've not done our usual thing of bowling her out in front and Sparks Fly has quickened away really impressively. We've got so much in hand I think that next year's going to be a really fun year with her - Laura Pearson, jockey.

quotes.race: Robin Hood Stakes (Listed Race) (Formerly Known As The Ben Marshall Stakes)
quotes.quote: Sparks Fly is unreal. I'm so proud of her mother [Stepping Out], who has produced some amazing horses for us. She's had her, Caroline Dale and Baby Steps, and they were all very useful. We thought last time in France she could have gone a bit faster even though she was in front, so Laura decided to go forward again this time and play catch me if you can. The filly never stopped and she loved it ? she had her ears pricked the whole way around. We'll go back to Saint-Cloud for the Prix Isola Bella she won last year. It's on November 10 and she'll get her preferred soft ground there - Dave Lowe, owner.

quotes.race: Prix Coronation (Listed Race) (3yo+ Fillies & Mares) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Sparks Fly has not had the best of seasons but the ground was wrong for her at the Curragh and we had to take her to the other end of the track because she hangs and we have to do what she wants to do. This track suits her down to the ground. She has a lot of ability and a lot of spirit and, as long as we point that in the right direction, she takes us there - Laura Pearson, jockey.

quotes.race: Book Bounce Bingo At Ayr Racecourse Handicap
quotes.quote: Every time I ride Sparks Fly she seems to be coming on mentally and physically. The sky's the limit. I remember when I rode her at Wolverhampton on her first go (in a handicap) and she wasn't quite there on the all-weather, but she's really bounced on the turf. She likes the softer ground, she prefers to be swimming more than running. There's definitely more to come and I'd say she's holding a lot more under her belly - Laura Pearson, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Four-time Listed winner who made Group 3 breakthrough at Saint-Cloud (1m, very soft) last October; ran well when 2l fourth in Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester (10.3f, good) recently; may be vulnerable to stronger stayers at this trip and she carries a 5lb penalty, but might not be far away.

stable_tour.quote: She was a real flag-bearer for us last year, winning eight races in all. To win her first race off 59 in May and then win a Listed race by 12 lengths and finish off on 107 was phenomenal. Once she started winning she kept pulling out more and more. She looks like she's strengthened up loads and I think we'll have a bit of fun again this year. Soft ground is paramount for her. The only bad run she had was at York and I was kicking myself for running as I walked the track and it was too quick, but we thought we have to try her on quick ground at some stage. We know now it's not her gig. As soon as she got back on to soft, she relished it again and finished off the season really strongly. We were struggling for a race to start her off this time and ended up running her over 7f at Haydock, which is too short but we needed to get a run into her. She's got loads of options but it's down to the weather. There's the Group 3 Princess Elizabeth at Epsom on Saturday and then Royal Ascot. If we don't get the ground, we'll have to go to France or Ireland. She's working the house down at home and is ready to rock and roll. 30-05-24

14:20.race_name: William Hill Silver Bowl Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners.comment: Considerable promise on all three starts; may well be superior to this opening mark
runners.name: Princling
runners.spotlight: Runner-up last October on both 2yo starts (7f, AW/good), on the second occasion in a novice contest at Newmarket that has worked out very well; reappeared with ready win at 1-4 at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) and there's every chance this unexposed colt will be superior to this opening mark.

runners.comment: Novice wins on last two starts; could be on an advantageous mark for this handicap debut
runners.name: Langstone
runners.spotlight: Reappeared having been gelded and left sole 2yo run (6f, soft) well behind to win at Doncaster (7f, good to soft); improved again to follow up in Kempton novice (7f, AW), doing well to score having been carried left; could be on an advantageous mark for this handicap debut, especially now at 1m.

runners.comment: The form of his sole nursery run reads well and he easily won an AW maiden on his return
runners.name: Crest Of Fire

quotes.race: Always Gamble Responsibly At BetMGM Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Crest Of Fire was entitled to go and win the way he did. He's been an exciting horse, he's been gelded over the winter and that seemed to do him a lot of good. He's a progressive type - David Probert, jockey

runners.spotlight: Having made the running he was beaten just a neck on nursery debut at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last September, which was the second leg of a four-timer for the winner; reappeared with 10l win at 2-5 in maiden at Southwell (1m, AW) in March and he could be well treated off an unaltered mark.

runners.comment: Travelled well when winning at Sandown and he could have more left in the tank
runners.name: Laureate Crown

quotes.race: Juddmonte British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands A/B/C/D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Hugo thought Laureate Crown was going to need the run but said he liked him a lot. You wouldn't have wanted to hear my language two furlongs out but he looks even nicer than we thought he was after that. As long as he comes out of it well, he'll go for the Group 2 Vintage Stakes [over 7f] at Goodwood. The Hays love Goodwood and will have a huge team, including the likes of Twisting Physics and Purosangue - Alex Cole, racing manager.

runners.spotlight: Reappeared at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in March having been gelded and won a small-field handicap, and he improved again to follow up at Sandown (1m, good); this hold-up horse travelled well last time and could have more left in the tank, provided the ground suits (unproven on slow surface).

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse. He won well on his debut and then we probably overfaced him a bit. He's been gelded since his last run and he'll improve given time because he's a very big horse. 08-10-25

runners.comment: Solid efforts on both starts this spring; remains lightly raced but needs a step forward
runners.name: Blue Courvoisier
runners.spotlight: Reappeared with close second on handicap debut at Newmarket (1m, good) last month and 3l fourth of 11 at Ascot (1m, good) since; remains lightly raced but he needs to take a step forward if he's to win today.

runners.comment: Won final two 2yo starts and denied clear run on reappearance; 1m can suit; chance
runners.name: Astrazar

quotes.race: British EBF £100,000 Final (Colts And Geldings)
quotes.quote: All the credit goes to Astrazar. He fluffed the start, he jumped very slow and I ended up a long way back. But he came good for me from halfway. I had to weave my way through and once I got daylight he really knuckled down and galloped to the line. He has a good attitude and will make a good three-year-old - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Won Ffos Las maiden (7.3f, heavy) last September on seventh start when going beyond 6f for first time, and he followed up in a valuable EBF final at York (7f, good); denied a clear run when mid-division in handicap at Newbury (7f, good) on reappearance and the step up to 1m looks a good move; chance.

stable_tour.quote: He's been gelded since winning twice in a busy first season and could be a progressive handicapper.  He's been training well. Things didn't go his way on his return at Newbury but he ran well in defeat. His trip will be 7f to a mile and we hope he could make into a horse for the Britannia at Royal Ascot. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Reappeared with close second at Musselburgh but soundly beaten at Newmarket since
runners.name: Vincenzo Peruggia
runners.spotlight: Won at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) on the second of his three 2yo starts and reappeared with close second of six in handicap at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft; unraced on softer); however, soundly beaten at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) since and needs to bounce back.

runners.comment: Short-headed on handicap debut at Naas in race that is working out well; respected up 4lb
runners.name: Jamestown
runners.spotlight: Promising fourth on debut at Dundalk (7f, AW) in March and runner-up on next two starts (7f/1m, soft/good), most recently short-headed at Naas on handicap debut in a race that is working out well; this Irish challenger is respected up 4lb for last time.

runners.comment: Did it nicely in small field on stable debut; 2-3 and open to further improvement
runners.name: Sovereign Ocean

quotes.race: Read Meg Nicholls' Blog At betmgm.co.uk Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: We thought Sovereign Ocean was quite a cheap purchase on his form. He's done that nicely and will get a mile no problem on breeding. The owner [Fabio Manservigi] is new to us and we'll talk to him about plans, but we could wait until the spring now - Marco Botti, trainer.

quotes.race: EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Iain [Jardine, trainer] and I went over to Fairyhouse last September and we were looking for quick two-year-olds. Sovereign Ocean has just taken a bit longer. He's by Ten Sovereigns and even though he was a six-furlong horse, most of his progeny are seven furlongs to a mile, so we waited until today. He stayed on fantastically well and he's done it really nicely against some nice horses. I think that was a good race - Ian Jones, owner, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Won for Iain Jardine on debut at Musselburgh (7f, good) last July then 11l sixth of seven in the Acomb at York (7f, good to firm); won in a small field on his stable/handicap debut at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in December and this likeable type is open to further improvement; not ruled out.

stable_tour.quote: He went to Musselburgh for his debut and went off at 33-1 but we went there thinking he'd run well and we weren't surprised when he won. He wasn't showing us a lot at the start of the year but we were really chuffed with the way he was working before his first run and then he took a massive step forward. Going for the Acomb at York was a tough ask but we'd had an offer after his debut, which wasn't quite enough, and we were looking to increase his value. He'll have an entry in the horses in training sale. 10-09-25

runners.comment: Promising start to career (all three runs over 1m on AW); improvement needed but possible
runners.name: Penny Time
runners.spotlight: All three starts over 1m on AW; first past the post on debut at Kempton in March (disqualified; rider weighed in light) then won easily at Southwell before 4l second of 12 in another novice there; improvement is needed if he's to make a winning turf/handicap debut but that can't be ruled out.

runners.comment: Close Listed 5th (7f, AW) on sole run this year; step up to 1m may eke out something extra
runners.name: Sir Albert
runners.spotlight: 2-2 in nurseries last summer (7f, good/heavy) and returned with close Listed fifth at Lingfield (7f, AW) in February; has top weight in this hot handicap but the step up to 1m may eke out something extra; each-way chance.

runners.comment: Good form on soft last September; may have needed comeback but not obviously well treated
runners.name: Suspended Sentence
runners.owner: G C Myddelton C F E Hill & Partner
runners.spotlight: Won Ripon novice (1m, good to firm) last August on third start then followed up in four-runner nursery at Sandown (1m, soft), before creditable Listed fourth in France (1m, soft); he may have needed last month's comeback run at Sandown (1m, good to firm) but he's not obviously well treated.

runners.comment: Worth a second look in view of his good third of 18 in a nursery at York last August
runners.name: Special Dividend

quotes.race: Book Hotel And Conferencing At Wolverhampton EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We know the family well, we have the three-part brother Dividend who has done really well for us. Special Dividend is a much bigger and stronger horse than where Dividend was last year. I didn't want to risk running him on quick ground first time out and it was a nice introduction on the all-weather, he did everything we hoped he would. Hollie [Doyle] said he got a little bit lonely in front and she went all the way down to the back of the back straight, she couldn't pull him up. I think he'd have won a bit further if he had anything around him. He's not your typical small, sharp two-year-old, he's a big scopey horse and weighs over 500kg. We don't want to push him too early - he could be really nice for us - Jamie Insole, joint-trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won last summer on first two starts (6f, AW) then kept on for third of 18 in nursery at York (7f, good to firm) that worked out nicely; well beaten in Newmarket Group 3 (7f, good) on final 2yo start (gelded since) but retains potential and he's worth a second look in a first-time tongue-tie.

runners.comment: 2-2 in slow-ground nurseries last autumn; could build on his respectable comeback run
runners.name: Synners Kid

quotes.race: GAIN The Advantage Series Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: That was Synners Kid's first run in handicap company and they went a nice gallop. The ground was soft enough for him, he took a little bit of time to get going but once he did he hit the front and stayed going. He didn't give up on me and I feel like there's plenty to come from him. He stayed the mile lovely and could get further in time - Wayne Hassett, rider.

runners.spotlight: Won for Joseph O'Brien on nursery debut at Naas (1m, yielding to soft) last September and easily followed up at Bellewstown (1m, soft), both in a tongue-tie; having shot up the weights he reappeared with a respectable sixth of ten on stable debut at Ascot (7f, good) recently and could build on that back on slow ground with the tongue-tie reapplied; not discounted.

runners.comment: Won at Newmarket three weeks ago and this progressive colt has gone up just 3lb
runners.name: St Anton

quotes.race: Betfred "The Classic Bookmaker" Handicap
quotes.quote: St Anton saw out the trip well. The ground was fast enough for him and he hit a few of the undulations but finished off well and he could get a mile and a quarter -  Joe Leavy, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Close third on handicap/seasonal debut at Newmarket (1m, good) last month and won there (1m, good to firm) next time; showed promise on good to soft last September (unraced on softer); he has a progressive profile and has gone up just 3lb for last time; could again be involved.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big colt who strengthened up through the spring and I thought he ran a super race at Newmarket last week, probably just needing it in terms of race fitness. He'll take a bit of beating if we can get him into something like the Britannia. He should get a trip in time, which is unusual for the sire. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Had to work hard to win at 1-4 at Nottingham but has potential off his opening mark
runners.name: Lighting Thunder
runners.spotlight: Runner-up at Yarmouth (1m, good to soft) last September on sole 2yo start and filled same position in big-field maiden at Newbury (1m, good) on return; had to work pretty hard to win at 1-4 at Nottingham (1m, good) last time but has potential off his opening mark; cheekpieces go on.

runners.comment: Failed to settle and weakened in 1m2f Classic Trial; could run well back down in trip
runners.name: Winding Stream
runners.spotlight: Won at Southwell (7f, AW) last October on sole 2yo start and returned with good second at Kempton (1m, AW); failed to settle in front and weakened in 1m2f Group 3 Classic Trial at Sandown (1m2f, good) four weeks ago; goes handicapping off a fair mark and could run well back down in trip.

runners.comment: 3-3 at 6f, including Group 1; failed to stay 1m on return; leading claims back at 6f
runners.name: Venetian Sun

quotes.race: Betfred 1000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: I've only had a brief chat with Cliff [Lee] and he didn't think Venetian Sun stayed. She hit the gates very strong and had no cover ? her draw didn't help. Two out, I thought she was getting on the tail of Venetian Lace, and I thought here we go. But she just petered out in the final furlong and we'll look at going down the Commonwealth Cup route now with her - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Sumbe Prix Morny (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (Straight Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Venetian Sun is unbelievable, she does everything so relaxed. I've been saying for a little while that she's a special filly and she's proved it there. Early on in the year she stood out in the string and I said to her owners a month ago, she doesn't quite stand out as much and the others have caught her up a little bit, but she's still got so much ability. She'll be better with easier ground. I was very worried when I walked the ground earlier, it's as quick as I've known it here and I've been coming for a number of years now. That dampened my confidence. She'll be better over an extra furlong as well, I'm convinced of that, so we'll go for the Moyglare next and see where we go from there. It will tell us if she's a Classic filly but she's got to prove it. She's got a temperament to die for - Karl Burke, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes (Sponsored By bet365) (Group 2) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: When Venetian Sun cruised to the front, she went a couple of lengths clear and thought it was all over. Ed's [Walker] horse quickened up nicely and Cliff [Lee] just said Venetian Sun was just dossing a bit in front. She is a filly a bit like that as she's so laidback and I also think the ground was on the quick side for her today. She is a very high-class filly. I think the Lowther would be out for her now as she has won a Group Two. She is in the Prix Morny and we'll have a look at that but we are very keen to step up to seven furlongs in the Moyglare. Her pedigree says she is more a miler at least and a three-year-old. She's a very mature filly with a great engine. I think she can be better on better ground and over a trip. She relaxes so well in behind. I think racing against the very best horses will bring out the best in her - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Albany Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: I think Venetian Sun is a a very special filly. The work she has done at home, I haven't had a 2yo filly do work like it; just the last six weeks. She's kicking older group horses out the way at home. I worked a good, old work horse with her about a month ago or just after her debut and I had to work her with another good one that I knew was reliable and she did the same to him and I'm talking 110 rated horses. I think she's very special - Karl Burke, trainer. Karl did say she was the 2yo filly he's had, so we had a lot of confidence in her. So we were confident and happy to back him, and he did a great job with her. I don't think everything went for her - tough draw and she didn't have much cover, so yeah - Ian McAleavy, joint-owner.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cliff [Lee, jockey] gave Venetian Sun a lovely ride and he said he ended up hitting the front too soon and she was just dossing about a bit in front. It's just greenness and she'll learn loads from that. It was a very good race for the grade and I would say she's very, very useful. If she goes to Royal Ascot it will be the Albany I would think, she's a real six-furlong filly - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Top 6f 2yo, completing a notable hat-trick with wins in Group 3 at Royal Ascot, Group 2 at Newmarket (July) and Group 1 at Deauville (all good/good to firm); seemed fine at 7f (ran on after meeting trouble) when third in the Moyglare at the Curragh (yielding) on her final start but shaped like a non-stayer when stepped up to 1m for 1,000 Guineas at Newmarket on reappearance; remains open to progress back at 6f; leading claims.

stable_tour.quote: The top two-year-old filly in Britain last year. I think she was every bit as good as Aidan's [O'Brien] fillies who came on strong late on, whereas we were on the go quite early, and she beat the colts in the Morny. On her last start in the Moyglare, she was beaten two out and it wasn't her true running. She's wintered really well and the plan is to go straight to the Guineas. The key question is whether she'll stay a mile, but if ever a filly was going to, it would be her - I think she's got an 80-90 per cent chance. If that doesn't come to fruition, we can revert back to sprinting. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Listed win at 2; improved again promising third to Coppull on Ascot return; more to come
runners.name: Division

quotes.race: Coral Rockingham Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: That was a good performance. Division is talented and very fast. He needed to know when to get serious and when I asked him he was there for it, which was great - Tom Marquand, jockey.

quotes.race: Thoroughbred Daily News EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Division has taken another step forward and was out on his own for long enough in a stiff breeze. He's bred to be good as his sister is Celandine. He has some nice entries but whether he's up to any of them just yet I don't know. We'll have a chat about it, no doubt - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: OW Mobile Bars EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Division wants to step up in grade for sure, but whether he wants soft ground, I don't know - William Haggas, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Raced at 6f; won three times last year, notably a York Listed race (good; also won on good to soft); improved again when coming with a strong late run (started slowly) for 0.5l third to Coppull in Ascot Group 3 (good to firm) on reappearance three weeks ago; probably capable of better again.

runners.comment: Landed 6f Ascot Group 3 on return, with two of today's rivals behind; should go well again
runners.name: Coppull

quotes.race: Commonwealth Cup Trial Stakes (Registered As The Pavilion Stakes) (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Coppull has wintered well, and by God, he's got a lot stronger. I was really impressed by the way he quickened twice, even though he idled a bit before going again. I'm very proud of him. The Sandy Lane is a very logical step, but we'll come back here. The Commonwealth Cup is a very important race for the three-year-olds and it's nice to be targeting that. It's important to have that pathway before it gets tough against the older boys in the second part of the year - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Middle Park Stakes (Group 1) (Colts)
quotes.quote: We're happy as Coppull has backed up his Richmond win at Goodwood. We're over the moon to be honest and he could have been second in another few strides. That will be it for the year - Clive Cox, trainer.

quotes.race: Markel Richmond Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: When Coppull ran so well at Ascot we felt that Goodwood would suit him. I really was worried about the rain coming too soon and we've literally timed it to perfection - Clive Cox, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won the Group 2 Richmond Stakes at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good) last July and rounded off his juvenile campaign with a close third in the Group 1 Middle Park at Newmarket (6f, good to firm); showed he's trained on well with a win in 6f Ascot Group 3 (good to firm) on reappearance, with reopposing Division 0.5l behind in third (Brussels sixth); likely to go well for yard which won this with Harry Angel in 2017.

runners.comment: Second in Middle Park last year but over 4l behind Coppull and Division on Ascot return
runners.name: Brussels

quotes.race: Tattersalls Middle Park Stakes (Group 1) (Colts)
quotes.quote: We were very happy. Brussels is a big, strong, fast horse and we were delighted with that run. He did look good on his first start, but he has been a bit babyish. I think it will come, but he's very big. I think all the experience he's getting this year will stand him in good stead for next year. He's not short of speed. I'd imagine we'll leave him alone now. We'll probably have a look at a Classic with him and see how it goes - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Avenuebloodstock.com Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Ryan said Brussels was very babyish, he's never been away. He will come forward a lot for it and all these horses are running with Ascot in mind but Ryan said it might come too quick because he was so babyish. We'll see how much he comes on. He said he'd have no problem getting seven and he's a massive, big, powerful horse - Aidan O'Brien, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Runner-up twice in Group 1 company as a juvenile, including in the Middle Park at Newmarket with Coppull narrowly behind in third; however, he made an underwhelming start to his 3yo career when only sixth to Coppull (Division third) in 6f Ascot Group 3 on reappearance 22 days ago; possible he simply needed the run but arrives with a point to prove.

stable_tour.quote: He was consistent last season and finished second in the Middle Park and the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint. He'll be on the three-year-old sprint programme on the way to the Commonwealth Cup. We were happy with him on Sunday morning, he just wants better ground. 31-03-26

runners.breeder: J Hanly A Stroud & Skymarc Farm
runners.comment: Gimrack second; yard no stranger to success in this but going softer than good a worry
runners.name: Rock On Thunder
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.spotlight: Raced at 6f; smart 2yo, notably second in the Gimcrack at York; below par tackling going softer than good for the first when sixth in the Mill Reef at Newbury on final start, which is a bit of a concern should the ground here remain on the soft side; on a positive note, his yard has won this twice since 2019, including with Inisherin in these silks two years ago.

runners.comment: Won Group 3 and 4th in Group 1 as 2yo; late headway on 5f reappearance; return to 6f helps
runners.name: Five Ways

quotes.race: Unibet Sirenia Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We've always liked Five Ways. He shows a lot of ability in his homework and he won well at Salisbury last time, so we just thought it was worth a go. He'll stay further in time, we'll just have to see if we go again this year. He's a lovely horse for the future. We were a bit disappointed first time out, but the ground was a bit loose and he had a bit of wheelspin and probably needed the run - Andrew Balding. trainer.

quotes.race: Michael Brunton Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted, I bred Five Ways, his dam, grandmother and the one before that. Andrew's always thought he was a good horse but I'm surprised by how easy he's won. We hope he's a nice horse but I've been breeding horses for over 50 years so I know not to get too excited. It was a quick time so it's all looking good. I think he'll stay further and it will be time for a reassessment after that - John Hobby, owner-breeder.

runners.spotlight: AW Group 3 winner last September and bettered that form when 2.75l fourth to Wise Approach (Brussels second, Coppull third) in Group 1 Middle Park at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) later that month; late headway for seventh of 14 in 5f Group 3 back at Newmarket on reappearance; likely to benefit from the return to 6f but whether he's quite good enough remains to be seen.

runners.comment: Finished in front of Venetian Sun in 1,000 Guineas but far from sure to back sprinting
runners.name: Spicy Marg

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF 'Bosra Sham' Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: This was only Spicy Marg's second run over six furlongs but on that you'd say she'd get further. We could look at something like the Nell Gwyn in the spring - Michael Bell, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I've been a little bit frustrated with Spicy Marg but, with hindsight, she's had legitimate excuses. She was impressive first time out and her homework has always been exceptional so I really fancied her going into the Queen Mary. She came into season the morning of [the race] so we had to put a line through that and when I rode her at Newmarket over six [furlongs] last time she pinged the gates, did too much early and didn't stay. The set up for her today was ideal and we saw the filly I hoped she was - Kieran Shoemark, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Spicy Marg did a nice piece of work ten days ago when she quickened up very nicely so we were hopeful coming here today. I trained her dam and when I saw this filly at the sales I was never going to be beaten in buying her. She'll go for the Marygate next - Michael Bell, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Proved a useful sprinter last season, notably winning over 5f at Glorious Goodwood in the summer and over 6f at Newmarket (good-ground Listed contest) final outing; finished in front of Venetian Sun when creditable eighth in the 1,000 Guineas on her reappearance; while she shouldn't be inconvenienced by the drop back to 6f it remains to be seen whether she can confirm that superiority over Karl Burke's filly at the shorter distance.

stable_tour.quote: She's one of the top-rated two-year-old fillies in Britain. After she won at Newmarket in early May everything was working backwards from Royal Ascot and the Queen Mary. We ducked a couple of options at York and Carlisle with a view that we're saving our powder. We think she's very smart. With the ground, I wouldn't mind it fast but if it was very soft that would be an unknown. We really like her and she's my trainer's pick. 09-06-25

runners.comment: Useful AW winner but limitations seemingly exposed at Group 3/Listed level last twice
runners.name: Aqpan
runners.spotlight: AW maiden winner but limitations seemingly exposed at Group 3 and Listed level at Newbury since, including dropped to 6f last weekend.

stable_tour.quote: I think he was beaten by two very good horses in his two races last season. He wasn't tuned-up 100 per cent for his return at Southwell on Saturday and was only really getting into top gear late on, but I thought he was a good winner at the line. He holds an entry in the French 2,000 Guineas and we have to put his credentials on trial now, possibly in the Greenham. We don't know how good he is, but hopefully he's a colt we can be bold and ambitious with. He'll get a mile no problem and I think he's quite smart. 01-04-26

runners.comment: Made all in Palace House on first run since being gelded and he could be tough to reel in
runners.name: Night Raider

quotes.race: HKJC World Pool Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Night Raider is a high-class horse and we always knew he had a huge engine. He won his first two races over seven furlongs on the all-weather and we then tried to turn him into a miler and ran him in the Guineas, but he was just too keen, too free and too fractious. Gelding has really made him and brought him on. He is 10kg lighter than last year and I thought he looked tremendous in the paddock. I thought if he jumped quick and got into a rhythm he'd handle the undulations, which he did.  He was a bit fractious in the stalls last year as a full horse, but the gelding has calmed him down a bit. He's been working nicely - he does a lot on his own, as you don't need to work him with other horses. That's a great result for Wathnan Racing and Richard Brown, who has always had huge faith in him. I think it would be Royal Ascot now. He is also in at York, but that might come too quickly for him. I think he'd stay six furlongs - Karl Burke, trainer.We gelded Night Raider because he wasn't doing things 100% right. It was a good decision by the whole team and it's transformed him, he's a much more relaxed character. I know looking at the race and the way he ran you wouldn't think that but that's what he is - a real ball of speed. He tired a bit late on as he was entitled to  given we went ferocious fractions but I like the way he pulled out. Last year when one came to him he folded quite tamely whereas there he went again - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: When everything goes smoothly for him and Night Raider is relaxed in the prelims and at the start, he's a horse with a lot of natural ability - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK Golden Rose Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Night Raider was very comfortable going a good gallop. He beat two decent benchmarks in Wiltshire and Annaf - Oisin Murphy, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Boost Your Acca At BetMGM Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The idea was to go straight to the Guineas with a racecourse gallop at the Craven meeting. Another run is probably the right thing to do, Danny [Tudhope, jockey] said Night Raider could do with another run, he's still green in front but he's obviously a very good horse - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Not beaten far in two 5f Group 1s last August/September (good to firm/yielding) and he finally got off the mark on turf when making all in the Group 3 Palace House Stakes at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; that was his first run since being gelded and he could be tough to reel in.

stable_tour.quote: He's just come back to us after a little operation. He's a very quick horse who has been gelded, which will help him because he was edgy. He'll be entered in the five-furlong sprints, although I still think he can stay six. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Two Group 1 wins last season and could leave her recent reappearance run well behind
runners.name: Asfoora

quotes.race: Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp Longines (Group 1) (2yo+) (Sprint Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It's just surreal really. We had a couple of little pre-race issues, we had to work through those. We were within a minute and a half of not running - I had an Uber driver on a retainer of 200euros to get the mare's passport here in time. We try to experience new things. I've never been to the races in France and here we are winning a Group 1 on Arc day - Henry Dwyer, trainer of Asfoora.Asfoora was fantastic. The sprint course is a fair bit drier than the round course and she was basically on the bridle throughout. She was fortunate to have a plum [low] draw and I didn't have to ask her much but her condition was the best it's been on the build up to this race. She still has her summer coat and it took some amount of management - Oisin Murphy, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: It seems surreal, silly and it's all been a novelty. I've really been on a holiday with Asfoora the last two years. It was all getting a bit hard before Ascot as we didn't have the transport, and if I'm 100 per cent honest, if I owned her I wouldn't have come back. Akram [El-Fahkri, owner] was very insistent we did and that she deserved another chance. I'd love to see the replay as I was under a scrum of people for the last bit, but that looked very convincing. When you know they're going to win at the two-furlong marker, you're on pretty good terms with yourself. It was an easy watch and really enjoyable. She'll tell us if she doesn't want to be racing any more, but after that you can't say that's the case. She's been a once-in-a-lifetime horse for two years in a row and who knows, maybe three. That'll be a decision for Akram. He's a sportsman and would love to keep her going, why wouldn't you? We can't rule out coming back next year, but she owes us nothing - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: Asfoora has run well but she was 6-4 favourite so you like to see those ones win. She didn't so we're probably a little bit disappointed but it's not as though she's run tenth. She's run well but probably not as well as her last couple. I didn't like her last 50 metres, she was there to run second or at least third and she was a little bit plain in that last little bit. Whether she's reached her peak or she's on the way down, or whether she didn't like the track, I'm not sure. We might go to Ireland for the Flying Five but if anything comes out of the run and we're not happy with her she'll be going home - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.race: King George Qatar Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Asfoora has gone as well as we could have hoped and we're very proud of her. You could just tell about 400 metres after the start she just came off the bridle. She's quick but they were a bit quick for her early. Big Evs controlled his own destiny whereas we were stuck behind a couple and got a bit of a bump which probably cost us the win but she's run well and we're more than happy just to be competing - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

quotes.race: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: We needed a lead-up run at Haydock, so we were always going to come early, but just with the changing of seasons we wanted to be here before it was too cold in Australia and too warm. We came over in the nice interchange period and Asfoora settled in brilliantly. The proof of that was in the pudding today. I've got to have a look at the race conditions again but we'd love to showcase her a bit. Everyone has just been so good to us over here and I'd love to send her down to Goodwood and up to York, but we'll put the horse first - Henry Dwyer, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Carries a 5lb penalty today and she was down the field on her comeback at Newmarket three weeks ago; however, she may have needed that run and is entitled to respect having won two 5f Group 1s last season, namely the Nunthorpe at York (good to firm) and the Prix de l'Abbaye at Longchamp (very soft).

runners.comment: Two Listed wins last August/October and could build on this month's Palace House third
runners.name: Shagraan

quotes.race: BetMGM Rous Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Shagraan is improving all the time. He's still growing and filling out and I think he'll be even better next year. We'll put him away now and look to next spring. He loves his racing and hopefully next year he'll be a Group horse. Kieran [Shoemark] gave him a great ride, he's not ridden many for me before but he did exactly as we told him and it was a great job - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Be Friendly Handicap
quotes.quote: Shagraan was drawn on the wrong side and the ground was a bit on the softer side than ideal, but he's done it well. He's still improving and places like Bahrain might suit him, so we'll have a look at where we're going to go - Mick Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Anderson Roofing Supplies Ltd 20th Anniversary Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Shagraan has taken a big step forward from his Haydock run and shown a bit of class. We thought he was a horse who could run in a decent grade and he's shown that there. We'll stay at six furlongs for now. Windsor is a nice, sharp track and he was always travelling smoothly and he picked up well. He'll come forward again for that - Clive Cox, trainer.

runners.spotlight: His form took a surge forward towards the end of last season with 5f Listed wins for Mick Appleby at Beverley (good to firm) and Ascot (soft); reappeared with 3l third of 14 to Night Raider on stable debut in the Group 3 Palace House at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) and he's open to improvement on this second start of the season; one to consider.

stable_tour.quote: He's a strong and competitive colt by a great sire in Sioux Nation. He made a pleasing second start when an impressive winner at Windsor over 6f, where he travelled strongly throughout. We upped him in class to Listed level last month for the Rose Bowl at Newbury where he stepped up with his performance in finishing a good second. On his homework I think 6f is his strip but he is sharp and ideally he would probably be at his best over 5½f, which leads me to think of the Flying Childers, which we won with Caturra in 2021, who had previously won the Rose Bowl on his way to that Group 2 success. This fellow is definitely going the right way and he runs in the Group 3 Molecomb Stakes at Glorious Goodwood on Wednesday. 02-08-23

runners.comment: Won this last year and some good runs in defeat subsequently; might be thereabouts
runners.name: Mgheera
runners.owner: Lord Lloyd Webber And Arthur Mitchell

prev_owners.owner: European Bloodstock Management & Mme Marie-Christelle Lacail

quotes.race: Betfred Temple Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Mgheera is a good sprinter and it's very exciting. We've got plenty of work into her, but she's always slowly away and that certainly wouldn't be a problem at Ascot. It should really suit her, especially that stiff five furlongs from being held up. There's a chance she might ship down to Australia after Ascot but we will have to persuade the owners to stay a bit longer as she would have a real chance in a Nunthorpe - Ed Walker, trainer.

quotes.race: Prix de Saint-Georges (Group 3) (3yo+) (Sprint Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It's quick ground out there and Mgheera loved it. Tom Marquand rode her at home and told me not to worry, she's got the action of a real fast-ground filly. Oisin [Murphy, jockey] nailed it. I was worried she was stuck behind [fourth home] Keran and that she wasn't going anywhere, but he wheeled out and got a lovely clean trip - Ed Walker, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Made it 2-2 for the yard (good/good to soft) when winning this last year and some good runs in defeat subsequently, including in Group 1s; could improve for her recent reappearance sixth at Longchamp; might be thereabouts.

stable_tour.quote: She's in great nick and has done everything right since joining us from France for this season, winning at Longchamp and then in the Temple Stakes. I'm really excited to see her step up in grade. She'll have to improve again but you wouldn't rule it out. 10-06-25

She stays in training and we have three shots with her before she retires to Australia. She'll follow the same campaign as last year in the Prix de Saint-Georges and Temple Stakes - both of which she won in 2025 - before the King Charles III at Royal Ascot. She seems as good as ever, if not better, and I'm sure we can make those races count. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Impressively made all in big-field handicap at York last week; could make another bold bid
runners.name: Jakajaro

quotes.race: Lindum York Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't expect Jakajaro to lead this field in such a high-quality race but he's just getting better and he's getting faster. I don't know why. He had talent when he was in Ireland and he contested some pretty snazzy races last year. This year he's been a different horse altogether. Maybe it's just that he's a year older and we know a little bit more about him. He'll have to go up to stakes company now, he's earned it. He's in the Temple Stakes and he could quite easily go for something like that - Robert Cowell, trainer.

quotes.race: Betway 4 To Win Handicap
quotes.quote: It wasn't the plan to make the running with Jakajaro but Jamie walked the track beforehand and the far side was the place to be. It's nice that he's retained all his old abilities - Robert Cowell, trainer.

quotes.race: La Celia Wines Sprint Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Jakajaro was a horse I thought would win a maiden. This is a good horse. He was still green today and hopefully he will go on. He's in the big sales race here in September and that will be in his target - David Marnane, trainer

runners.spotlight: He's got back on track in a major way in 5f handicaps this spring, winning at Newmarket then impressively making all in a big field at York last week (both on good ground; effective on soft early in career); back up in grade this afternoon but this thriving 5yo could be capable of another bold bid.

stable_tour.quote: His win at York last week was really good. He won decisively and certainly merits going up in class now, as he did that very well. He's entered in the King Charles III but will probably go next to the Temple Stakes on Saturday as long as the ground is good or softer. We'll see about Royal Ascot after that. He's moving in the right direction, which is really positive. The race he won at York was won last year by American Affair, who went on to win the King Charles III. There will be options but I think he is slightly more ground-dependent, in that it's got to be good or slower for him. It's 11 years since we won the King Charles III (or the King's Stand as it was then), and it would be great to win it again if we could. 20-05-26

runners.breeder: P Taplin & Mike Channon Bloodstock Ltd
runners.comment: Others have better form but he was unlucky when Listed third at Naas on reappearance
runners.name: Getreadytorumble

quotes.race: Weatherbys Racing Bank Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Getreadytorumble has a lot of boot and is from a very fast family. He had a few issues at two but has come to hand nicely. The ground was a bit too quick for him, but he had a bit too much class for the others. I'm hoping it will be onwards and upwards when we go into handicaps - Jack Channon, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 4yo who made his debut last May and progressed very nicely, his campaign culminating in Listed third at Ascot (5f, soft) in October; returned with Listed third at Naas (5f, good) where he might have won with a clear run; others have better form but he's unexposed and could have more to offer.

runners.comment: Group 2 winner last August and he could improve for his comeback fourth at Newmarket
runners.name: Jm Jungle
runners.owner: MPS Racing Ltd & The Ayrshire Tradesmen

quotes.race: King George Qatar Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Sometimes certain races in the sprint division can be winnable and this looked one. When the rain came yesterday it looked like it might inconvenience some, whereas JM Jungle always turns up. If you don't put your hat in the ring, you've no chance, so we said we'd give it a go. He's much stronger this year and looked so calm before the race that I knew he was going to run his race again. They went lickety-split and Jm Jungle loves that. Earlier in the season Jason Hart said the race he'd love to ride him in was the Nunthorpe, simply because of how fast they go and how much he likes York. It looks the natural next step because he's a Group 2 winner now and you want to be going up from there. We put him in the Abbaye earlier this week and that's a similar race. If you get a good draw up against the rail, with his speed he'd be in the van early doors - Sean Quinn, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Aston Martin "Dash" Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: JM Jungle deserved that and he's won a load of consistent races and the handicapper has never missed him for being placed, so it's great he's got his day. I rode him in the three-year-old Dash here a couple of years ago and I got stuck behind a wall of horses and I was never able to get into a rhythm that day. He never handled the track that day but today I was out on a wing and able to keep momentum rolling forward and I think that has helped - Jason Hart, jockey.

quotes.race: Symphony Group Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: When the draw came out and the ground was dry we were delighted. This was the plan all along, but Jm Jungle will roll away in all the big five-furlong handicap sprints for the rest of the year - John Quinn, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: World Pool Handicap
quotes.quote: JM Jungle is in very good form, and up to Haydock he had been running really well and just got touched off at York and Hamilton. Then he won nicely at Haydock. He's got a lot of speed from the gate, so we felt that this track would suit him - John Quinn, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: JM Jungle has been running consistently and I thought he was unlucky to bump into a well-handicapped horse last time. He went to bite the second horse and I had to drag him back off, but he's done it well in the end - Jason Hart, jockey.

runners.spotlight: 6yo who rose through the ranks last season and won the Group 2 King George Stakes at Goodwood (5f, good to soft) in August; reappeared with respectable fourth of 14 to Night Raider in the Palace House at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago and he could show the benefit of that outing today.

stable_tour.quote: He's another who did well in Bahrain and he arrived back in such good form that we decided to keep going for now, so he'll either head for the Scottish Sprint Cup at Musselburgh or a valuable race at Bath a week later. He gave Jason [Hart] a good feel on his last run in Bahrain and he could still be improving. He's an out-and-out 5f horse. 20-03-24

runners.comment: 5f Group 1 winner at Royal Ascot last June; well beaten ten days ago on sole outing since
runners.name: American Affair

quotes.race: King Charles III Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: I've trained the family for three generations so it's very sweet. American Affair's grandfather had his day here so we're pretty lucky that we can breed horses like that. He's just getting faster, we went seven furlongs at Wetherby in his maiden, we've learnt to run him over the right trip, we took him back to five and he's just getting better and better. I was quite confident he could do it today, he had the talent, we got it wrong at Haydock. I knew he was probably one of the fastest horses in the race but it's how you control that. We've come down a day early and got him relaxed and it all fell into place - Jim Goldie, trainer.I first won his maiden on him over seven furlongs round Wetherby, it's hard to believe. And then American Affair started getting sharper and sharper and I rode him one day at York over seven and he proper latched on and I said to Jim 'I think this lad could be a sprinter' and obviously he's just got quicker as he's got older as do a lot of sprinters - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

quotes.race: Lindum York Handicap
quotes.quote: It's probably American Affair's last go in a handicap. He's done nothing but improve and started off last year in the mid-70s, but the more racing he's had the sharper he's got. He just shuts down when he hits the front and is still quite raw. Jim said we'd learn a lot more about him today as there's no easy five-furlong race here. He's proved he's up to going to the next level - Paul Mulrennan, rider.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Scottish Sprint Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: We probably have to go into Group races. There's the King Charles over five furlongs at Ascot, which would be okay. I don't think we'll go to Newmarket but American Affair is a good horse and he's maturing - Jim Goldie, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Portland (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: American Affair has done nothing but improve all year. Jim Goldie is some trainer. The last couple of races he's been running with the choke out and not really finishing. Jim said today to ride him ice cold, I got him to switch off and he finished really well. What will he be like next year with another winter on his back? He's still very babyish and raw - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap
quotes.quote: American Affair is a homebred and as he came off the box, I said to him, 'Your granny [Class Wan] won here' and we've had a few generations of this breed. From where he was drawn [13], Paul got the rail and kind of bossed it - Jim Goldie, trainer, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: American Affair is a work in progress but the uphill finish and the step up to seven played to his strengths. He's a big horse and there should be a lot more to come from him - Paul Mulrennan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Highly progressive in 2025, winning the Group 1 King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm); also won on good to soft last year; it was his first run since when down the field at York recently and he may have needed it, but a dramatic transformation is required just ten days on.

stable_tour.quote: He's very talented. We hoped he would bounce back the way he did at Musselburgh and he'll improve for it. We're excited. He'll probably go to York for a 5f handicap next but I've put him in the Temple Stakes and the King Charles at Royal Ascot. We'll probably stick to 5f at the moment. I think he's up to that class over five and he's a simpler ride over that trip. He appears very fast and seems to be comfortable at that pace. 07-05-25

runners.comment: Placed in two Group 1s last season but has to leave heavy reappearance defeat well behind
runners.name: Frost At Dawn

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Frost At Dawn is a star. She's had plenty of seconds and now a third, but how can you complain? I'd just love to find that win at this level - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.race: Women In Racing/British EBF Cecil Frail Listed Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I think Frost At Dawn is better over five and we'll come back to that trip and might go and run in the King's Stand as the owner is very keen to go to Ascot. She ran a good race at Bath behind the winner when they beat the track record and then she probably veered off the line at Newmarket last time. The older she gets the faster she's getting as she's a bull of a horse. She likes that quick ground and since we've put the visor on her she's improved. She's a quick filly and the stiff five at Ascot would be right up her street. If it was fast ground there I think she could run a massive race. She'd be the fastest I've ever had - William Knight, trainer.

quotes.race: Nad Al Sheba Turf Sprint Sponsored By Emirates Skywards (Group 3) (Turf)
quotes.quote: I had the luck to have a good draw today, so I just played my card. It's the first time I've ridden Frost At Dawn. She's fast and I think she would travel even better over six furlongs - Mickael Barzalona, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Made all in Listed race here (6f, good to firm) last May and placed in two 5f Group 1s subsequently; in the mix on best form and she's a lot better than she showed at Newmarket on her return, but has to leave that heavy defeat well behind; cheekpieces go on; slight doubt about slow ground.

runners.comment: Three-time Listed winner but below par in France last time; may be vulnerable
runners.name: Beautiful Diamond

quotes.race: Arran Scottish Sprint EBF Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: The ground at Newmarket jarred Beautiful Diamond up very badly and we've had to take our time with her a little bit and start again. Every bit of the soft ground will have done her a world of good today. She's a classy filly - James Cowley, assistant to Karl Burke.

quotes.race: British EBF Stallions Harry Rosebery Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Beautiful Diamond deserved that and clearly didn't see the six out last time. She's all about speed, Clifford just let her roll along and it all came to her. I'm not sure if she'll run again this year, but she's probably done enough for the season and could go away now. She might get six furlongs next year on better ground but we'll probably stay over five. We'll definitely be looking at Group level now - Philip Robinson, owner's racing manager.

quotes.race: Queen Mary Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Beautiful Diamond is still a bit of a weak filly to be honest. She's had a hard race today and we'll give her a nice easy month and then take it on from there. She's a good filly for the future. Our other two ran blinders too - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Beautiful Diamond was a bit edgy when she came but we've not really pushed any buttons with her at home. I said whatever she did today she'll improve on, and we had to train her with the handbrake on leading into the race - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Three Listed wins, latest at Ayr (5.5f, soft) last September; returned with Listed third at Bath (5f, good) but well beaten in Longchamp Group 3 (5f, soft) since; fifth in this race in 2024; may again be vulnerable.

stable_tour.quote: She's done really well physically from three to four and will head to the Palace House at the Guineas meeting to start her season. She was on the tails of some good sprinters last year and I think she's got a chance of being bang there in those Group races. She looks all speed and beyond Newmarket we can look at races like the Temple. 11-04-25

runners.comment: Two-time Group 1 winner but this 10yo was below his best on sole run this year
runners.name: Khaadem

quotes.race: Longines Hong Kong Sprint (Group 1) (3yo+) (Course A) (Turf)
quotes.quote: The stirrup leather broke, I was without one iron and unfortunately the race was over - Oisin Murphy, jockey of Khaadem.

quotes.race: Prevagen Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint (Grade 1) (3yo+) (Turf)
