quotes.quote: By reading the form, I knew they were going to go hard, and I couldn't ask for any more. For a nine-year-old gelding against the best sprinters in the world, third is quite a good job. Khaadem thinks he's two, honestly. The winner was head and shoulders above everybody else. It's a shame I couldn't catch Ag Bullet, but third is good enough. Full credit to Charlie Hills. A nine-year-old gelding getting third in a Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint against the best sprinters in the world, amazing effort. The blinkers helped and we've done a lot of gate schooling and the race went really well. The winner was far too good but I'm just delighted with the run - Frankie Dettori, jockey.

quotes.race: Woodford Stakes presented by FanDuel (Grade 2) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Khaadem seems to thrive being here. He's nine years old and he won his first race as a two-year-old, so we go back a long way. He's won some fantastic races back in England - two Jubilees at Royal Ascot - and he's won some amazing prize-money, so he's given us all a lot of joy. Horses have such good characters and he's certainly got one. I think we have to go [Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint]. It just makes sense - Charlie Hills, trainer, speaking to Bloodhorse.Khaadem fluffed the start. That's why he was so far back. I got him in a good spot and he decided to run. He's a character and we love him for it - Frankie Dettori, jockey.

quotes.race: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: Khaadem got a fantastic ride there off the pace and he never looked like he was going to get beat; he travelled beautifully through the race. He loves the place and it's the first time he's had the ground, pretty much since he ran here last time. I think fast ground is key to him. He had a lovely pitch, they went a good strong pace in front, but he just travels so well. He's such a versatile horse; he was making the running over five furlongs two years ago. I just really felt there's a different trajectory to running like a good horse over six, and it seems to have suited him very well - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: I've always had massive faith in Khaadem and that's why I've kept him for so long. He won a Group 2 last year over five furlongs and this year I wanted to try to race him properly again and make sure he got the six well. The horse is very, very fast. He's got his quirks but most good sprinters do and he's just taken time to come to himself - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Coolmore Wootton Bassett Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1) (British Champions Series)
quotes.quote: We were pleased with that. It was a little bit loose over on the side Khaadem was but he's run a really good race.  We'll definitely look at the Flying Five - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: King George Qatar Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Khaadem has never really come back like his Stewards' Cup win until today. It's taken a while and he's a quirky horse, but very talented. He took everything in his stride and the race unfolded perfectly for him. I'm made up. He always wears his heart on his sleeve - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Palace House Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: We only bought Khaadem at the end of last year from Shadwell and we're over the moon. These are hard races to win but he's just seriously fast. He's a proven horse and the Hays like to have runners in Dubai, so it was an easy decision to make to buy him. You'd have to go to Ascot after that and take on the rockets there and you'd have to keep him over the same trip too - Alex Cole, owner's racing manager.

quotes.race: Unibet Stewards' Cup (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I guess we will have to look at the Group 1 at Haydock. Magical Memory won this race and just got touched off there. I think Khaadem is a very good horse who is only going to get better and better - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Shalaa Carnarvon Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Khaadem is hugely talented but has his quirks. He's just a bit hot-headed and has been hard to settle, hence the hood in the paddock before. I think Ascot and a stiff six will suit him. He might just prefer a little bit more give in the ground in time but he's an exciting horse - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Conditions Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Khaadem is a lovely horse - he's got size and scope. One of the reasons for bringing him here was we wanted to go softly with him, try to give him more experience until we move him up to the bigger races. He's in the Middle Park and Sheikh Hamdan will probably decide where he wants to go, but there's a good possibility he'll go there - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Randox Health EBF Novice Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Khaadem got struck into when he ran here last time and has grown up a lot since then - Dane O'Neill, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Won the 6f Group 1 at Royal Ascot in 2023 and 2024 and added 5.5f Grade 2 win at Keeneland last October; however, this 10yo wasn't at his best at Meydan in March on his sole run this year, and the drop back to 5f and the forecast slow ground are likely negatives.

stable_tour.quote: He needed his return at York and was drawn on the wrong side. He looks a picture of health and seems in just as good a form going there as he did last year when he won the same race. He enjoys being ridden a bit differently from time to time and came from the back last year but he's undoubtedly a fast horse, who has won a King George over five furlongs at Goodwood in the past. 13-06-24

He wintered in Dubai and I was delighted with his first run back here when third in the Listed Cathedral Stakes at Salisbury late last month. We rode him a little differently there as he was held up to come with a late run, which I think suited him. He has an entry in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes on Saturday, and I'm currently wanting to give it a go. Glorious Goodwood will again be on our radar as he has a real liking for the course having won the Stewards' Cup and King George. 21-06-23

runners.comment: 2yo Listed winner last June and in good heart this spring, but she would be a shock winner
runners.name: Argentine Tango

quotes.race: HKJC World Pool Molecomb Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Argentine Tango just keeps finding a bit more every time we run her. She's had plenty of runs so she looks more exposed than the rest but she keeps finding a bit more improvement. I thought the five [furlongs] here might catch her out but she's that tough she just dug in again at the finish to get up for second - David Allan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Empress Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I couldn't believe Argentine Tango was 9-1 as she was second to Karl Burke's Royal Ascot winner Venetian Sun at Carlisle the time before last giving her 6lb. Somehow she was rated only 84 and Venetian Sun is now 20lb higher. I would say that Tim, as a Yorkshireman, would want to have a crack at the Lowther at York instead [of the Empress Fillies' Stakes]- Terry Holdcroft, owner-breeder.

quotes.race: Hilary Needler Trophy EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was brilliant. Argentine Tango is really tough and genuine, she tries like hell.  We don't know about Ascot. It depends what the ground is like, if it was sparking fast ground we probably wouldn't go - Tim Easterby, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Club Day EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Argentine Tango is as hard as nails and was very hard to break in. But she's tough and she'll improve masses. When the other horse came to her she went again. We might take her to York for the Marygate Stakes - Tim Easterby, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 2yo Listed winner at Newmarket last June and has run well when fourth in Group 3/Listed races on her two starts this spring, but she would be a shock winner today.

runners.comment: Group 3 winner at Newbury last September and she may have needed comeback run at Newmarket
runners.name: First Instinct

quotes.race: Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: First Instinct has had a couple of starts this year where she's probably not been the quickest out and I was conscious that she'd have to be here. I gave her a kick out of the gate and within three strides she was rocking, and she actually took me by surprise. She's tough, she's fast, and she appreciated that tiny bit of give in the ground - Tom Marquand, rider.

quotes.race: Goffs Irish EBF Polonia Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: Mr Haggas was bullish with First Instinct and thought she had a good chance. She jumped so fast coming out of the gates that I nearly came off, but she got into her stride really quick. Billie (Lee, on Town And Country) was coming quick, but I was pulling out more. I'd be happy at today's distance - Chris Hayes, jockey.

quotes.race: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: First Instinct has been faultless. I was a bit worried that the ground today might just blunt her speed but she fell asleep early - which was key I think - and showed that trademark turn of foot which she showed on her first run. I think she'll be even more effective on better ground - Tom Marquand, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Close third in the Group 2 Sandy Lane on this card 12 months ago (6f, good) and she won a Group 3 at Newbury (5f, good to soft) last September; drawn badly when down the field in the Abbaye at Longchamp last October and she may have needed her comeback run at Newmarket; she's not discounted.

16:05.race_name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.comment: Back-to-form third with first visor at Newmarket (1m6f) three weeks ago; stamina unproven
runners.name: Pole Star
runners.owner: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: The first two home ran against each other at Doncaster and it wasn't total shock because Pole Star is a big raw horse and he'd won here before. I thought he was beat on the turn but once he got into a battle I thought he was in with a shout because he's that type of horse. Subjectivist was second in this race and we've won it a few times, and in the future we'll take the same line as the horses who ran in it before - Jock Bennett, trainer's assistant.

runners.spotlight: Won two 1m6f handicaps last term, one in a valuable race here; back-to-form third with a first-time visor at Newmarket (1m6f) three weeks ago, so re-enters calculations despite earlier lesser efforts over 2m2f and 2m.

stable_tour.quote: I thought he ran like he was a little bit rusty on his comeback. He's got entries in a one-mile-six-furlong handicap at the Guineas meeting and the Chester Cup, but William Buick suggested coming back in trip, so Newmarket is the most likely of his options. I'm sure he'll come on for Friday's run and it wouldn't surprise me to see him land a big one this season. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Making his presence felt again; player on good or good to soft, but unproven on soft
runners.name: Prydwen

quotes.race: Liz And Izzy's Hoap Podcast Handicap
quotes.quote: That was great, I was delighted with Prydwen. Callum gave him a lovely, confident ride. It was an unbelievable effort carrying that weight. He obviously loves the AW so the Northumberland Plate looks a legitimate next step. He'll be weighted out of something like the Copper Horse at Ascot, but we might try the Goodwood Cup, he's moving into that sort of realm now - George Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: BetUK All-Weather Championships Marathon Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a really good performance. Prydwen has been a light-framed horse so we've given him a bit of time and he's filled into his frame. He's a bit older and wiser and that performance opens a few doors, I think he deserves a go at Royal Ascot in something like the Copper Horse Handicap - George Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: Cazoo Search Drive Smile Handicap
quotes.quote: Prydwen has been a nervous horse in the past and has been slow to come to hand. They didn't go too hard up front which enabled Marco to get a smooth run into it - George Scott, trainer.

runners.spotlight: What a fantastic horse he's been, hitting his peak in 2024 but coming down the weights in handicaps and already making his presence felt over 2m and 1m4f this season; his fifth in Germany 13 days ago was in a Group 2, so another good run; effective at this track and remains in serious calculations on good or good to soft, but unproven on soft.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a career best on his last start when narrowly second, which is quite a good effort considering he's a six-year-old. He's been pretty consistent considering how much he's run and he might go for a break now, have one run before Royal Ascot, and he'll go for the Copper Horse Handicap. He deserves a chance to run at a meeting like that and going back in trip there would suit him. 29-03-24

runners.comment: 1-14 on turf; second of six in this last year but a supporting role again seems likely
runners.name: Humble Spark
runners.spotlight: Held up; 6yo who is 6-27 on AW surfaces but 1-14 on turf; minor honours back on turf for last four outings and he was second of six in this race last year, but a supporting role again seems likely.

stable_tour.quote: What a year he's had. He was coming in the Stayers' Handicap on his last run but we were hoping to get into the 1m2f race as that's his trip, but you'd say he was a player at the 2m race. His ability to switch off is impressive, especially on the all-weather. We're hoping to get him into the Northumberland Plate, so we'll probably go back to Newcastle on Saturday. He'll probably have to go up to get into it, and if not we'll get in the Vase on the same day. He's another with stall issues but we're getting around them. He's not showing signs of diminishing. He's interesting, he's not straightforward but I don't think good horses are. We've had a lot of fun with him. He's got a good pedigree and he's getting there. 07-05-25

runners.comment: Two soft-ground wins (1m4f/2m) in France; bold show at York (1m4f) on recent British debut
runners.name: Hermetic
runners.spotlight: Dual soft-ground winner (1m4f/2m) in France last autumn, from just four races there; picked up for 105,000euros in November and put up a bold show when fourth of 17 at York (1m4f, good) ten days ago; stuck to his task at 20-1 that day and looks a strong candidate if that run has brought him on.

runners.comment: Respectable second last time; peak efforts on softer than good, so she needs a close look
runners.name: Blazeon Five

quotes.race: Colliers Business Rates Experts Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Blazeon Five has been crying out for this ground and the handicapper gave her a chance by dropping her a few pounds, so it was well executed - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

quotes.race: John Guest Racing Brown Jack Handicap
quotes.quote: Blazeon Five had a little bronc. I thought she was quite tired pulling up, but perhaps she could have gone around again. She had a little buck and dropped the shoulder on me, it's something you expect on a Monday morning but not here. It was a weird race pace-wise, essentially we had a target to run at entering the straight and he dropped away. Temporize took me to a point where I felt like I was going okay, but when he dropped away I was left in front with a bit to run and I had to commit. I think she was just waiting for him - Jack Mitchell, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Ended last year in storming form for 1m6f/2m hat-trick and came a respectable second at Newbury (2m, good) five weeks ago after a three-month break; peak efforts on softer than good, so she needs a close look.

runners.comment: Left R Beckett 90,000gns October; just a maiden win but staying trips are worth exploring
runners.name: Venezuelan
runners.owner: P and Mrs G A Clarke
runners.spotlight: Small-field Lingfield maiden last August was his only win but he was on the premises in nearly all his handicaps; tried various headgear on last five starts and switches it again on this first run since leaving Ralph Beckett for 90,000gns in October; unraced beyond 1m4f or on softer than good, but staying trips are worth exploring and he has a competitive mark.

stable_tour.quote: Quite a highly rated horse off the Flat from Ralph Beckett, he was bought as a dual-purpose by Alan O'Keeffe for owner Peter Clarke before he came here. He's schooled well and is a nice horse for jumping - I'm very fortunate to have acquired him. He'll probably start off on the Flat, probably at Chester, and then we'll introduce him to a little maiden hurdle somewhere. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Stepping back up from 1m6f should suit but this race may also prove too tough
runners.name: Almuhit

prev_owners.owner: J Carthy & Paul Byrne & Patrick John OBrien

quotes.race: Back The Super Boost At BetVictor Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Almuhit has improved so much and, although the wind op made a difference, switching from hurdles back to the Flat seems to have freshened him up - Faye Bramley, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Rediscovered the knack for new stable last year, including two front-running wins over 2m in four-runner Flat races and two places when the action got more competitive; returned to some hurdles form on last two outings in that sphere; a lesser show on Musselburgh Flat in between was over 1m6f but this race may also prove too tough.

runners.breeder: S A S U Ecurie Des Monceaux Et Al
runners.comment: Well handicapped were he to return at his best after 588 days off; market may guide
runners.name: Premiere Ligne
runners.spotlight: Finally off the mark in Britain in May 2024 and runner-up on next four starts, including when coming from well back over 2m4f at Glorious Goodwood; however, he flopped when just 9-1 for the Cesarewitch (soft) that October and not seen since; that was his only run in Britain on softer than good; well handicapped were he to return at his best after 588 days off; market may guide.

stable_tour.quote: He won for us at Lingfield last May and then ran up four consecutive seconds in staying handicaps, including in the Goodwood Handicap over 2m4f, and when only just beaten in the Cesarewitch Trial. He was well beaten in the Cesarewitch on his final start of the season and is out at the moment, but will be back later this year. 29-05-25

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khans Studs S C
runners.comment: Had a disappointing 2025 and a mixed hurdles campaign; all wins have been on soft or heavy
runners.name: Tashkhan

quotes.race: Paxtons Now Stocking Stihl Equipment Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a good learning experience for Tashkhan. Brian gave him a great ride and he jumped well while being a bit excited. He travelled nicely and it's good for him to win and get it out of the way. He just never had his ground last year. He needs it heavy, so we thought we'd try him jumping. He's had issues with his joints before but this year he's been grand, so it was the time to do it. He's done a fair bit of schooling and he's always done it well, he'll come on a lot for that. - Brian Ellison, trainer

quotes.race: Prix Royal-Oak (Group 1) (3yo+) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Maybe if Tashkhan hadn't run in the Cesarewitch he could have been second. He's had all the travelling on top of Newmarket, where he had a hard race, but he's still run his heart out. We went to Chester because of ground, and we went to Newmarket because it went soft. We're governed by the ground and that's why he came here. But saying that, he's picked up over a hundred grand in three races so he hasn't done badly for a horse who cost very little money - Brian Ellison, trainer.

quotes.race: Club Godolphin Cesarewitch Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: Tashkhan has run a massive race under top weight and that 4lb penalty he picked up for winning at Chester has just made the difference. We've kept him off fast ground and he's gone down fighting on a surface he loved - 'Brian Ellison, trainer.

quotes.race: Watergate Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Tashkhan is a star. The rain came and that's all he wanted, fast ground is no good to him. That just shows you how good he is. I know he hasn't won for two years but he's had some hard races. There are three races he could go for. He's in the Cesarewitch, the Long Distance Cup on Champions day and the Royal-Oak and he'll go wherever the ground is right - Brian Ellison, trainer.

quotes.race: Qatar Prix du Cadran (Group 1) (4yo+) (New & Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Ben (Robinson) just said that having run four times on fast ground, Tashkan didn't know whether he was just thinking about that (early on). He said once he got his confidence he raced a bit better. But the winner's a machine isn't he? Just a different ballgame. This is just a cheap horse and he never lets me down. We might go to Ascot and if not we'll come back here for the Royal-Oak, I think that will be more likely - Brian Ellison, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: Tashkhan is very exciting and there are lots of options now. The soft ground is key to him, he wants a bit of cut and it really makes a difference. He's entered in the John Smith's Cup but with his three-year-old weight-for-age allowance, he won't get in. There's the Melrose at York and he could run against the older horses. The two-mile races could be an option as he stayed well there-Patrick Boyle, owner

quotes.race: Follow Us On Twitter Handicap
quotes.quote: I would say getting gelded has made a big difference to Tashkan and he definitely has his mind more on the job. You could see that Ross was rowing away on him a long way out but he just kept galloping. Down the line I can see him making into a nice three-year-old hurdler - Emmet Mullins, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 2-2 here on the Flat, albeit in 2021; very smart on Flat at his best but he's not scored in this sphere since 2023 and had a disappointing 2025; had a mixed hurdles campaign last season, last seen 11 weeks ago; all wins have been on soft or heavy ground.

stable_tour.quote: He's in great form and we're just hoping for a bit of rain. He's run two good races this year, considering the ground hasn't been right for him. He loved the softer ground when he was second to Trueshan there last season and two and a half miles is tailor-made for him; all he does is stay. 08-06-22

He's in tremendous form and will probably start back next week in the Listed Further Flight Stakes at Nottingham, in which he finished third last year. He's been working great and looks a picture. He finished second in the Long Distance Cup at Ascot in 2021 and has suffered a bit since then. He had a few joint problems from running on fast ground, but they're all sorted now. He finished off last year in really good form, winning under a big weight at Chester and finishing third in the Cesarewitch, giving a stone to two very good horses [The Shunter and Pied Piper]. He was then third in the Group 1 Prix Royal-Oak but it just came too quick after the Cesarewitch. He's come back great. He'll have entries for the Chester Cup and the Ormonde and could go for the latter if the ground is on the softer side as there won't be many runners. We'll go ground hunting with him as he doesn't like fast ground - he has to have soft ground, he's a different horse altogether on it. He's likely to end up back in France at the end of the year. We'll pick out his races a bit more and the autumn is likely to be the best time for him. 03-04-24

runners.comment: Has not lived up to April 2025 win; hood/blinkers (other headgear has been tried) go on
runners.name: Yashin

quotes.race: Longines Sagaro Stakes (Group 3) (A Gold Cup Trial)
quotes.quote: Yashin is imposing and should be getting better with age, but Kate Harrington did say he doesn't jump!  He wasn't 100 per cent ready today and the Gold Cup needs to be considered. He's going to have to take on Kyprios, who has had the beating of him before, but after beating Coltrane today it's got to be an option. He'd have to go up another half mile but I don't see why he wouldn't get it. The Melbourne Cup could be on the agenda as well - Nick Bell, son and assistant to Michael.

quotes.race: Saval Beg Levmoss Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Yashin will have to go up a bit to get to the Melbourne Cup, but he stays well and he has to have good ground. He probably likes going left-handed too. He was hung wide and keen all the way there. Shane said he really had no right to pick up and win like he did. I know it was only a short head but he was always getting there - Jessica Harrington, trainer

quotes.race: Fund A New Home For Festina Lente Handicap
quotes.quote: Yashin was good. We went from 1m to 1m4f and it probably looked a bit stupid but we knew after the last day that he really needed to go a distance There was no maiden coming up for him so when this three-year-old only handicap came up we thought this was where he should be, because we thought he was probably quite nicely handicapped - Jessica Harrington, trainer

runners.spotlight: Started 2025 with a bang when winning a slowly run, four-runner Group 3 at Ascot (2m, good to firm) in April; remote with ambitious targets on next three starts, followed by an upturn (sixth of 11) in 2m handicap at Chester in September but well beaten on Newmarket reappearance (1m6f) three weeks ago; hood and blinkers (he has tried other headgear) are now given a go.

stable_tour.quote: He won the Saval Beg at Leopardstown last season and ran very well when seventh in the Ebor. The Ebor will probably be his main aim again but we won't run him unless the ground is quick. 24-04-24

He'll be going for the Ascot Gold Cup. He might not appear in the Racing Post entries yet as it's a bit of an anomaly - he was entered by Ascot racecourse as a free entry after he won the Sagaro Stakes and for some reason there was a bit of a glitch being transferred over. It's a lovely race to be involved in. We gave him a minor wind op and, while we haven't done anything different with him, I just think he's matured and grown. He had a small back issue last year but that hasn't bothered him and he seems to be moving really well. He fully deserves to line up in the Gold Cup. Obviously a few like Kyprios have fallen by the wayside but I think Aidan O'Brien still holds the aces with Illinois, who'll be a very tough nut to crack. But if ours is there turning for home we'll give him a good shout. 09-06-25

runners.comment: Ex-French; well-beaten last of seven at Hamilton (1m3f, good; 14-1) eight days ago
runners.name: Ouro Preto
runners.spotlight: 3-15 when trained in France, the latest win in a claimer at Longchamp (1m4f, very soft) last September; well handicapped judged on peak French efforts but he was a well-beaten last of seven on British debut at Hamilton (1m3f, good; 14-1) eight days ago.

runners.comment: Tailed off on his favoured soft ground in August last time; left Ian Williams; clear risks
runners.name: Zinc White

prev_owners.owner: S Beetham And DPL Fab Ltd

quotes.race: tote Fantasy, Whos In Your Stable Chester Plate Handicap (For The Bobby Mcalpine Memorial Cup)
quotes.quote: Zinc White is fragile, so what we do with him next I don't know and as long as he comes out of his race then we'll have a lot of fun with him - Ian Williams, trainer.

runners.spotlight: All three wins have been on soft going, the most recent in impressive style in the Chester Plate (2m2f, soft) in May 2023 off 1lb higher than today; absent 678 days before an encouraging run last June, followed by two backward steps and he was tailed off on his favoured soft ground in August last time; has left Ian Williams and comes with clear risks.

stable_tour.quote: A nice horse in his younger days, he has found his way here. He won on the Flat for his previous trainer Ian Williams in the Chester Cup consolation race three years ago. We've been very pleased with him and he's another one for Chester. He should be well handicapped now. 08-04-26

16:40.race_name: William Hill Price Boosts Every Day Handicap

runners.breeder: Lynch Bages Camas Park & Summerhill B/S
runners.comment: Comfortably won recent Bath maiden; could be on a handy mark if things have now clicked
runners.name: Noble Vow

quotes.race: Best Cleaning Group Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hopefully now Noble Vow has worked out to do it he can get a bit of a sequence going - Richard Hannon, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Can be headstrong but comfortably got off the mark at the seventh attempt in a recent maiden at Bath (5.7f, firm); ran well on good to soft last year (unraced on softer); could be on a handy mark if things have now clicked.

runners.comment: Well-bred filly who might appreciate drop to 5f on handicap debut; could have part to play
runners.name: Bintaryana
runners.spotlight: Improved upon sole 2yo run to win at Nottingham (6f, good) last month, and runner-up in Southwell novice (6f, AW) since; she could do with settling better but this well-bred filly might appreciate the drop to 5f on handicap debut, and may well have a part to play.

runners.comment: 5f AW novice winner; open to further improvement and not ruled out on turf/handicap debut
runners.name: Burdett Estate
runners.spotlight: All three starts over 5f on AW; won at Wolverhampton in December on second outing and not beaten far when third of three in novice there in March; open to further improvement and not ruled out on turf/handicap debut.

runners.comment: Step back in right direction when fifth of 17 in a higher grade at York last Friday
runners.name: Hanney Girl
runners.spotlight: Two wins from her 11 starts, both last summer; took a step back in the right direction with 2l fifth of 17 at York (5f, good) last Friday and she's back down in grade today; also effective on soft ground; one to consider.

runners.comment: Disappointing in sole nursery but could settle better in first-time hood on reappearance
runners.name: Sands Of Josepi
runners.spotlight: Made all at Southwell (5f, AW) last November on third start then disappointing on nursery debut at Newcastle (5f, AW); however, he could settle better in a first-time hood on this reappearance and is not ruled out.

runners.comment: Won at Thirsk (5f, good) last May on his second start but failed to progress subsequently
runners.name: Under The Radar

quotes.race: Ladbrokes 'Gaffer Of All Accas' Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (GBB/IRE Incentive) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Under The Radar is a nice horse, he has a wonderful temperament. He was dossing in front, he's really lazy and laid back. He's in the Super Sprint and he might go there eventually - Tim Easterby, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Won at Thirsk (5f, good) last May on his second start but failed to progress subsequently; he needs to raise his game on this reappearance and first outing since being gelded.

runners.comment: Made all on h'cap debut at Newcastle (5f, AW) in January but two lesser runs have followed
runners.name: Justmyluck

quotes.race: Read Meg Nicholls' Blog At betmgm.co.uk Handicap
quotes.quote: Justmyluck has got a lot of speed. He ran a good race here the last day over six [furlongs] but he's been growing and getting stronger. He's been training well and he's only run five times so there should be plenty more to come - Paul Mulrennan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Made all on handicap debut at Newcastle (5f, AW) in January but two lesser runs have followed (5f/6f, AW) and a return to form is needed.

runners.comment: Won on final 2yo start and not much went right on reappearance; she's not written off
runners.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners.spotlight: Built upon previous promise to win four-runner novice at Musselburgh (5f, soft) last October for Kevin Philippart De Foy; well beaten on recent stable/seasonal debut at Beverley but unseated rider on the way to post, had a bad draw and failed to settle; she's not written off.

runners.comment: Underwhelming in December but gelded since and has a competitive mark if back on song
runners.name: Akirra
runners.spotlight: 5f AW winner last November having shown promise on turf previously (unproven on slow ground); underwhelming back in a handicap at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in December but gelded since and has a competitive mark if back on song.

17:15.race_name: William Hill Each Way Extra Handicap

runners.comment: Completed hat-trick over C&D last October and could build on reappearance 7f in Lincoln
runners.name: Eternal Force

quotes.race: Live Racing Streaming At CopyBet Handicap
quotes.quote: Eternal Force is improving but he's still learning. He was less green than he was last time but he's a baby. He's a nice horse who's definitely going the right way and will stay in training. He'll go up a few more pounds for that and could be one for the Lincoln - Maureen Haggas, wife of William Haggas, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Made it 3-3 since being gelded when winning by 3l over C&D (good to soft) last October; reappeared with respectable seventh of 21 in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and this lightly raced 4yo could build on that latest effort today; firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: Appealing handicap form last September and could take step forward from April reappearance
runners.name: Stem

quotes.race: Etcetera Construction 40th Anniversary EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: We were hoping to get Stem on the track quite quickly from the breeze up but Richard Hannon kept saying he needed more time and we've been as patient as we can. We went down there last week and he surprised everyone with how well he worked. After that we were hoping he'd run well today. Ryan said he'd get a mile plus eventually and that was great - Johnny de la Hey, owner.

runners.spotlight: Second on handicap debut at Ascot last September (1m2f, soft; no match for handicap blot) before close second of 15 at Newbury (1m, good to soft) a fortnight later, behind Eternal Force who was on the middle leg of a hat-trick; not beaten far when ninth of 24 in the Spring Cup at Newbury (1m, good) on his reappearance and this unexposed 4yo could take a step forward today.

stable_tour.quote: He's one of the most gorgeous horses you'll see; he's massive. I thought he'd get a mile and a half, but it appears he doesn't. He's the type who'll keep improving at four and I was pleased with him in the Spring Cup, although he got caught a bit flat-footed over the mile with the ground as quick as it was. On soft ground he has a real turn of foot, and he'll come on for the run. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Soft-ground winner last June and returned to form with a near-miss at Thirsk last Saturday
runners.name: Hot Cash
runners.spotlight: Left his reappearance run well behind when beaten just a head at Thirsk (1m, good) last Saturday; back up 2lb, he has the same mark as when winning at Carlisle (1m, soft) last June; respected.

stable_tour.quote: I'm delighted with him and we've taken a very speculative punt and stuck him in the Derby. He had only two runs last year, ­winning his maiden at Epsom and then finishing fourth in a Group 3 at Deauville in August. He went for another novice at ­Wolverhampton last week because he wasn't qualified for a handicap mark and was third. We might look at a Derby trial for him. If he cuts it at that level then brilliant, but if not we'll take stock and ­rebuild him, but we're very ­excited about him and he's been training really well. 02-04-25

runners.comment: Step back in right direction when fifth at Chester but needs to build on that effort today
runners.name: God Of War
runners.spotlight: Won off 2lb higher at Sandown (7f, soft) last August and he took a step back in the right direction with close fifth of 13 at Chester (7.5f, good) this month; however, he needs to build on that latest effort today.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a cracker at Chester last week, just getting touched off by El Burhan, and seemed to handle the track well. He's been doing a lot of his training with Harvard Sound as they're similar types. He's in good form. 14-05-25

runners.comment: Progressive towards the end of last season and could improve for last month's comeback run
runners.name: Maeva
runners.spotlight: 2-2 in handicaps last year (1m, AW/soft) before creditable Listed sixth in France (1m, heavy); not at the top of her game in Wolverhampton handicap (8.6f, AW) on reappearance but could improve for that run; not discounted.

runners.comment: Down to an attractive mark and slow ground would very much aid his cause
runners.name: Rhoscolyn

prev_owners.owner: Julie Martin & David R Martin & Partner

quotes.race: Coral Golden Mile (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I imagine they might not have bothered running the first day if they'd realised it was going to be so wet yesterday, but it didn't do Rhoscolyn any harm. He's a real old Goodwood specialist and this is probably the biggest race he could win down here. It's nice to see he's won it for the Horse Watchers. I think there's another handicap here for him at the end of August worth 100,000GBP over seven furlongs, so he'll probably come back for that - David O'Meara, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap
quotes.quote: Rhoscolyn lost his mojo a bit, but he likes Goodwood and likes that ground - Dominic McFadden, part-owner.

quotes.race: World Pool Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought it went perfectly. We'd had a bit of a look at the race earlier and thought that you would want him a little bit handier round here normally, but there looked to be a good bit of pace on. I think it's really important that Rhoscolyn gets a well-run race and he got one today. David has always been adamant that you get him in a good rhythm and more often than not, that is sitting a little bit further back, because he is a bit too keen and strong in his races. But today, he has relaxed. He jumped better than he did at Beverley when the blindfold came off a bit late, but he's a lot better if the blindfold is off before the last horse goes in. And that was my fault for not reminding the jockey last time out, to be honest. It went to plan today and I couldn't be happier - Chris Dixon, of The Horse Watchers.

quotes.race: Bet At racingtv.com EBF Novice Stakes
quotes.quote: Rhoscolyn is very smart to do that from stall ten. He's got a good temperament, he's laid back and you would imagine there would be more to come from him next year - Paul Mulrennan, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Down the field in the Thirsk Hunt Cup (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago but promising reappearance there (7f, good) previously; won the Golden Mile at Goodwood (1m, soft) last August when 3lb higher and slow ground would very much aid his cause.

stable_tour.quote: He bounced back last year, having paid the price for a good first year with us. Soft ground and seven furlongs brings out the best in him, particularly at Goodwood. He won three races from August onwards, so again he'll be starting this year with his mark right up there. He'll start back in a conditions race at Thirsk on Saturday. 19-04-24

He's been a flagbearer for us over the last three years. We bought him for a cutdown 23,000gns during Covid and he's been a revelation. He's won big races at Epsom twice, has a great record at Goodwood and has been placed at Royal Ascot. He's a top-end handicapper. Nowadays, soft ground is imperative to him having a good chance. He hasn't been running so well on ground that's been too quick for him, but he's shown time and again he can come back and win another race. He goes to Goodwood on Wednesday, provided the ground is on the soft side. He won the race last year and he's still got all his ability. 26-09-24

runners.comment: Encouraging fourth at Chester on stable debut but yet to run well on turf away from there
runners.name: Miami Matrix
runners.spotlight: Two wins at Chester last summer for Hugo Palmer (7.5f, soft/good) and ran well when fourth of 13 there (7f, good) on his recent stable and seasonal debut; lightly raced but he's yet to run well on turf away from Chester.

runners.comment: Winless since 2023 but on a reduced mark and his reappearance wasn't devoid of promise
runners.name: Ancient Rome

prev_owners.owner: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg

quotes.race: Mint Millions Stakes (Grade 3) (3yo+) (Turf)
quotes.quote: To be fair, Dr Hay picked this race out even before he purchased Ancient Rome. He's Kentucky-bred so it fitted in well. I think he went well on the [firm] ground today and he's pretty adaptable when it comes to surfaces. He ran in softer conditions a lot of the time in France and last time [at Goodwood] it was soft, but he's a War Front and they go on fast turf - Jamie Spencer, quoted by Bloodhorse.

quotes.race: Coral Chesterfield Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: They did go a good gallop, which was quite tiring in dead ground, and the race fell into his lap in the last furlong. I always thought I was going to be involved; maybe outside the three-furlong pole, he was moving up easily enough and I was following Tom Marquand [on Millebosc], who was kind of dying so we went round him. Ancient Rome is a very lazy horse - you ask him and he'll go for three or four strides, then he's lazy again. Even right at the line he pricked his ears and kind of jammed [the brakes] on, so he's a hard horse to assess. I just planned to drop out, stay on the outside, get cover and come down the outside. Dr Jim said, just ride like Richard Hughes! He's a smart horse and I thought he was a stakes horse, so I'm sure he will be capable of at least Listed company - Jamie Spencer, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Disappointing in the main last year but has dropped down the weights and he saw very little daylight when 17th of 24, beaten about 6l, in the Spring Cup at Newbury (1m, good) on his return; might not be a forlorn hope.

stable_tour.quote: He had an injury at the backend of last season and has had some time off. He's a big horse who takes a bit of getting ready but he's undoubtedly talented. He's not a certain starter in the Wolferton but if he does take his chance, I think he's well up to that class. 13-06-24

runners.comment: Second of 17 off this mark at Ascot last September but well beaten on both starts since
runners.name: Mr Swivell
runners.spotlight: Runner-up off this mark at Ascot (1m, soft) last September in a competitive handicap; however, well beaten in the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket later that month (pulled hard) and there was no return to form on his reappearance at Lingfield a fortnight ago.

runners.comment: Well handicapped on his close second here last July; could be in the mix on reappearance
runners.name: Bobby Bennu
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent during light campaign last season but he's 3lb lower than when a close second here (7f, good) last July, and he hinted when fifth of 20 at Ascot (7f, good to soft) in September that 1m might be a good fit; handicapped to be in the mix if at the top of his game on this reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: He's solid and consistent and there's a lovely seven-furlong Class 2 programme through the summer for him. He might stretch out to a mile around a bend but he'll start off over seven. The Victoria Cup might come a bit too soon but there are plenty of races for him and, while he's already rated 97, he's still relatively lightly raced. 11-04-25

runners.comment: Running well over 7f this spring and each-way claims if seeing out the trip
runners.name: Itsneverjustone
runners.owner: Ian OConnor & The Fox And Hounds

prev_owners.owner: Ian OConnor & The Fox And Hounds

quotes.race: Clayton Hotel Galway Handicap
quotes.quote: It is soft Flat ground and It'sneverjustone loved it. He is a fine, big, strong horse and won nicely. I hope he is in again during the week! I've had two rides for David and two winners. He is an up-and-coming young trainer, so it's good - Declan McDonogh, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Two wins last summer (7.3f/7f, soft/yielding) and he's run well in fourth on his two starts this spring (7f, good to soft/good); there's a slight question mark regarding today's return to 1m but he's an each-way contender if seeing out the trip.

stable_tour.quote: He's a half-brother to Aberama Gold and El Hombre, who have won 20-odd races between them. He looks a pretty smart colt who I think will progress through the ranks each season. 30-05-24

runners.breeder: Sun Bloodstock S A R L
runners.comment: Only seventh of 11 at Ascot latest but won on AW previously and he's effective over C&D
runners.name: Tilted Kilt
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent and only seventh of 11 at Ascot three weeks ago; however, prior to that he made a winning reappearance at Southwell (1m, AW) and he twice went close over this C&D last season; could bounce back.

runners.comment: Won here last July on second h'cap start and may have benefited from a gelding operation
runners.name: Padua
runners.owner: P C J Dalby & R D Schuster
runners.spotlight: Won here (7f, good) last July on second handicap start and 3l fourth of seven at Sandown (7f, good) in August; absent since but gelded in the interim and he could be the type to improve for it, having been headstrong in the past; brings potential to this 4yo campaign; unraced on slow ground.

stable_tour.quote: He nearly won first time out at Lingfield in November when sent off at 125-1, but then we ran him back a bit quickly afterwards. He ran a nice race on his seasonal return at Kempton in April behind Ernst Blofeld and we're now just waiting for the ground really. I've got rather too many three-year-olds rated in the high 70s who are still maidens - they've all been second and are very difficult to place in the current system. Ever since a novice system for three-year-olds came in it's been very difficult to place those who are in the 75-80 range. Normally you'd have won a maiden by then and been competitive in a handicap, but now they're novices you're taking on basically Group horses. If you come second or third that puts you up too high in the handicap and you're in the middle of nowhere. 29-05-25

runners.comment: Reduced mark appeals on form as recent as last June but he's failed to shine subsequently
runners.name: Star Anthem

quotes.race: Reduce Household Bills With The Eco Scheme EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Star Anthem ran super for the first time at Newbury and the form of that race has worked out really well and he took a nice step forward there. He was very at home on the track and the ground and we like the way he's progressing. He's a really strong, well-grown colt and I'm pleased we've managed to get two positive runs into him. We'll let him keep his strength now and hopefully he'll be good enough to go to Ascot. At the moment five furlongs is far enough, he hits the line well, so I'd be looking at the Windsor Castle or the Norfolk - Clive Cox, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo whose reduced mark appeals on form as recent as last June, but he was disappointing on his final two starts last season and (following wind/gelding operations) it was the same story on his recent return.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Bath last season and ran well when eighth in the Coventry Stakes, considering it was good to firm ground and he'd prefer it softer. He came back in the autumn and made the frame in a couple of Group races. He's strengthened up a lot since then and I'd hope he could be one to follow. 17-04-25

runners.comment: 1m French winner last August but soundly beaten on last month's stable debut at Newbury
runners.name: Nizam
runners.spotlight: Won at Deauville (1m, good to soft) last August and he may have needed the run on last month's stable/seasonal debut at Newbury (1m, good); however, he was soundly beaten at 80-1 and has to leave that performance well behind.

runners.comment: Won a shade cosily at York last week, taking record in turf handicaps to 3-3; respected
runners.name: Startled

quotes.race: Conundrum HR Consulting Handicap
quotes.quote: I wanted to get a bit of cover, but the horses from the outside took a while to get across. It ended up very messy when we got on to the main track. I wanted to give Startled a clean shot at it. It looked unlikely that we'd get a run, but he's done it nicely in the end - Saffie Osborne, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Overcame trouble to win a shade cosily under Saffie Osborne at York (7f, good) last week, taking his record in turf handicaps to 3-3 and record since upped to 7f to 2-2; may well show further progress and defy another rise in the weights; respected.

runners.comment: Chance of showing progress depends on the effects of two physical tweaks
runners.name: Catullus

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's a fine big animal. It's the first time I've sat on him. Catullus has a lot of scope, a lot of power. He's just kept stepping up, it was the perfect race to introduce to his win, to break his maiden in and he's done that in style. Hopefully, he can keep stepping up the ladder - Dougie Costello, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Unraced on ground softer than good; has consistent RPRs over 7f and looks reasonably solid in that respect; chance of showing progress depends on the effects of his physical tweaks (gelding/wind operations) since a disappointing effort over 6f at Meydan in February.

runners.breeder: Attlehill Ltd T/A Ridge Manor Stud
runners.comment: Unexposed colt who looks a possible danger, provided he stays this new trip
runners.name: Ironwill

quotes.race: Free Tips Daily On attheraces.com EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Ironwill battled hard, especially as he's a big horse, but Marco managed to get him to settle nicely. He's got the ability to improve a bit - Stuart Williams, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Unexposed colt whose sprinting form includes two wins last term and a respectable fifth at Newmarket (good) on reappearance; a possible danger with that outing under his belt, provided he stays this new trip.

runners.comment: Steadily progressive last term; ran well in the Horris Hill; enters calculations
runners.name: Wechaad
runners.spotlight: Ended his steadily progressive 2yo campaign by scoring readily at Doncaster (sole handicap attempt) then running well in the Horris Hill at Newbury, both over 7f (soft/good to soft); may well have more to offer this term and enters calculations on reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: He won well on his penultimate start at Doncaster, where he was able to get his toe in, before running well in the Horris Hill. I don't think he'll be ready to start back until May, when there are a few nice seven-furlong handicaps to consider, and that will point us to either something like the Jersey Stakes or perhaps the Britannia. He's a nice horse but needs to prove if he's very nice. 01-04-26

He won the nursery at Doncaster well. We've always liked him and it was a bit disappointing that it took four attempts to get him off the mark, but maybe he found the ground a bit too firm at Ascot and Newbury on his second and third starts. He seemed to enjoy getting his toe in last time. I think you'll see him being a pretty smart horse this autumn. He's down to run in the Group 3 Tattersalls Stakes at Newmarket on Thursday. He's also still in the Dewhurst because sometimes you just never know. He'll have to do something between now and then to prove himself for that top-class company, but maybe if we don't run him at Newmarket, he could be a Forest Hill Stakes horse in October. I think he's quite a smart individual and I was pleased to see him win the way he did at Doncaster. 24-09-25

runners.comment: Ran encouragingly at Pontefract on reappearance and has possibilities
runners.name: Reciprocated
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

quotes.race: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Reciprocated is turning out to be a really nice horse. We'll definitely look at stakes races now. He had a penalty and he did it really easily. He's got plenty of size and scope about him, he'll improve again for that run and the further he goes, the better he'll get - James Cowley, assistant to Karl Burke.

runners.spotlight: Gelded prior to finishing 2l third at Pontefract (6f, good; wore cheekpieces) on reappearance, posting best effort since starting his career with two wins; ideally needs to settle better back up in distance but otherwise has possibilities off the same mark.

runners.breeder: Lady Bamford & The Hon Alice Bamford
runners.comment: Still open to further progress; interesting despite conceding weight all round
runners.name: Pathein

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Winner Receives Free Entry To 2026 St Leger) (GBB/GBBPlus)
quotes.quote: Ed said he liked Pathein and to ride him to run well. He got away with the ground. He's still a bit on the weak side but he has a good attitude - Robert Havlin, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Thrice-raced colt who has useful 1m figures, most recently 2l third of four in conditions race at Goodwood (good); visual impression and pedigree both suggest this drop to 7f is worth exploring; still open to further progress and looks interesting despite conceding weight all round.

stable_tour.quote: He's one I like for later in the year. He's a good-bodied colt who has a nice pedigree on the dam's side and cost a few quid at the sales. He's from the first crop of St Mark's Basilica, who won four consecutive Group 1s in 2021 for Aidan O'Brien. 30-04-25

runners.comment: Form includes close second at last year's Glorious Goodwood; could go well
runners.name: Shaman Champion
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-6 since debut success but he has a notable piece of course form, namely close second in nursery at last year's Glorious Goodwood; could go well returned to this venue with Newbury reappearance (stable debut) under his belt.

stable_tour.quote: He's nice and won really well on his debut at Leicester. He should run a good race in thew Windsor Castle. 10-06-25

runners.comment: Ran well on reappearance but has something to prove back on turf
runners.name: Bone Marra
runners.spotlight: Ran well at Lingfield on seasonal debut, taking AW record to 112; however, far from certain to back up that effort, with his turf form much less convincing.

runners.comment: May rebound but balance of form suggests his mark may be difficult
runners.name: New Monarch
runners.spotlight: Eased once beaten upped to 1m on Good Friday when bidding for an AW double; consistent sort otherwise, including on turf last year, and may rebound; however, balance of form suggests he's no certainty to defy his mark on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Steadily progressive until below par last time; others are preferable
runners.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners.owner: Hambleton Racing Ltd XXXV & E Burke

prev_owners.owner: Hambleton Racing Xlviii & Mrs E Burke

quotes.race: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Royal Mile Handicap
quotes.quote: The race went exactly as I hoped it would, with a strong pace. Strength Of Spirit doesn't do a lot when he hits the front and I thought Sam might have got there a little bit too soon. We gelded him after his last run last year. He's a little bit of a monkey, he saves a bit for himself and I don't think he was overdoing himself when he hit the front there. We'll see what the handicapper does and he'll step up again - Karl Burke, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Three-time winner at 7f-1m and steadily progressive until a below-par effort at Chester (7.5f) most recently; may bounce back but this is no easy task off current mark in such a competitive affair.

runners.comment: Transferred her good AW progress to turf with a creditable effort at Chester
runners.name: Cool Molly
runners.spotlight: Has made excellent progress on AW this year and transferred that ability to turf with creditable third at Chester (7.5f, good) last time; needs additional improvement to add to her tally, however.

runners.comment: Needs to prove he can transfer the form of AW Listed success back to turf
runners.name: Hilitany

quotes.race: BetMGM Spring Cup Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Hilitany did well out in Dubai where Billy [Loughnane] had said to step him up the seven furlongs, but there wasn't a race for him. We brought him home and the intention was to give him a break but George said he was in such good form that we should run him in this race and it's paid off. There aren't any obvious races after this for him, so he could have a break and hopefully this sets him up for a productive summer - Chris Wall, Victorious Forever racing manager.

quotes.race: Oktoberfest Comes To Windsor EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hilitany did everything right. I loved his work last time, from the half-furlong pole to the line, and I got that same feel for a couple more furlongs today, which was really pleasing. It was a taking performance. He can get a little stressed in the prelims, which is why we ran him in a novice today to give him a bit more experience, but he's got some nice entries to look forward to now - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Absent and gelded since bagging Listed honours at Lingfield in February when upped to 7f and making AW debut; needs to prove he can transfer that improved form to handicap level and back to turf; otherwise unexposed over this distance and hard to dismiss.

stable_tour.quote: It didn't quite work out for him in Dubai, but then he was a pretty impressive winner of the Spring Cup at Lingfield. He looked like he'd get a little bit further and we'll probably need to step up in grade, potentially slightly further afield in Europe. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Creditable sixth to Startled at York but failed to show further progress
runners.name: Hasbro Market
runners.spotlight: Creditable sixth to Startled at York last week but finished out of the first two for the first time and failed to show further progress; that defeat suggests he's not the percentage call in another competitive field.

runners.comment: Seasonal debutant who gained his 2yo win when fresh and may do better still
runners.name: Siren Suit
runners.spotlight: Absent and gelded since finishing last in valuable event at Ascot on Champions Day; scored readily at Kempton (AW; sole 7f attempt) earlier in October when back from a layoff, and that performance bodes well for him being fresh; may do better still.

runners.comment: Disappointing back on turf last time; something to prove off his mark
runners.name: Richies Rocket
runners.spotlight: Far from disgraced in the Listed event won by Hilitany when bidding for a Lingfield AW double; disappointing at Newmarket, the scene of his promising debut, returned to turf last time (gelded since) and consequently has something to prove off his mark.

runners.comment: Returns to the scene of peak effort, namely fourth in the Vintage Stakes
runners.name: Goodwood Galaxy

quotes.race: Dragon Symbol Standing At Whitsbury Manor British EBF Blagrave Maiden Stakes (GBBRace)
quotes.quote: Goodwood Galaxy did everything right. We don't train to win first time out, so we never really go there with a massive expectation. But his work was good and his two working companions have won well in the past few days. He can be a bit opiniated at times, so the plan was to keep it simple. By keeping him happy he kept everyone else happy. He has his quirks and I was told his stallion [Kodi Bear] was the same. He wants to do things his way at times and instead of stopping him from doing them, you have to channel them into positive attitudes - David Menuisier, trainer.

runners.spotlight: A local runner in all respects and aptly registered his peak RPR in sole Goodwood attempt, namely fourth in last year's Vintage Stakes (7f, good); not exactly solid on his form since but the return to this venue may have a positive effect.

stable_tour.quote: He won really well on his debut at Salisbury and his Racing Post Rating of 92 was quite high for a debutant. Looking at previous winners of the Vintage, that rating is usually what horses ran to on their first or second start and he went for that race on Tuesday. Of course there's his name and owners [Goodwood Racehorse Owners Group] and he ran well to be fourth, beaten about two lengths. Nobody was under any illusions that it was a tough race, but it was well worth a go. 30-07-25

runners.comment: Ran creditably on reappearance but needs to do better still
runners.name: Aqua Bear
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish runner whose form for new yard comprises a success in AW maiden (subsequently gelded) and creditable fourth in Ascot handicap, both over 7f; needs to do better still in this field, however.

runners.comment: Prevailed in latest 6f start; bred to stay 7f and open to further improvement
runners.name: Rogue Messiah
runners.spotlight: Prevailed in Lingfield handicap (AW) in latest 6f start, adding to debut win (turf) and taking record to 2-4; bred to stay this extra furlong and may be capable of further improvement; one to consider.

14:00.race_name: British Stallion Studs EBF Cocked Hat Stakes (Listed Race) (Colts & Geldings)

runners.comment: Promising colt who is two from two, latest success in trial at Epsom; commands respect
runners.name: Saxon Street

quotes.race: Betfred Blue Riband Trial Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: This was a big jump coming here off a novice win last year, and Saxon Street is very much learning on the job, but when William asked him, he picked up nicely.  He should stay a mile a half without a problem. We'll have to decide whether we go straight there or stay at a mile and a quarter next time. There's a lot of water to go under the bridge between now and the Derby but that was a nice performance for his first run of the year  - Thady Gosden, joint-trainer.

runners.spotlight: The only Derby entry in this field; promising colt who is two from two and already a trial winner, having comfortably beat his rivals in the Blue Riband Trial at Epsom (1m2f, good; Listed) on seasonal debut; should take well to Goodwood and commands respect.

runners.comment: Rallying third in the Dee Stakes; open to additional improvement upped further in trip
runners.name: Golden Story

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: James [Doyle, jockey] said Golden Story was as green as grass going down, never mind coming back, and [was] in front a fair way [out]. It looked as though he was going to win twenty lengths and then when I looked around he was pulling himself up a hundred yards from the post, I think he just spotted a cameraman in the hedge. He's a lovely horse with a good temperament and it'll do him the world of good. He's at least a Listed horse next year - Karl Burke, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Twice-raced colt who is open to additional improvement upped further in trip; won at Doncaster (1m, soft) in the autumn then rallied for third place in the Dee Stakes at Chester (1m2f, good; Listed) on reappearance; one of the main contenders.

stable_tour.quote: A really exciting horse with a lot of ability. He'll be out from mid-April onwards and will hopefully show he's good enough to have a Derby trial in May, possibly the Dante. He's got a Derby entry, but being by Lope De Vega there's a question over the mile and a half trip. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Consistent; not disgraced in the Chester Vase; possibilities if taking well to cheekpieces
runners.name: Del Maro
runners.spotlight: Record is only 1-6 but he's consistent on bare figures and has two pieces of Group 3 form, last time fourth of five (not disgraced) in a Chester Vase won by the the colt who is now Derby favourite; possibilities, provided he takes well to first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Progress has stopped since Listed win and he still has something to prove beyond 1m
runners.name: Command The Stars
runners.owner: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
runners.spotlight: Did too much up front over 1m1f on penultimate start but never landed a blow when ridden with restraint in first-time hood (retained) over 7.5f latest; progress has stopped since French Listed win and he still has something to prove beyond 1m.

runners.comment: Far from solid on his form since heavy-ground win and this is a stiff task
runners.name: Oratorical
runners.spotlight: Progressive start to his career culminated in heavy-ground novice win at Nottingham; much less solid on his Listed/handicap form since and this step back up in class presents a stiff task at the weights.

14:35.race_name: Elston Consulting EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.comment: Close second of seven at Nottingham, running above market expectations; the form pick
runners.name: Knock Three Times
runners.spotlight: Ran above market expectations (22-1 shot) in 6f event on good ground at Nottingham, finishing half-length second of seven; the form pick, assuming that promise is confirmed.

runners.comment: Rallying third of 12, faring best of the newcomers, in 5f contest at Ascot
runners.name: Wondervision
runners.spotlight: Rallying third of 12, faring best of the newcomers despite seeming green, in 5f contest on good ground at Ascot; likely to be suited by this extra furlong and looks open to progress; possibilities.

runners.comment: 220,000gns yearling; Blue Point half-sister to Group 2 winner Chindit; interesting
runners.name: Coat Of Red
runners.spotlight: 220,000gns yearling; Blue Point half-sister to two winners, notably Chindit (7f/1m including 2yo/Group 2; RPR 119); dam well-related 7f AW scorer (67); yard's first 2yo runner of the season; has good credentials and market support would heighten interest.

runners.comment: 62,000gns yearling; by Dark Angel; stable has landed this race twice in last three years
runners.name: Dark Issue
runners.spotlight: 62,000gns yearling; by Dark Angel and first foal of French 9.5f/1m2f winner (RPR 96); stable has landed this race two times in the last three years; newcomer to consider.

runners.comment: 75,000gns yearling; yard's two individual 2yo runners this term include a winner
runners.name: Yumuri
runners.owner: Glentree Pastoral Pty Ltd And Partners
runners.spotlight: 75,000gns yearling; by Havana Grey and first foal of 5f/6f-winning (including 2yo; RPR 100) daughter of 5f 2yo scorer; suitably bred and her yard's two individual 2yo runners this term include a winner.

runners.comment: £85,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; by St Mark's Basilica; check the betting
runners.name: Vesper Honey
runners.spotlight: 55,000euros yearling, £85,000 (breeze-up) 2yo; St Mark's Basilica half-sister to two French winners, notably Tiger Touch (1m2f; RPR 79); dam 6f-1m scorer (including 2yo/Group 3; 113); check the betting.

runners.comment: 75,000gns yearling; by Havana Grey; stable's first 2yo runner of the season
runners.name: Virtue Charity
runners.spotlight: 75,000gns yearling; Havana Grey half-sister to winners Forever Penywern (1m2f AW/1m3f turf; RPR 87) and Waiting For You (French 1m1f 2yo); stable's first 2yo runner of the campaign; market informative.

runners.comment: The progeny of two winners for her connections; both parents took time to get off the mark
runners.name: Beautiful Effort
runners.spotlight: The progeny of two winners (sire 5f-7f, dam 8.6f AW) for her connections; both parents took a little time to get off the mark; may need this debut outing.

runners.comment: 30,000gns yearling; yard's record with 2yos thus far in 2026 doesn't augur well
runners.name: Forever Faithfull
runners.spotlight: 17,000gns foal, 30,000gns yearling; by Caturra and first foal of 7f winner (including 2yo/Spain; RPR 79); yard's record with 2yos thus far in 2026 doesn't augur well.

15:10.race_name: Fitzdares Height Of Fashion Stakes (Listed Race) (Fillies)

runners.comment: Stretched nicely clear at Newmarket to build on her 2yo effort; looks a smart prospect
runners.name: Earth Shot

quotes.race: Darley EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: I was delighted with Earth Shot. I was a bit concerned about the ground but she strode out well. The owners sponsor the mile and a quarter fillies' Listed at Newbury on the 17th of May and I suspect she'll go there. Tom [Marquand] was keen that she has another race relatively soon before we put a big target in front of her so we'll do Newbury if she's OK then decide whether to go to Epsom [Oaks] or Ascot [Ribblesdale] - William Haggas, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.It was an impressive performance. Earth Shot had that really nice introduction at Newbury behind one of our other exciting fillies [My Ophelia] and that performance was everything you'd want it to be. She took a while to work it out with the track being the track. She took a bit of a hop and a jump over some of the ridges early on but she worked it out late and, as ever with ours, William [Haggas] likes to leave a bit to be improved on into the season and I'm looking forward now to seeing what she really can do - Tom Marquand, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Twice-raced filly who is open to any amount of further progress and looks a Listed/Group performer in the making; eye-catching second at Newbury (1m, soft) in the autumn then went one better by stretching nicely clear to score by 5l at Newmarket (1m2f, good) on reappearance; respected.

runners.comment: Two from two this year, gaining those wins by an aggregate of nearly 20l; brings potential
runners.name: Brilliant Star

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I rode Brilliant Star's mother Star Catcher on her debut, and also rode her father Cracksman to win on his debut. She's a mile-and-a-half-filly all over and could be a Ribblesdale type, but I'm sure John and Thady [Gosden] will have a chat and decide her next target - Rab Havlin, jockey.

runners.spotlight: The progeny of Group 1 winners for her notable connections; has duly shown plenty of promise at novice level and is 2-2 this year, gaining those wins at Yarmouth (good to firm) and Kempton (AW) by an aggregate of nearly 20l, both at about 1m3f; brings major potential to this next step.

runners.comment: Came up short in 1,000 Guineas but brings a respectable rating to this drop back in class
runners.name: Inis Mor
runners.spotlight: Campaigned only over 7f/1m but she's bred to be suited by this new trip; solid form as a 2yo then ran well in the Nell Gwyn on reappearance; came up short in the 1,000 Guineas since but brings a respectable rating to this drop back in class and there's still a chance she can do better still.

runners.comment: Prevailed in the Italian 1,000 Guineas on reappearance, taking record to 4-7; progressive
runners.name: Just Call Me Angel
runners.spotlight: Prevailed by half a length in the Italian 1,000 Guineas on seasonal debut to complete a San Siro double (1m, good) and take overall record to 4-7; progressing well, albeit incurs 5lb penalty and needs to prove she can transfer that Group form back to domestic soil; dam stayed 1m2f.

runners.comment: Improving sort and one of her siblings include a Listed-placed filly for her connections
runners.name: On Message
runners.spotlight: Proved well treated off a mark of 80 at Epsom (8.5f, good) on handicap/seasonal debut, following up her autumn win (7f, AW); goes into deeper waters but is improving and her pedigree bodes well, with one of her siblings a Listed-placed filly (stayed 1m2f) for her connections.

stable_tour.quote: She has a few entries but will probably go for a handicap to Epsom on Tuesday. She has an Oaks entry and although she has a miling pedigree, there's a good chance she can stretch out. She shows up well, hence her smart entries. 27-04-26

runners.comment: Needs to rebound from a couple of heavy defeats; goes without usual hood
runners.name: Classic Cuvee

quotes.race: Coopers Marquees EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Classic Cuvee is a lovely filly. We've always liked her and her work's been solid at home. She made a lovely debut and she built on that today. She has a Group 1 entry and that shows how much we think of her but whether or not that's realistic this year we'll have to see - Roger Varian, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Gained her Doncaster maiden win (7f) at the chief expense of the current Oaks favourite but needs to rebound, having suffered a couple of heavy defeats at Newmarket subsequently; goes without usual hood in this first middle-distance attempt.

stable_tour.quote: She has something to prove after her last two starts, but I think she's got quite a lot of talent. She's a half-sister to Legatissimo, who won the 1,000 Guineas, so if she can get back type she's a very valuable filly. That's what I'll be trying to do. 01-04-26

We were delighted with her win at Doncaster. She'd run well when second on her debut at Newmarket and we had a few options where to go with her next. I think that was probably a strong maiden at Doncaster - it often is - and the filly we beat, Amelia Earhart, was quite well fancied on the day, so it was probably a strong performance from our filly. I'm going to train her for the weekend of the Fillies' Mile. She's entered in that race, but that's not to say she'll run in it because on the same card at Newmarket on October 10 there's the Oh So Sharp Stakes, which is a 7f Group 3. I think she has Pattern-race potential - she's got a Classic pedigree being a half-sister to Legatissimo - and now that she's a winner we'd love to shoot for some black type. I think she'll be left in the Fillies' Mile at the forfeit stage, when we can see the shape of that race and see how she's training. But maybe more favourable would be the furlong-shorter Oh So Sharp. 24-09-25

runners.comment: Last of five in the Cheshire Oaks; again looks up against it
runners.name: Winged One
runners.spotlight: Won well at Newcastle (1m, AW) in the second of her two autumn starts but was the rank outsider and ran accordingly (last of five) in the Cheshire Oaks on reappearance; again looks up against it.

runners.comment: Ran well in AW handicap on reappearance; this is a much stiffer task
runners.name: Della Pace
runners.spotlight: Registered her 2yo win on AW and ran well in Wolverhampton handicap (9.5f) returned to that sphere on reappearance; has steadily progressive RPRs, including on turf, but this is a much stiffer task; bottom on ratings.

stable_tour.quote: She's going to be stepped up to ten furlongs. She's done well over the winter and we're looking forward to getting her started. 02-04-26

15:45.race_name: Darley British EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Fourth in Lingfield AW maiden that has thrown up a few winners since
runners.name: Evening Fades
runners.spotlight: Front-running fourth of 12 in December maiden at Lingfield (1m, AW) that has thrown up a few winners since; represents major yard and has possibilities with progress plausible.

runners.comment: Close second in latest Lingfield AW start; leading player on the figures
runners.name: St Hilda
runners.spotlight: Both starts on Lingfield AW, finishing fourth over 7f then taking a step forward with neck second over 1m2f; leading player on the figures and may improve further to boot.

runners.comment: Only about 2l behind St Hilda at Lingfiled; set for an interesting rematch
runners.name: Lady Magu
runners.spotlight: Showed promise with fifth of 12, only about 2l behind St Hilda who had the benefit of experience, in 1m2f AW maiden at Lingfield; set for an interesting rematch with that rival.

runners.comment: Largely consistent efforts over shorter; bred to be suited by this new trip
runners.name: Guesstimate
runners.spotlight: Disappointing on reappearance but has consistent form otherwise, creditable third at Wolverhampton (8.5f, AW) most recently; bred to be suited by this new trip; reasonably solid.

runners.comment: Similar type to Kenkelly and may build on her Ripon effort
runners.name: Triumph
runners.spotlight: Similar type to Kenkelly, having finished third of five on debut; ran to an ordinary RPR in that Ripon maiden (1m2f, good) but looks open to improvement.

runners.comment: Pedigree raises doubts regarding this new trip and switch to turf
runners.name: Cixi
runners.spotlight: Has proved reasonably consistent over 7f-1m on artificial surfaces, good third at Kempton most recently; however, pedigree raises doubts regarding this new trip and switch to turf.

runners.comment: Green and always behind in 7f newcomers' event at Newbury
runners.name: Mother Dear
runners.spotlight: Green and always behind in 7f newcomers' event at Newbury, having been friendless in the betting; by Masar and may fare better over this longer distance.

runners.comment: Modest third at Yarmouth but may do better with the outing under her belt
runners.name: Kenkelly
runners.spotlight: Only a modest third behind the form fillies in small-field contest at Yarmouth (11.5f, good to firm) but may do better with that outing/experience under her belt.

runners.comment: Expensive red-hot favourite this season, narrowly over 1m2f and some late headway at 1m4f
runners.name: Valedictory
runners.spotlight: All the rage in the betting for both starts this term; the line came a touch too soon for his strong finish at Newbury (1m2f) on handicap/seasonal debut, while trying to come from further off the pace did not work out at Ascot on the step up to 1m4f but he did muster some late headway (despite hanging right); that sees him upped further in trip today with first-time headgear; it will be interesting to see whether his backers dare go in again.

runners.comment: Won in March; 2nd in valuable race at Newmarket (1m6f) confirmed that he's turned a corner
runners.name: Align The Stars

quotes.race: Coral Summer Handicap
quotes.quote: Jason Hart galloped Align The Stars in July last year before he'd ever run and said he'll win the Ascot Gold Cup, and we're still bang on track.   He still hasn't really raced over a relentless mile and six furlongs and I think an emphasis on stamina in the St Leger is really going to take him to the next level. It will take another step up for him to be competitive, but I have enough faith in him that it's a realistic aim.  I think back to Subjectivist at the same part of his career and he went to the Leger and it was too sharp a test for him, but then he won a Group 1 in the Prix Royal Oak as a three-year-old - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: Align The Stars is a huge horse who's bred to be top-class. We probably ran him more than we wanted to last year, chasing his Book 1 bonus. I've always hoped he would be a Group horse in time and I've not seen anything today that doesn't give me that confidence. If he went to Goodwood he'd have to come back to a mile and a half and Tony [Farmer, owner] is a big York man, so the Melrose has been on the radar for a long time - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 2024 C&D winner who broke his losing run in clearcut style when he reappeared with restored cheekpieces at Kempton (2m, AW) in March; second in valuable race at Newmarket (1m6f) confirmed that he's turned a corner and must remain in serious calculations.
