stable_tour.quote: The wheels came off a little bit last season but he came into this year with a clean slate and I thought he won very well on his comeback at Kempton. He's a huge horse and it's quite possible he's stronger and more mature as a five-year-old, and will see out those extreme distances better than he did last term. His next run will be in either a valuable one-mile-six-furlong handicap at the Guineas meeting or the Chester Cup. He won't run when there's any soft in the going description and, given that he's just won a Queen's Prize on the all-weather, the Northumberland Plate looks an obvious mid-season target. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Absent last term after April 2m win; possible excuses this season, the Chester Cup latest
runners.name: Moon Over Miami

quotes.race: Compton Beauchamp Estates Ltd Silver Bar Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Moon Over Miami is a complicated horse. He's not been easy and we've had to train him in a certain way, so it's been a long road. He's talented but he's had his trials. The all-weather didn't suit him. He lugged right throughout the race, so that rules him out of the Chester Cup, but he might be one for the Queen Alexandra. He might stay really well - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Third turf win was a narrow one at Newbury (2m, good; rallying) in April on his final start last year; may have needed his 2026 reappearance and the unusual test of the Chester Cup might excuse his disappointing show next time, but a revival is needed.

stable_tour.quote: He's had his issues so I was very pleased with his win at Newbury. I think we'll go right-handed next time as I see him as a Queen Alexandra horse. He's a tough customer and I think he'll stay really well. 28-04-25

runners.comment: C&D winner; return to 1m6f should help and might offset good ground if it dries out
runners.name: Dancingwithmyself
runners.spotlight: Her second win last year came over C&D (good to soft); career-best form when second at Musselburgh (1m6f, soft) on reappearance, meeting trouble in running, but she could not lay a glove on the principals when returned to 1m4f at Ripon (good) three weeks later; return to 1m6f will presumably help and might offset good ground if it dries out; one to consider.

runners.comment: Game front-running win (1m4f, good to soft) final 3yo start; worth another go at this trip
runners.name: Spinning Wheel
runners.owner: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum

quotes.race: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Spinning Wheel is very tough and stays very well. He likes to get his toe in a bit and could be a nice horse as time goes on. He's done well to win under a 5lb penalty. The more you ask, the more he gives you, so he's a joy to ride - Harry Davies, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot (good to firm; 25-1) was the only blemish in his five-race 3yo career, which he ended with a narrow but game front-running win in handicap at Leicester (1m4f, good to soft); raised 6lb but worth another go at this trip.

runners.comment: Tailed off when 7-1 for the Chester Cup (2m2f) but he was going places before that
runners.name: Peaky Blinder
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at Redcar (1m6f, good to soft) in October and won well again when reappearing at Southwell (slowly run 2m, AW; gelded) this April; raised substantially in class for the Chester Cup (2m2f, good; 7-1) 15 days ago, which saw him chase leaders to 4f out before dropping right out, but he was going places before that and could rebound.

runners.comment: Fourth at Ascot (1m4f) latest was his closest finish in winless period and he kept on well
runners.name: Too Soon
runners.spotlight: No win since 2yo, having come up short in Group races, Listed races and four handicaps; fourth of 14 off this mark at Ascot (1m4f) latest was his closest finish in that winless period and he kept on well, so some hope is revived.

runners.comment: Classy on Flat; pulled up in hot hurdle races this spring; left W Mullins for 15,000gns
runners.name: Hipop De Loire

quotes.race: Tote #50,000 Guaranteed Placepot Today Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: It wasn't the plan to make the running but Hipop De Loire just took off and, jumping as slick as he did, Paul said he let him go as he was enjoying himself. His Ebor run was a helluva run. Hopefully we can go back this year, get a bit more daylight and keep out of trouble - Willie Mullins, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Sixth off 1lb higher in last year's 1m6f Ebor at York and third in the 2m2f Doncaster Cup; however, ended last season on a low note and pulled up in hot races for all three starts over hurdles this spring; left Willie Mullins for 15,000gns 16 days ago and blinkers (last worn in Germany in 2023) replace recent cheekpieces; which side he shows today remains to be seen.

stable_tour.quote: A high-class stayer on the Flat who was unlucky in the Ebor last year, and ran well in it again this year. I loved the way he jumped at Galway when he won a maiden hurdle there during the summer and he's one who will head down the staying novice hurdle route. He could do well at that game. 17-11-25

runners.comment: Well handicapped and will pop up in front again at some stage but it's hard to say when
runners.name: Oneforthegutter

quotes.race: bet365 Trophy (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: It was the perfect set-up for Oneforthegutter with fast ground, a decent gallop and plenty of cover, and when I finally got a gap he was very game - Silvestre De Sousa, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: I never expected Oneforthegutter to get in off his mark, but has run a huge race. He and Joe have just gelled together and ultimately just got outstayed. It was a huge performance and a little bit better than the what we were expecting. Class as much as anything beat him today but we'll look for similar sort of things. He could turn out in the Old Borough Cup at Haydock if it doesn't come around too quickly - Ian Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Magnum Classic Ice Cream Handicap
quotes.quote: Oneforthegutter has suffered with his wind in the past and that's his third run back after probably his third wind operation. You couldn't be confident the wind op had worked. As you can imagine [with his breathing] we were worried about the ground but Ben Curtis has given him a great ride and he's stuck at his task and stayed on well. He's always merited winning a prize like that and the new trip today was a good thing. It opens up options for him - Ian Williams, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Scored at the Newmarket July meeting (1m6f) last year but hasn't accomplished a lot since; he's back 2lb below that last winning mark, so will pop up in front again at some stage, but it's hard to say when.

runners.comment: Hat-trick before two narrow, battling defeats and she looks worth this first crack at 1m6f
runners.name: Chilli Queen
runners.spotlight: Can front-run; hat-trick last May/July and short-headed at Doncaster in September when next seen; suffered another narrow, battling defeat at Kempton (again 1m4f; AW) on reappearance 19 days ago but that was improved form yet again and she's worth this first crack at 1m6f.

runners.comment: C&D second to Dancingwithmyself on final outing; could be a useful staying prospect
runners.name: Finalise
runners.spotlight: Won an AW novice and runner-up on turf in her other three starts last term; made the running in C&D handicap (good to soft) on final outing but was mown down late on by Dancingwithmyself; interesting raised just 2lb and she could be a useful staying prospect.

runners.comment: Thrice-raced colt who has progressive AW form; completed a 6f double last time
runners.name: Riley Rocks

quotes.race: Read Meg Nicholls' Blog At betmgm.co.uk Handicap
quotes.quote: Riley Rocks was a little green early on but he's a progressive sprinter and should improve a lot when he goes on the grass - David Probert, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Thrice-raced colt who has progressive AW form and completed a 6f double with handicap success at Southwell most recently; likely danger provided he's as effective on turf and returned to 5f.

runners.comment: Worth a crack at this new trip and has possibilities if taking well to headgear
runners.name: Wedonttelllies
runners.spotlight: Gained his 2yo win over 7f on AW but ran respectably over 6f at Ascot (good) most recently, while shaping as if this drop to 5f is worth exploring; possibilities if taking well to first-time headgear.

runners.comment: Overcame traffic issues to win at Bath last time; may show further improvement
runners.name: Coyy
runners.spotlight: Overcame traffic issues to get up near the finish in Windsor handicap (5f, good to firm) last time, opening his account; may build on that success and show further improvement; enters calculations.

stable_tour.quote: He's had three runs and ran well when third in a 6f maiden at Windsor  last time. He had a little problem, so he couldn't run when he was due to at Bath this month - he pulled a little muscle but he's fine now. I think we'll probably go to the Super Sprint with him. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Runner-up in two of her three starts this year; not ruled out
runners.name: Angel Numbers
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-9 since debut success but she is somewhat threatening to double her tally, having finished second in two of her three outings this term, latest at Bath (5f, firm); not ruled out.

runners.comment: Record of 133 (all over 6f) since handicapping; close third last time
runners.name: Eightthreeone
runners.spotlight: Record of 133 (all over 6f) since switched to handicaps, the success on AW; close third at Windsor (good to firm) most recently; may remain competitive, provided he's as effective back at 5f.

runners.comment: Has posted two sound placed efforts since returned to turf and dropped to 5f
runners.name: One And Gone
runners.spotlight: Gained sole success on AW but has posted two sound placed efforts since returned to turf and dropped to 5f, latest at Chester; again has each-way possibilities.

runners.comment: Chance largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear
runners.name: Tie Fighter
runners.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is making belated handicap debut; chance of opening his account largely depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

runners.breeder: W H R John And Partners
runners.comment: Record of 2-3 in handicaps last term; below par on stable/seasonal debut
runners.name: Campenaerts
runners.spotlight: Had a record of 2-3 in handicaps (AW/soft) last term for previous yard; below par at Bath on stable/seasonal debut but may do better with the outing under his belt.

runners.comment: Record of 2-2 at Brighton bodes well for this first visit to Goodwood; interesting
runners.name: London Is Blue
runners.spotlight: Record of 2-2 at Brighton bodes well for this first visit to Goodwood, which is quite a similar track; may resume progress with Bath reappearance under his belt and looks interesting.

stable_tour.quote: He ran five times as a two-year-old and won a couple of races, both at Brighton. He was supposed to run at Yarmouth the other day but he misbehaved in the starting gate and got his leg trapped, so he had to be withdrawn. He has a lot of speed and looks as if he's wintered really well and turned into quite a nice, big three-year-old. I would hope he has a good career in front of him. He'd be my dark horse. 20-05-26

runners.comment: Progress is likely required in this field on reappearance
runners.name: Dark Alley
runners.spotlight: Successful in Bath maiden (5.7f) last summer and ran respectably in 5f AW handicap on final 2yo start; however, progress is likely required in this field on reappearance.

runners.comment: Has failed to back up the form of her debut success
runners.name: Arlos Girl
runners.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who has failed to back up the form of her debut success (AW); never landed a blow at Chester switched to turf most recently; something to prove.

13:30.race_name: William Hill Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap

runners.comment: Returned in form, including close second to Mae Amor at Hamilton last Sunday; good shout
runners.name: Jonny Concrete
runners.spotlight: Second to Kats Bob over C&D (good to firm) last year off 3lb higher; has resumed in good form this spring, following Chester near miss with a close second of 13 to reopposing Mae Amor at Hamilton (6f, good) last Sunday; obvious chance off the same mark; second-time blinkers replace regular cheekpieces.

stable_tour.quote: He's done well this year and we're very pleased with him. He could have probably run another couple of times but we've kept him back for Ayr next week. We'll take him there fresh and he'll probably get in the Bronze Cup, where he could run a really big race. 10-09-25

runners.comment: In good form over 5f, including close second last weekend; player if as effective at 6f
runners.name: Al Hussar
runners.spotlight: Raced around 5f; creditable in-frame efforts on all four outings this year, notably when neck second of 17 at Thirsk (good) last Saturday; nudged up another 3lb but it shouldn't prevent a prominent showing if proving as effective at the new trip.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a fairly frustrating summer as he's talented, but he started the year high enough in the handicap. He's quick - he wants the fastest five you can get - and he's starting to look well handicapped again. He's just been held up by some ringworm but he's started back breezing and is on the way back now. He goes on the all-weather as well. 04-09-25

runners.comment: Added to good record in mud at Haydock on Thursday but ground likely to be quicker here
runners.name: Trilby

quotes.race: Beverley Beaker Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Trilby shows nothing at home. He's so laid-back for a sprinter. He's a pleasure to deal with and, because he's so easy and rideable, he just saves himself, which is great. He's been a great horse for us so far, so anything else he achieves is a bonus. He likes Haydock, and we all like a day out at York, so fingers crossed we'll keep tipping away with him. It will be fun to see what the season brings - Sam England, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Reacted well to first-time cheekpieces when picking up nicely to collar a back-to-form rival (pair clear) at Haydock (5f, soft) on Thursday; 5lb penalty in a deeper race but a bigger factor could be that the ground is unlikely to be as testing this time (has won on good but seems most potent when the mud is flying).

stable_tour.quote: He's another star, although he's high in the handicap now and it's hard for him. A progressive three-year-old beat him at Haydock and he ran another fine race at Doncaster last Saturday, which was one of the few times he's had his favoured soft ground this season. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Better signs from reduced mark when fourth over 7f here last week, leading long way
runners.name: Orne

quotes.race: Betfred Horris Hill Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: It wasn't the plan to make the running. Orne went last in, but he was first out. Normally he doesn't do a stroke when he is in front but I went on a fresh bit of ground, and he found a rhythm. Just towards the end he got a little bit lonely and ducked left, but he has done it well. It wasn't the plan to go on the far side as I wanted to drop in and get a lead and get there late. When I ended up in front I could see there was fresh ground there so I thought I might as well go there. He didn't stay the mile in the Autumn Stakes. He travelled good and he handled the ground, but he just didn't stay. He could get quicker this horse over the winter - Rab Havlin, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Very useful on his day for previous yard; nowhere near the same force for his current one but his mark reflects that and he looked to be coming to hand when fourth of 22 over 7f at here at last week's Dante meeting, travelling comfortably in the lead for a long way; not discounted back at 6f.

runners.comment: Back-to-form second at Windsor latest; has handicapping scope if able to build on that
runners.name: An Outlaws Grace

quotes.race: Byerley Stud Peter & Virginia Walwyn Memorial British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You go to the races hoping they can get it done and I'm relieved An Outlaw's Grace did it on his debut. It was a very kind ride from Sean [Levey, jockey], he nursed him into the race and he will have learned plenty - Tim Palin, director of racing to the owners.

runners.spotlight: Down in weights and step back in the right direction when second of nine at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 12 days ago; has handicapping scope if able to build on that.

stable_tour.quote: A talented horse who won first time out as a two-year-old and went to the Prix Robert Papin afterwards, but he kind of lost his way. He's working well now and looks great, so I expect him to be winning races. 21-04-26

runners.comment: Edged out Jonny Concrete at Hamilton but Iain Jardine's charge is weighted to turn tables
runners.name: Mae Amor
runners.spotlight: Struggled on first three starts for this yard last autumn but back to form with a bang when accounting for the reopposing Jonny Concrete and 11 others at Hamilton (6f, good) last Sunday; only scraped home by a short head so she may struggle to confirm that narrow superiority over Iain Jardine's charge on the revised terms.

runners.comment: Two AW wins for previous trainer; met trouble on recent return for new yard
runners.name: Kiniro
runners.spotlight: Won twice for Harry Charlton, both over 6f on Lingfield's AW track; didn't get the chance to show what he could do (repeatedly denied a clear run) when eighth of 12 on recent Chester return for new yard; left the impression he'd have been involved in the finish with more luck and enters calculations.

runners.comment: In good form, including 2nd back on turf latest, but he's 5lb above highest winning mark
runners.name: Papa Cocktail
runners.spotlight: Consistent spell on Tapeta over the winter and continued the good work back on turf when close second of six at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; he's never won above a mark of 75, though.

stable_tour.quote: I think he is a very nice colt with a bright future. His work had been encouraging this spring and we started him off over 7f late last month at Yarmouth in what looked a particularly hot maiden, with several of the big yards represented and many trainers liking their charges. He ran a cracker to be third behind New Science, where he was rather green but ran on well. It was the perfect start to his career as he will have learned plenty and mentally handled things well. There are a few 7f maidens around Royal Ascot time later this month and we will pick our spot to make him a winner and take it from there. He runs in the colours of owner Khalifa Dasmal, who is a great man to train for. His patronage is largely thanks to my former guv'nor David Simcock giving him a nod in my direction. David has been a huge help to me in my career and I am very hopeful that I have a potentially nice horse here for Mr Dasmal. 10-06-21

runners.comment: Scored on turf last summer and went close on AW latest but done all his winning over 7f
runners.name: Beattie Is Back
runners.owner: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd

quotes.race: Grace And Dotty Fedoras And Feathers Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: They came up the middle so I had to take my medicine but we weaved our way through and Beattie Is Back picked up well. - Jack Garritty, Jockey.

runners.spotlight: Landed a 7f turf win at Doncaster (good to firm) last summer and close second at Wolverhampton (7f) on latest start in February; back from a 12-week break with his stable among the winners but he's done all his winning at 7f.

runners.comment: All the sharper for reappearance when second at Thirsk (6f) three weeks ago
runners.name: Mister Sox
runners.spotlight: Started 2025 with three wins; wasn't as forward for this year's reappearance but quickly back on form when second (Kats Bob fourth) of nine at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago.

runners.comment: Thirsk win for new yard last month and this easier than Newbury Class 2 last weekend
runners.name: Yes Im Mali
runners.spotlight: Prevailed in big-field Class 5 event at Thirsk (6f, good) last month on second start for new yard; found it harder in a Newbury Class 2 last weekend but could fare better with his sights lowered.

runners.comment: Five wins for Ruth Carr last year, including C&D; has run with credit this spring
runners.name: Kats Bob
runners.spotlight: Enthusiastic front-runner who shone for Ruth Carr in 2025, winning five 6f handicaps (including a defeat of Jonny Concrete here on good to firm); creditable in-frame efforts on two of three starts this year without necessarily suggesting he's ready to strike again.

stable_tour.quote: He's a front-runner who wears his heart on his sleeve. He's really straightforward and a pleasure to have at the yard. He was a good second at Catterick on his reappearance last week. He's declared at Ripon on Thursday and we'll see what the handicapper does about the Catterick run. I don't really like to back them up too quickly on the back of a break, but he might run if the handicapper forces me to and he seems okay. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Hasn't fired in two runs this year but yard's good recent form provides hope
runners.name: Lord Roxby
runners.owner: N Skinner D Jenkins J Glover

prev_owners.owner: N Skinner D Jenkins T Goodair J Glover

runners.spotlight: Generally performed with great credit last season, including a 6f Hamilton win in May off the same mark as today; never involved in either start this year but his stable's good recent form provides some hope.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very good horse who works very well. We've not quite got it right with him as he's been placed a lot of times and it's disappointing he's only won once this year. We've probably got his trip wrong and he can be very keen. He was like that at Newbury last time when he ran a respectable race to finish sixth. He's rated 81 now and I'd like to go for the 0-80 over 7f at York in a couple of weeks. He could also go to Southwell, where they go a right gallop which helps him settle. He'll be a nice horse next year. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Yet to find best form this year but well treated if a first-time visor gives him a lift
runners.name: Jenever

quotes.race: Download The PricedUp App Grassroots Series Final Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: On Jenever's best form I knew he was capable of winning something like this, but something has to fall right. He's a bit older and wiser and perhaps needed a change of headgear, he didn't try particularly hard last time so I think the blinkers have made all the difference - Jessica Macey, trainer.

quotes.race: Chris Barnett Memorial Handicap (A Jockey Club Grassroots Sprint Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: The race was run to suit Jenever as he likes to peg them off at a fast pace. He's a five-and-a-half-furlong horse, so he likes it at Sandown because you get a stiff five and a good pace - Jessica Macey, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Still to find top form this term but he is well handicapped if a change of headgear (first-time visor for cheekpieces) gives him a lift.

runners.comment: Met trouble at Chester a fortnight ago but no obvious excuses at Newmarket last weekend
runners.name: Miraculous
runners.spotlight: Met trouble when fifth at Chester (6f, good) a fortnight ago but there were no apparent excuses when filling the same position at Newmarket last Saturday; the type to click for this yard before long but others are stronger today.

runners.comment: Tremendous stable servant who won on 2025 reappearance and has a strong York record
runners.name: Dakota Gold

prev_owners.owner: Doug Graham Alan Drysdale & Ian Davison
Doug Graham & The Late Ron Davison

quotes.race: Armstrong Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: There's only my daughter Sophie who rides Dakota Gold and he just does his work on his own. He's still keen at home and I said to Connor [Beasley, jockey] to just let him bowl along if he's enjoying it. We thought we'd just get away with the quick ground. He'd come on for the run - Michael Dods, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Vertem Leading The Field Handicap
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold loved the ground. He got headed and he fought back and he's still got that enthusiasm for it. He's tremendous. He's not as good as he was, you don't expect them to be, but he can still race to a good level. Although there were only six runners, they were six good horses and he showed a good attitude - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Churchill Tyres Handicap
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold looks better this year than last year - I was never really happy with him in his coat. Six furlongs on good ground is perfect for him. For an eight-year-old to go and do that, he's got some heart. It's nice to see him come back and hopefully he'll go on from here - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Wentworth Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: They were coming to Dakota Gold but he's dug deep. He's finished for the season and we'll look forward to next year. He's getting better, I think he's improving big time. He dug deep here and if you look at his 5f race at Nottingham he was impressive. He'll definitely be looking at Group races next year - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Bengough Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: It was a plus when Stormy Girl came out as that meant Dakota Gold could dictate it. He loves it here, I couldn't tell you why it brings out the best in him but it's a good, flat track - the best in the country. I'm not ruling out running him again on Wednesday (in a Listed race at Nottingham) but otherwise there's only the Listed race at Doncaster at the end of the season - Michael Dods, winning trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Beverley Bullet Sprint Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold is back to his best. It's been hard for him, being rated 110 from the start of the season. We thought he was coming back to his best last time in the Great St Wilfrid. He travelled and quickened but he had 9st 10lb and the weight caught him out. He was well placed by the boss, bringing him back here. He sprung the lids and his tactical speed did the job. It was good to get him back in the winner's enclosure -  Connor Beasley, jockey.

quotes.race: UK Hi-Fi Show Live Rous Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: The soft going, five furlongs and the stiff track suited Dakota Gold. He was always in control and showed his guts by outbattling them when they came to him. We will either finish him for the season or we will have a look at the weights in the Wentworth Stakes at Doncaster next month. If that is it for the year, we've got a lot to look forward to next season - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: LNER Supporting CALM Garrowby Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: I would say that is another career best. Connor said Dakota Gold was in trouble when they were coming to him, but once he sensed the horses were there he picked up and he's gone away at the end. He won't run in the Ayr Gold Cup as he has another penalty. There is a Group 3 at Newbury on Ayr Gold Cup day and that's a possibility - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet And Symphony Group Handicap
quotes.quote: We'll go for the Ayr Gold Cup rather than the Portland. Dakota Gold was 3lb well in today and only won three-quarters of a length so hopefully the handicapper won't go silly - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Great St Wilfrid Handicap
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold is improving, with another year on him he's getting the six furlongs, he has put the race to bed at halfway - he showed so much speed - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold is really a five-furlong horse but the ground came right for him. He had an injury at the end of January after getting a leg caught and cutting it so it's great to see him back. Connor Beasley gets on so well with him and there aren't many as strong as Connor. I'd say he'll be back at five furlongs for the Ebor meeting but he loves this soft ground - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Smarkets Handicap
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold has been difficult as he's a bit of a hot head. He's bad in the gates and is allowed to go in last. He's been running at six furlongs and I do think that's his best trip but he's just too keen. However, I won't be altering his distance now and we'll look for another race providing the ground is not too good - Michael Dods, trainer.

quotes.race: Watch Racing UK In HD Handicap
quotes.quote: Dakota Gold struggled to settle a bit last year but he's been dropped back to 5f and relished it there - Connor Beasley, jockey.

quotes.race: Always Trying Maiden Stakes (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: There's an engine there and Dakota Gold showed a good attitude, but he was just a bit keen and I wouldn't be frightened to go back to five furlongs - Michael Dods, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Tremendous stable servant over the years with 17 wins; understandably not the force of old but won on 2025 reappearance (off 6lb higher) and has a strong York record (6-18).

stable_tour.quote: He always runs his race but he's an old horse now. I always felt he would become competitive again when he dropped below 90 and he's shown that this season. He ran well at York off 84 and then won at Redcar off 86 in May, then ran well again at Ripon off 90, which is his current mark. There's a 0-95 at Thirsk on Friday over 6f and he'll probably run there next, but he doesn't want firm in the going description. 28-08-24

runners.comment: While since he won but his three efforts for Paul Midgley have been encouraging; claims
runners.name: Almarada Prince
runners.spotlight: Split James's Delight and Elmonjed in top 3yo handicap over C&D (good to soft) in 2024; failed to win in 2025 but he has edged down the weights and his three runs for Paul Midgley have been quite encouraging, faring best of those in the far-side group when sixth of 16 back on turf at Ripon (6f, good to soft) 37 days ago; considered.

runners.breeder: D & S L Tanker Transport Ltd
runners.comment: Well handicapped without obviously shaping as if ready to take advantage
runners.name: Intervention

quotes.race: William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap
quotes.quote: It's a massive pot for a horse like Intervention. It's a big handicap for whatever horse it is, but at his age, he's just been an absolute star for us. We kind of felt he could run well, looking at the quality of the race this year. Outside the top three, it was a 0-90. With question marks against each of those three classier horses, we did feel that we had a decent chance and that the track would suit him - and it did. He wasn't much higher for Wolverhampton and he'd got good form on the all-weather off slightly higher marks. Martin [Dixon, brother and part-owner] got William [Pyle] booked very early on and his three pounds off was always going to help. We thought we were going to need a lightweight rider, so we thought we may as well take a little bit of weight off on top of that. William does seem one of those riders where some of these sprinters will just run for him - Chris Dixon, part-owner.

quotes.race: Win £2,000,000 With BetMGM's Golden Goals Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a fantastic win again and Intervention is just an amazing horse. That's eleven wins since we bought him, his last four on the bounce. He's going on seven, in the form of his life and is better than ever. It secures at least sharing the top prize for the all-weather horse of the month at the Arc (Arena Racing Company) tracks in December because that's three wins from his last three runs. We're thrilled with him, he came to us as a longstanding maiden and Mick's just worked wonders with him. He's a bit of a hero of ours, he's won more races for us than any other horse and he's a firm favourite - Chris Dixon, syndicate boss.

runners.spotlight: Won last season's Great St Wilfrid at Ripon off a 7lb higher mark; didn't run badly at Nottingham (5f, good) on penultimate start and a wide draw offers an excuse at Chester since.

stable_tour.quote: Our winningmost horse with 11 victories. He had quite a few goes before we bought him and he's won all those races for us and well over £100,000 in prize-money. He's just a legend. He runs his race nearly every time and always seems to be in the money. He's come down to a good mark again for the all-weather season and he's ready to win again soon. He's having a break now and usually thrives through the winter. 26-09-24

runners.comment: Won this in 2024 but isn't obviously in good enough form to stage a repeat
runners.name: Tiriac

quotes.race: Betonline At BetGoodwin Cock O'The North EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Tiriac ran very well at Newmarket the other day, it was a good horse who beat him there. He's a full-brother to Nastase who won the Rockingham Stakes - Mick Channon, trainer

runners.spotlight: Slowly away and never a threat on all three starts this year, the latest last weekend; being dropped another 2lb can only help but he isn't obviously in good enough form to add to his 2024 success in this.

runners.comment: Well held both starts this year and others are much more obvious
runners.name: Blind Beggar
runners.owner: New Vision Bloodstock & Steel A Win

quotes.race: Texas At Sandown Park 7 August Handicap
quotes.quote: Blind Beggar had dropped to a good mark and jumped much cleaner today. I was hoping to get a really clean trip for him and then gradually work through the gears. I thought we went an even gallop and I was keen to get the momentum rolling forward because I knew he'd gallop through the line - Luke Morris, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Record of 240500 for current yard reflects that he hasn't been able to hold his form; others are much more obvious.

stable_tour.quote: We bought him at the October sales from Ger Lyons' yard with one win to his name. I've given him three runs on the all-weather since he arrived and he has won two of them at Southwell and Chelmsford. The most recent was six weeks ago and I've deliberately put him away now with a turf campaign in mind. He's effective over 5f and 6f and is up to a mark of 84, which looks quite workable. He's well capable of winning off that and hopefully improving some more. 22-03-23

runners.breeder: D Ryan D S Ryan & R A Williams
runners.comment: Nearly gained seventh Ripon win latest but his York record isn't anywhere near as strong
runners.name: Fortamour

prev_owners.owner: C Barclay Racing Knights & C Cleevely

quotes.race: Wilmot-Smith Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: Fortamour broke well and I got a good position; everything just went so smoothly. He was pulling up as soon as he hit the front, but just seems to love this track - Paul Mulrennan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Back on form when only narrowly denied a seventh Ripon win 15 days ago but the fact he's placed just once in his eight visits to York is less encouraging

runners.comment: Four AW wins; confirmed he's as good on turf when second on Thursday but this is harder
runners.name: El Bufalo
runners.spotlight: Four-time AW winner who has shown he's equally as effective on turf this spring, shaping better than the result at Ascot before finishing second of six at Chepstow (5f, good to soft) on Thursday; same mark if turned out again quickly but this is a stronger race.

14:05.race_name: Tomahawk EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands A, B, C And D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Promising third at Ascot two weeks ago, briefly looking a threat; looks the one to beat
runners.name: Cuban Heels
runners.spotlight: 100,000gns yearling by Havana Grey, out of 1m 2yo winner; promising third of ten at Ascot (6f, good; 2-1 favourite) two weeks ago, briefly looking a threat; open to improvement and looks the one to beat.

runners.comment: Bred to be useful and represents an excellent stable; needs serious consideration
runners.name: Possessive
runners.spotlight: By Lucky Vega; dam 7.5f/1m winner (including 2yo/Group 2 German 1,000 Guineas; RPR 110), sister to three winners at up to 1m, out of Listed-placed 6f winning half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Zinziberine; bred to be useful and represents an excellent stable; needs serious consideration.

runners.comment: Beverley winner; came up short in Listed event here last week; should stay this far
runners.name: Lake Muritz
runners.spotlight: Beat four rivals at Beverley (5f, good to soft) earlier this month but came up short in Listed event here last week; needs to get back on track; should stay this extra furlong.

runners.comment: 52,000gns purchase at the breeze-ups; bred to be pretty sharp and worth a market check
runners.name: Mussab
runners.spotlight: 52,000gns purchase at the breeze-ups; by Ten Sovereigns; dam 6f winner (RPR 78), half-sister to 6f winner Rhossili Down, out of 6f 2yo winner; bred to be pretty sharp and worth a market check.

runners.comment: 90,000gns yearling; interesting newcomer for yard whose 2yos have been in top form
runners.name: Stardom Glory
runners.spotlight: 90,000gns yearling; Starspangledbanner half-brother to winners Rebel Tale (Group-placed 5.7f 2yo; RPR 106), Rebel Step (1m 2yo, 95) and La Vale (US 6f-1m); dam US 1m1f turf winner, half-sister to 1m-1m2f Listed winner Arch Rebel; interesting newcomer for yard whose 2yos have been in top form.

runners.comment: 0-3; did not convince with stamina for 6f when fourth at Newmarket last Friday
runners.name: Turnstile
runners.spotlight: Has had three goes already; faded into fourth of 13 at Newmarket last Friday, not convincing with his stamina on first attempt at 6f; one of three runners for Tim Easterby.

runners.comment: Signs of ability in two runs over 5f; retains potential but needs a big leap forward
runners.name: Ponte Carlo
runners.spotlight: Signs of ability over 5f at Musselburgh (third of four) and Beverley (met trouble when eighth of 11); retains potential but needs a big leap forward over this extra furlong.

runners.comment: Brother to a 5.5f/6f 2yo winner but may need a run or two before becoming of interest
runners.name: Ubetawatchout
runners.spotlight: 20,000gns foal, 45,000gns yearling; brother to 5.5f/6f 2yo winner Tricky Tel (RPR 82), half-brother to three winners; dam maiden (61) sister to useful 7f/10.6f winner Jackaroo; may need a run or two before becoming of interest.

runners.comment: Sprang 40-1 C&D surprise last week on stable debut; may still be unexposed
runners.name: Fortification

quotes.race: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap
quotes.quote: Fortification has showed lots of speed at home and I'd been telling the owners he's the fastest horse we've got. On the all-weather he's always been getting going towards the end. I told Ben [Robinson] if it wasn't happening early on, take your time and find the place to go from. We won't rush him and look after him - Brian Ellison, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Sprang a 40-1 C&D surprise last week on first start since leaving Archie Watson, finishing fast to lead late on; now 4lb higher but he hasn't had much racing and there may be better still to come.

runners.comment: Encouraging return to action when second at Goodwood; solid credentials
runners.name: King Of Light
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 better than ever and he made an encouraging return to action when second at Goodwood (5f, good) at the start of this month; has run well over C&D in the past; solid credentials.

runners.comment: Only second go in blinkers when making all at Hamilton; possibilities under 5lb penalty
runners.name: Vantheman

quotes.race: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap
quotes.quote: If Vantheman wasn't a bit lively beforehand, I'd have been worried ? he's always like that. He's been going well at home, but has just been unfortunate. Last time the blind got stuck in the blinkers, so this was essentially the first time he properly raced in them. He's done it well - Tom Eaves, jockey, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: Midnite Ain't Your Grandad's Bookie Handicap
quotes.quote: Vantheman is a good horse. It was his first run for a while and he did have a blow so he should come on a lot for that. He is a big boy who is probably better with a lead for a bit longer but he showed a great attitude - Shane Gray, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: None too consistent but he had an excuse on his penultimate start and surged back to form to win at Hamilton (5f, good; made all) last Sunday; that was only his second go in blinkers and he's again of interest under a 5lb penalty.

runners.comment: Has claims on narrow Beverley win but never the slightest threat over C&D next time
runners.name: Air Force One

quotes.race: NavanRacecourse.ie Maiden
quotes.quote: Air Force One is a horse that joined us last year. He has gotten stronger and had been showing a bit of pace. This was a nice place to start. I think he's a five furlong sprinter - Paddy Twomey, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Has claims on his narrow Beverley win in April (5f, good to soft; only 2lb higher here), but he was never the slightest threat over C&D next time after a sluggish start; needs to bounce back.

runners.comment: Musselburgh winner; fourth in big field over C&D last time; in the mix off unchanged mark
runners.name: Pilgrim

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Scottish Sprint Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: I thought the ground would beat Pilgrim but he's a bit older. We've had a long spell off with him, he had a couple of runs on the all-weather which helped him get back. He is a turf horse and he's capable off his mark and showed it today - David Barron, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Palace Of Holyrood House Stakes (Handicap)
quotes.quote: Pilgrim has done it well there. I thought he might have knackered his handicap mark at Musselburgh. We always thought that he was a really nice horse, not just a good two-year-old, and he's shown there today he's good. It's a great place to come and have a winner so it's very nice. This lad has a lot of speed. He travelled very well and he won quite comfortably. He done it easy - Joe Fanning, rider.

runners.spotlight: In-form 5yo; overcame trouble to win at Musselburgh (5f, soft) in April and was a creditable fourth in a big field here (6f, good) ten days ago; should be thereabouts again off an unchanged mark.

runners.comment: Third in warm C&D event this time last year; very dangerous if staging a revival
runners.name: Toca Madera
runners.owner: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi

quotes.race: British EBF 40th Anniversary Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands B, C And D) (Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Toca Madera had done everything right first time, and was a little bit unlucky, but he did that well. We'll see how he comes out of it. He didn't like the ground but Kieran was very complimentary, saying he'll be better on much better ground. With rain round the corner Royal Ascot is a possibility - Brian Meehan, trainer, talking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Useful on his day for Brian Meehan, third to subsequent Group 1 winner American Affair over C&D (good to firm) last spring off an 11lb higher mark; might have needed both his runs for new connections, midfield over C&D at the Dante meeting last time; very dangerous if staging a revival.

runners.comment: Upwardly mobile 3yo; better than result when fourth at Chester; commands major respect
runners.name: Alvin
runners.spotlight: 3yo who arrives on the up; easy winner at Bath (5f, firm) last month and ran well considering he was drawn wide and slowly away when fourth at Chester next time; still unexposed and commands major respect.

runners.comment: Not disgraced from wide draw at Chester; falling in weights; solid each-way claims
runners.name: Vintage Clarets

quotes.race: William Hill Catterick Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: It was a bit easier this year [than last year]. Vintage Clarets' last couple of runs were good, he enjoys that ground, he broke well and I was able to get the run of the race - Osin Orr, rider.

quotes.race: William Hill Catterick Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: We got there plenty soon enough and in the last-furlong Vintage Clarets was only just doing enough but I did think we got nailed on the line.  He's a legend of a horse and he's been very consistent all year. It's great to get a win on him - Oisin Orr, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Prolific winner over the years, including over C&D; no impact yet this season but he wasn't disgraced from a wide draw at Chester last time and he's tumbling in the weights; solid each-way claims.

runners.comment: Found only Vantheman too strong at Hamilton and 5lb better off here; respected
runners.name: Reigning Profit

quotes.race: Welcome Racing TV Members Handicap
quotes.quote: Reigning Profit was a bit slower away than we'd hoped but it worked out well in the end. He likes it here - Ruth Carr, trainer.

quotes.race: Ripon Races Ladies Day 22nd June Handicap
quotes.quote: He did it well. Reigning Profit broke very quickly so I travelled strongly through the race and I think he was just getting a little tired near the line - James Sullivan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap (Round 3)
quotes.quote: Reigning Profit is usually a good eater and he's a solid sprinter so I see no reason why he shouldn't go to Goodwood on Friday - Ruth Carr, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 5lb lower than last winning mark and came close to taking advantage when finding only Vantheman too strong at Hamilton (5f, good) last week; meets that rival on 5lb better terms; should be involved in the shake-up once more.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a good old horse for us. He won three last year and was second, beaten only a neck, in a 5f heritage handicap at Ascot in July. He's had no luck in running three times this year but is capable off his current mark. He wins his races every year and has been a really fun horse for the owners. 15-04-26

runners.comment: Runner-up in 2024 and warmed up nicely at the Dante meeting; should be thereabouts
runners.name: Lethal Nymph

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Fox

runners.spotlight: Runner-up in this race in 2024, and he warmed up nicely for another bid with a good fourth in a big field over C&D at the Dante meeting; should be in the thick of things once more.

stable_tour.quote: He's done really well over the winter and wants quicker ground rather than slower. We'll look at a summer campaign over six furlongs. Ascot suits him really well and hopefully he could be one for the Wokingham. 02-05-23

He ran a solid second in first-time cheekpieces at Pontefract and we thought he'd win at Thirsk but he got a bump there and it's taken him a long time to get over it. He's back galloping now and, with a bit of luck, he should be running soon. 14-08-25

runners.comment: Met trouble when second favourite at Chester on return to Britain; not discounted
runners.name: Partisan Hero

quotes.race: Societies Welcome At Gowran Park Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't use my whip much as I was fairly confident Partisan Hero was doing enough the whole way up the straight. His last furlong was probably his best so he will be able to go up in trip. There should be improvement in him - Jake Coen, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: All wins at 7f/1m but he was placed twice over 5f in Bahrain during the winter; met trouble when second favourite at Chester (extended 7f) on his return to Britain 17 days ago; harder to pin down than some of these and certainly not discounted.

stable_tour.quote: A horse I bought out of Dermot Weld's, he had his first start for us at Windsor this month and just got done in second when he was probably unlucky. He was an expensive horse [72,000gns] for what he's rated [68], but I like him a lot and think he'll be a lovely horse. We got him in October and he's taken time to get right. It was quick enough at Windsor and he probably wants a bit of cut in the ground. I hope he could end up being a Saturday horse. 30-05-24

runners.comment: Not disgraced when sixth over C&D but he'll need more if he's to return to winning ways
runners.name: Sports Coach
runners.spotlight: Hasn't built on his success at Southwell (5f, AW) in March; not disgraced when sixth over C&D nine days ago but he'll need more if he's to return to winning ways.

stable_tour.quote: I think he's a Group sprinter in the making. He won his last two races on the all-weather very well and will go to Bath for a £45,000 three-year-old handicap on Sunday. If it comes up very soft he'll wait for a 0-90 at Thirsk, then he'll go for the Westow at York. 03-04-24

runners.comment: Last effort best ignored and he'd previously run well at Newcastle; not ruled out
runners.name: Stratusnine
runners.spotlight: Slipped and was pulled up at Chester 16 days ago but he'd previously run well when second over 6f at Newcastle; creditable efforts on both his runs at York (7f); yet to prove his effectiveness at 5f but he's not short of speed; not ruled out.

runners.comment: Excuses this year and now 7lb lower than when winning over C&D last summer; interesting
runners.name: Squealer

quotes.race: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Dash Handicap
quotes.quote: With the second winning at Epsom, it swapped the weights around a bit and it's brilliant to win at our local track. Squealer has only got one run of 100 yards and I'm not sure where we'll go next. We'll see what the handicapper does - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

quotes.race: Custom Chairs By KC Sofas Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't quite think Squealer would pick up like he did, he hit a little bit of a flat spot then he picked up very well in the end. He's got an electric turn of foot when you can get him to switch off in the first half of the race. He wants top-of-the-ground. He's been a bit unlucky a few times but now he's got his head in front I think he'll grow in confidence. He's a nice sprinter going forward - Rowan Scott, jockey.

quotes.race: Ire Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Squealer is a lovely colt who has done little wrong in his career so far. It was a good place to win today. He'll go to the Cornwallis Stakes next as there aren't many other races left this season for horses like him - Nigel Tinkler, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Only sixth and ninth this year, but he caught the eye on his reappearance and blew the start next time; now 7lb lower than when winning over C&D (good ground) last summer; likely to be doing his best work late on and a leading contender if getting the breaks.

stable_tour.quote: His win at York in June meant a lot to us as it's our local course and the owners have an apartment in the old Terry's Chocolate factory, which overlooks the track. He beat Jm Jungle that day and that form looks even better now. The handicapper has got his measure a bit and he's been unlucky with his draws in recent races. He'll go back to York for the final meeting there but he needs quick ground. He won't go to Bahrain this time as he didn't travel well there last year. 01-10-25

runners.comment: Followed Musselburgh win with below-par run over C&D; others are more enticing
runners.name: Ziggys Triton
runners.spotlight: Returned to form with a win at Musselburgh (5f, good) in April but followed that with a below-par run over C&D last week; Danny Tudhope jumps ship; others are more enticing.

runners.comment: Stiff task and met trouble in Listed race here last week but others are still more obvious
runners.name: Temple Of Athena
runners.spotlight: All three wins at 5f; below par since beating eight rivals at Wolverhampton in March, although she faced a stiff task and met some trouble in Listed race here last week; this is a more realistic assignment but others still have more obvious claims.

runners.comment: Two Southwell wins this year; fair run last time but will need career best to go in again
runners.name: Master Of My Fate
runners.owner: Ms Janelle Cao Ross Harmon & Partner

quotes.race: Free Bets With BetUK Bet Club Handicap
quotes.quote: Master Of My Fate jumped really well and the more he's racing the more he's improving. I'd like to think when he gets back on turf he will do the same - Jason Hart, jockey.

quotes.race: Trevor Woods Memorial British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands A, B, C & D) Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Master Of My Fate been training well at home. I'm very pleased with how he did it. You can only beat what's put in front of you, but we've always liked him and I was delighted to see him win - John Quinn, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Successful twice over 5f at Southwell this year and ran respectably at Nottingham in April, but he's 3lb above his highest winning mark and will need a career best if he's to go in again.

stable_tour.quote: He beat very little when winning at Pontefract on his debut but he beat them very well and also ran well in a novice at Lingfield, even though he wasn't in love with that track. Then it didn't look like he stayed 6f at Newcastle. I'd imagine we'll drop him back to 5f and he could be one for decent sprint handicaps. He's been gelded and I think that will help him. 20-03-24

runners.comment: Might have needed the run when seventh at Catterick; has possibilities if building on that
runners.name: Franciscos Piece

prev_owners.owner: Keatley Racing Owners Group & D Moore

quotes.race: Prix la Fleche (Listed Race) (2yo) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Francisco's Piece is a good horse and this is a massive step forward. We're delighted to get that win under his belt. He's going to improve loads as he's still a little bit behind in his coat and is still a little bit underdeveloped. He could come back for the Prix Robert Papin. Everybody want's to go to Royal Ascot, but I don't mind if this fella stays at home in his box. Everything is still on the table, and we'll see how he is come Tuesday or Wednesday - Adrian Keatley, trainer.

quotes.race: Northern Commercials New Buy From Stock EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Qual) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: We've liked Francisco's Piece for a long time and he's still very backward, in his coat and a little bit physically. When this fellow comes to himself and puts on a little bit more weight and really matured he's going to turn into a fine horse. I couldn't get my head away from him when I saw him at the sales. I hope he'll turn into a really good horse. I'm not in a mad hurry, the more time he gets he'll mature and get stronger - Adrian Keatley, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Smart 2yo; struggled in good handicaps last year but he has slipped down the weights and might well have needed the run when seventh of nine at Catterick on return; has possibilities if building on that.

stable_tour.quote: We've been waiting all year for the autumn and he could even end up being an Ayr Gold Cup horse. We ran him over 7f at Epsom and I don't think that's his trip. He's an out-and-out 6f horse who wants ease in the ground. His run at York recently will have sharpened him up. He's going to get an entry in the three-year-olds-only race at the Shergar Cup. He needs rain as he wants juice in the ground and, if he gets it, we'll be looking forward to running him there. 07-08-25

runners.comment: Ended 2025 in top form, winning twice, but has looked rusty on both starts this year
runners.name: Elegant Erin

prev_owners.owner: Pall Mall Partners And Sue Hopgood

quotes.race: Eddie And Violet Smith Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's massive really. Elegant Erin is honest, genuine and loves soft ground. Everything on paper was going to set up perfectly. I entered and then declared her because there weren't many runners. The handicapper then put her up 5lb this morning and I thought, we've probably got to run and I'm glad we did. We'll try to find some black type for her next. You'd love the Beverley Bullet to have been next week, but it's not, so we'll look elsewhere. She's very sound and I don't see why she shouldn't unless a silly offer comes for her - Paul Midgley, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 in top form, winning twice at Beverley (5f, soft), but she has looked rusty on both her starts this year; absent another seven weeks since her last run and probably best watched.

stable_tour.quote: She's an absolute sweetheart, I love her to bits. She's very honest and genuine and she's easy to train. The lack of early pace got her beaten at Pontefract last time and she has run well all year without winning, which is quite frustrating. She needs a proper end-to-end gallop over a stiff 5f. 14-08-25

runners.comment: Seems better on AW these days; poor efforts last two turf outings; others appeal more
runners.name: We Never Stop

quotes.race: BetUK All-Weather Sprint Handicap
quotes.quote: We Never Stop didn't have the best of draws but he has such a high cruising speed I was able to get him up there. The key to him is the first half of the race and getting him switched off - Shane Gray, jockey.

quotes.race: Gamble Responsibly At BetUK Handicap
quotes.quote: Everything fell into place today really. We Never Stop jumped well, and they went a blistering gallop, so I just sat off the lead a little bit and it worked out really well. I had something to aim at going to the furlong pole, and he had a good look when he got there, but he's done it comfortably in the end - Shane Gray, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Seems best on the AW these days and has run poorly on his last two turf outings, including here; others make more appeal.

runners.comment: Old-timer who notched win number 12 at Doncaster's Lincoln meeting; 4lb higher here
runners.name: Spoof

quotes.race: Boodles Diamond Handicap
quotes.quote: Callum gave Spoof a cracking ride as they went very fast up front and he was nice and patient on him. He's done well off top weight, he'll be up to a mark of near 100 now and we'll probably have to look down the Listed route. He's in the Dash, but it's not easy for 3yos against older horses - Charlie Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Watch Racing UK On Sky 432 Nursery Handicap (Jockey Club Grassroots Nursery Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I just had to keep Spoof as chilled as I could. He looks difficult but that was probably the best he's been. He's got a lot of ability, he travelled so well, and I didn't really have a choice but to go in the end. As soon as you do he runs about all over the place - he's a bit quirky - but he is a good horse, he's very quick - Callum Shepherd, rider.

runners.spotlight: Old-timer who notched win number 12 at Doncaster's Lincoln meeting (5f, good to soft; 40-1); can't be discounted off 4lb higher but others are still higher on the list.

15:15.race_name: William Hill Bronte Cup Fillies' Stakes (Group 3)

runners.comment: Runaway winner in big field on final 4yo start; the one to beat after a winter break
runners.name: Danielle

quotes.race: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Irish EBF Gillies Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Danielle has run with credit all season and she relished the conditions. She was the one to beat today. It was a drop in class for her - James Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: William Hill Oaks Trial Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Danielle ran fine, came down the hill well and just found the ground a little lively in the straight. She won on soft ground at Wetherby and loved it and we need to look for those conditions again - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Burrows Mazda York Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Danielle has improved from her last start, when she was run down by a filly who had been out previously [that season]. It was a good starting point, though. She had a good blow after the race, but she was always going to be a filly who improved markedly for the turf. She'll stay a mile and a half no problem, and I expect that's where the boss will be looking. Let's hope she keeps improving. We'll see how she comes out of the race. She probably had a harder race at Chelmsford last time, but went through the gears a lot better. She's improved a lot - Robert Havlin, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Likeable 5yo who signed off for last year with a demolition job on 17 rivals in Listed event at Doncaster (1m2f, heavy) in November; possibly ideally suited by the mud but drying ground should not inconvenience her unduly and she has made the frame in two Group 2 races over 1m6f; the one to beat if giving her running after a winter break.

runners.breeder: Miss K Rausing & Sunderland Holding Inc
runners.comment: Upwardly mobile 5yo; third in Group 3 at Ascot; should go well despite this shorter trip
runners.name: Miss Alpilles

quotes.race: Jockey Club Rose Bowl Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: When she was a two-year-old I thought she'd be our Oaks filly but she's been nothing but horrifically disappointing. Miss Alpilles finally won at Haydock and since then we always thought she wanted soft ground until Kieran Shoemark rode her at Ffos Las and said she hated soft. So we ran her on fast ground at Goodwood last time and here we are today. It's extraordinary - Ed Walker, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Upwardly mobile 5yo who seemed suited by the step up to 2m when winning Listed race at Newmarket (good) last autumn; ran creditably against male rivals when 8l third of eight in Group 3 Sagaro at Ascot on return; today's drop back in distance isn't an obvious positive but she may have more in the tank and should give a good account of herself.

stable_tour.quote: She did nothing wrong on fast ground at the end of last year. She relaxes well now and stays, so she'll start in the Sagaro Stakes at Ascot. She could be a fun mare for staying races. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Went close in Group 2 as 3yo; missed 2025 and seemed rusty on return; needs a leap forward
runners.name: Lava Stream

quotes.race: Ribblesdale Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
quotes.quote: We were surprised how well Lava Stream travelled. She got a perfect trip round and a great ride, so you can't be disappointed with that. She's very exciting and she's seen the trip out well, which looks perfect for her. We thought she'd be a black-type filly but she's probably exceeding our expectations. She's still lightly raced and a little bit raw; she'll improve - David O'Meara, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Went close in the Group 2 Ribblesdale (1m4f, good to firm) during a 3yo campaign that ended in the Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks; missed 2025 and shaped as if needing the run when beating only one home in Listed race at Nottingham (25-1) four weeks ago; usual hood is left off today; not ruled out but she'll have to make a major leap forward from her reappearance.

stable_tour.quote: She progressed very well last year and then had a little niggle towards the end. She showed a lot - and surprised us - when going so easily in the Ribblesdale and maybe hit the front a tad early. She's a Listed winner with plenty of ability and the aim would be to win a Group race. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Fourth in French Listed races; something to find on form but her fitness is guaranteed
runners.name: Desert Spring

prev_owners.owner: Elliott Bloodstock Services William Jackson-Stops & Monaugh

runners.spotlight: Stablemate of Danielle last season, winning 1m4f novice at Southwell; creditable fourth in French Listed races (10.5f/1m6f, good to soft/very soft) for new yard, rallying in latter; fair bit to find with the favourite but she's still relatively lightly raced and her fitness is guaranteed.

runners.comment: Has come up well short at Listed/Group 3 level and has a mountain to climb on form
runners.name: Miss Wong

quotes.race: British EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Miss Wong is bred to get better and there's a possibility for a step up in trip - that's when she'll come into her own - David Simcock, trainer.

runners.spotlight: From a useful middle-distance family and she won two handicaps at around 1m3f in the second half of 2025; however, she has come up well short in two attempts at Listed/Group 3 level, and she has a mountain to climb on form.

stable_tour.quote: She's from a family we know well given we trained her dam and she's related to Madame Chiang, who won for us on Champions Day in 2014. She's done everything right. 04-09-24"

runners.comment: All six wins in handicaps; faces much stiffer assignment on first attempt at a Group race
runners.name: Rock N Roll Pinkie

quotes.race: Skybet Proud To Support ROR Stayers Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Rock N Roll Pinkie is a filly who is improving. She's getting better with age, like an old wine. I think she's going to go to Nottingham for the staying final later this month, she won't mind a bit of cut in the ground and it's a good pot. The ground was quick enough today and a bit more cut will help her - Ivan Furtado, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Six wins (all handicaps) from 32 runs; not disgraced after losing ground at the start when fourth of six at Nottingham four weeks ago; faces a significantly stiffer assignment on her first attempt at a Group race.

runners.comment: Only seventh in Gowran Listed race last time and flying even higher today
runners.name: Tamam Desert
runners.spotlight: Often highly tried and unplaced all seven starts since winning a Galway maiden in September 2024; seemed to stay 1m6f in Gowran Listed race last time but still finished only seventh; flying even higher today.

runners.comment: Progressive; came to rear to win at Doncaster; retains potential and high on the list
runners.name: Reliable Ricki
runners.owner: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
runners.spotlight: Has progressed with every run and his form has a solid look; came from well back when leading late on at Doncaster (1m, good) at the start of this month; drops back 1f in trip but he's not short of speed; open to further improvement and high on the list.

runners.comment: Made it 3-3 on AW at Southwell last time but up 10lb and turf form is at much lower level
runners.name: Sporting Light
runners.owner: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd

prev_owners.owner: Sporting Life Racing Club - R Fahey

runners.spotlight: Made it 3-3 on AW with convincing success over this trip at Southwell two weeks ago; however, he's gone up 10lb and his turf form is at a much lower level.

runners.comment: Good third of 19 on handicap at Ascot; unexposed over this longer trip; leading contender
runners.name: Moscow Power
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced and unexposed; landed odds at Chelmsford (6f, AW) in March and the runner-up has boosted the form; beat all bar two of his 18 rivals in warm handicap at Ascot (6f, good) two weeks ago, doing his best work late on; should be suited by today's step up in distance; leading contender.

runners.comment: Reliable type; third over C&D at Dante meeting; another bold bid anticipated
runners.name: The Resdev Scholar
runners.owner: N Bradley 29 Resdev & South Bank Racing

prev_owners.owner: N Bradley Racing 29 & South Bank Racing

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: You can ride The Resdev Scholar however you want. He's been very consistent but he's really relished that soft ground - Joanna Mason, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Reliable type who again gave his running when third of 14 over C&D at the Dante meeting (good); nudged up 1lb but that should not prevent another bold bid.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khans Studs S C
runners.comment: Seemed suited by step up in trip when winning on stable debut at Catterick; this is warmer
runners.name: Zarvali

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan

runners.spotlight: Trained last year in Ireland by Johnny Murtagh; made an immediate impact for new yard when winning Catterick novice (7f, good) 12 days ago, seeming suited by the step up from sprint distances; may improve further but this is a fair bit warmer.

runners.comment: Wolverhampton maiden winner; this is tougher but he may not have reached his ceiling
runners.name: Cotai Eye Joe
runners.owner: Ursa Major Racing & Alfa Site Services
runners.spotlight: Looked green first two starts; improved a bit under positive ride when winning 11-runner maiden at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) last month; hardly looks thrown in for handicap/turf debut but he may not have reached his ceiling just yet.

runners.comment: 0-7 for the Crisfords; looks exposed unless a change of scenery gives him a lift
runners.name: Toastmaster
runners.spotlight: 0-7 for the Crisfords, only fifth of seven on turf debut at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) last month; looks exposed unless a change of scenery gives him a lift.

runners.comment: Followed good effort at Craven meeting with poor one at Guineas meeting; others preferred
runners.name: Stellar Vision
runners.spotlight: Free-goer who followed a good effort at Newmarket's Craven meeting (7f, good) with a poor one at the Guineas meeting; beginning to look a difficult ride and on a retrieval mission here.

runners.comment: Creditable fifth at Ascot last time and first-time cheekpieces could give him a boost
runners.name: Goldwork

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I'm going to think long and hard about Royal Ascot but we might come back here for Glorious Goodwood. We've always thought Goldwork is one of our best juveniles - Eve Johnson Houghton, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Proved his effectiveness over 7f when fifth of ten at Ascot (good ground) two weeks ago; others have more obvious potential but first-time cheekpieces could give him a boost.

stable_tour.quote: He finished eighth on his debut at Ascot in April and then won at Goodwood. He's a really nice horse and I'm very pleased with him. I'm looking to run him again but not sure where he'll go. I'll try to find a novice for him but I'd fancy him wherever he goes. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Two recent AW wins but mark has risen and he's 0-5 on turf
runners.name: Pints In Peace

prev_owners.owner: Arvin Savage & Ian Marmion & Justin L Murphy

runners.spotlight: Has been busy on the AW, winning over this trip at Wolverhampton in March and May; most recent success came in a weakish race and he's now up 6lb and back on turf (unplaced all five starts); enough doubts.

runners.comment: Gelded prior to making winning return in novice at Redcar; more persuasive than many
runners.name: Lucky Hero
runners.spotlight: 0-7 as 2yo but improved a bit for gelding operation when making winning reappearance in Redcar novice (7f, good to firm; 11-4) three weeks ago; may find a bit more and he's more persuasive than many.

runners.comment: Has not finished with much purpose on last two starts; needs a revival
runners.name: French Affair

quotes.race: Daily Bet Boosts At BetVictor Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: It's nice to get French Affair to win because he's been a little disappointing up to now. We gelded him and it's brought the best out of him - Richard Hannon, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Usually runs some sort of race but he has not finished with much purpose at Southwell (AW) or Lingfield (turf) on his last two starts, and this is more competitive; needs a revival.

runners.comment: Showed he retains ability with Beverley third; this is warmer but could make frame again
runners.name: Ubetterseethis
runners.spotlight: 1-13; showed he retains all his ability when third of ten at Beverley (7.4f, good to soft) on reappearance, in the firing line throughout; this is warmer but he could make the frame again.

runners.comment: Consistent filly; good-value claimer takes 7lb off; not ruled out each-way
runners.name: Sandy Craic
runners.spotlight: 0-6 but she's proving consistent and she was beaten off by the reopposing Zarvali only late on at Catterick (7f, good) 12 days ago; good-value claimer takes 7lb off; not ruled out each-way.

runners.comment: Treading water in sprint handicaps; hard to make a case for but this longer trip may suit
runners.name: Bye Law
runners.spotlight: Won Ayr maiden and Redcar novice (6f, good/good to firm) last summer but hasn't repeated the form in sprint handicaps; hard to make a case for but perhaps this step up in distance will suit.

runners.comment: Unplaced in three 7f novices this spring; needs a chunk of improvement on handicap debut
runners.name: Record Day
runners.spotlight: Unplaced in three 7f novices this spring, racing freely in rear on latest; needs a chunk of improvement on handicap debut, but market support would be significant.

runners.comment: Two places behind Goldwork when seventh at Ascot; needs positive reaction to the hood
runners.name: Illys Roo
runners.spotlight: All three wins have come over this trip but he finished two places behind Goldwork when only seventh of ten at Ascot two weeks ago; needs a positive reaction to the first-time hood.

stable_tour.quote: He's another horse who needs plenty of pace to aim at. He won at 28-1 at Southwell in March and I think he could pop up again when there's a race run to suit. He'll probably be aimed at some of the bigger handicaps where there's more chance to get that sort of pace angle for him. We have entered him at Chester - which I'm not terribly sure will suit - but he'll just run in any handicaps around 7f that have good prize-money and where it looks like they'll have a bit of pace. 06-05-26

runners.comment: No real impact in handicaps but at least he's now falling in the weights
runners.name: Harswell Angel

quotes.race: Watch Live On Racing TV EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't there, but I watched it on my phone and the only reason I can think of why we've kept the race is that we didn't touch the other horse in the last furlong, but it was a nervy wait. Harswell Angel had really bad colic earlier in the year. He had all sorts of problems, but we chucked him in a field for a bit and it seems to have worked - Roger Fell, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Progressive first three starts but he has not cut much ice in handicaps, fading into eighth at Wetherby on latest; at least the handicapper is cutting him some slack and the good recent form of his stable is a plus.

runners.comment: Rather fizzled out as 2yo and tailed off on return at Wetherby; difficult to recommend
runners.name: Dacres Cross
runners.spotlight: Rather fizzled out as a 2yo and he was tailed off on reappearance at Wetherby; difficult to recommend after that.

runners.comment: Two runs for current yard have been some way below par; needs to turn over a new leaf
runners.name: Try Storm Cat

quotes.race: EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Try Storm Cat has run well in defeat on both [previous] occasions and he deserved to get his head in front. We'll see what the handicapper does and what kind of mark but I think he will go another furlong and the seven-furlong nursery at Goodwood could be an option- Charlie Johnston, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Hasn't built on a 6f win at Pontefract last summer, and two runs for his current yard have been some way below par; falling in the weights but needs to turn over a new leaf.

runners.comment: Didn't go with much fluency when fourth of six at Musselburgh; more required
runners.name: Kanishka
runners.owner: C Booth P Boyle S Coleby & S Smith
runners.spotlight: In frame all three runs this year, although he didn't go with much fluency when fourth of six at Musselburgh (1m; wore cheekpieces) on latest; more required.

runners.comment: Incremental progress with each run, third on handicap debut at Newmarket; in the mix again
runners.name: Nanoscience

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Nanoscience has done it nicely and Oisin [Murphy, jockey] was very pleased with her. She's a lovely filly, well bred and I'm delighted for Kirsten [Rausing, owner] - Anna Lisa Balding, trainer's wife.

runners.spotlight: Incremental progress with each run, third of 11 on handicap debut at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) on latest; should be in the thick of things again provided her wide draw is no inconvenience.

runners.comment: Open to further improvement after Goodwood 1m2f win; 3lb rise probably underestimates him
runners.name: Bridge Of Eagles
runners.owner: C & L Washbourn And Mrs S Woodward
runners.spotlight: 11-2 for handicap/seasonal debut at Goodwood (1m2f, good) three weeks ago and showed improved form to come from off the pace and win narrowly; the runner-up went one better on Monday; open to further improvement and the 3lb rise will probably underestimate him.

runners.comment: Second in a warm 1m4f race here last week and shaped as if a return to 1m2f would be fine
runners.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners.spotlight: 33-1 winner of a 7f novice at Thirsk last September; improved form from off the pace again in all three handicaps since, this season's over 1m4f at Doncaster and York; the latter was a warm race in which he shaped as if a return to 1m2f would be fine; up 4lb but on the shortlist.

runners.comment: Not at all discredited at Chester latest and may resume his progress; cheekpieces go on
runners.name: Moment Of Light

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: I knew as soon as the race came out it was going to be a tactical affair that probably wouldn't see Moment Of Light to best effect. He's one who likes something to aim at and he likes an even-run race and that was never going to be the case today. He's galloped on strongly and when he felt the Gosden horse [Devil's Peak] he's drawn more out again - Luke Morris, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Gelded and tongue tied when justifying favouritism in five-runner handicaps over 1m3f on Kempton AW this February and April; raced a bit freely and never got into it when back to turf at Chester (1m4f, good; second favourite) 16 days ago but not at all discredited and it's possible he may resume his progress; cheekpieces go on.

runners.comment: Shaped as 2yo as if he'd prove capable of better, including at this trip; one to note
runners.name: Plan C
runners.spotlight: Fair form at Kempton (7f, AW) and Sandown (1m, soft; three ran) on his last two starts as 2yo and he shaped as if he'd prove capable of better, including at this trip; one to note on handicap/seasonal debut.

runners.comment: Led 3f out to 2f out before cracking behind Stoneacre Donny in 1m4f race here last week
runners.name: Pendella
runners.spotlight: Won one of four AW races to start career; 14-1 for turf debut in warm race here (1m4f, good) nine days ago, leading 3f out to 2f out before cracking and shaping like a non-stayer behind Stoneacre Donny; 5lb claimer is enlisted and this first go at 1m2f should suit.

runners.comment: Not discredited when up against it both starts this term and this is much more realistic
runners.name: Pearl River
runners.spotlight: All seven races on good or softer; 1m2f suited him well on final two runs as 2yo, culminating in a Nottingham handicap win; not discredited when up against it on his two starts this term and this is much more realistic, but he still needs better.

runners.comment: 106 days off when severely disappointing on handicap/turf debut (1m4f, good to firm)
runners.name: Alba Gu Brath
