runners.spotlight: Two seconds and a win (hung left) to start his career this winter on AW, all over 1m; many from this stable bounce back but, notwithstanding the 106 days off, last month's handicap/turf debut at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) looked severely disappointing.

stable_tour.quote: He won his novice over a mile but is shaping as though he'll be better when stepped up to a mile and a quarter, and he may well get a mile and a half come the summer. He's a colt we've always liked and strikes me as one of those three-year-old middle-distance handicappers that we tend to do well with. 21-04-26

runners.comment: This trip is worth a go judged on 1m reappearance but he needs to raise his game markedly
runners.name: Mr Seagull
runners.owner: Two Plus Three Two Plus Four
runners.spotlight: Made bright start as 2yo, before well beaten at big prices in two sales races in September; gelded and wore cheekpieces on handicap/seasonal debut at Haydock (1m, good to firm; 18-1) four weeks ago, when keeping on into fourth as if this trip is worth a go, but he needs to raise his game markedly.

runners.comment: Fifth of six in hot race for handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good) was his highest rating
runners.name: Magic Trip
runners.spotlight: Won at Bath (1m, good to soft) last September on the first of his four starts; prominent long way and took a bump in the closing stages when fifth of six in a hot race for handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good) last time, which was his highest rating and he can probably do better still.

runners.comment: Weakening here last week when perhaps both in need of the race and stretched by 1m4f
runners.name: Northern Brave
runners.spotlight: Ran twice over 1m at Ayr last autumn, on second occasion stretching 5l clear when 2-7 in a four-runner novice (heavy); made his reappearance in a warm handicap here last week, weakening markedly behind Stoneacre Donny but perhaps both in need of the race (28-1) and stretched by the 1m4f; better may well be forthcoming this time.

runners.comment: Pedigree and manner of 1m novice win suggest that this step up in trip will suit him well
runners.name: Simon Pierre
runners.spotlight: Showed promise on debut in March and justified market interest to win from off the pace in a seven-runner novice at Thirsk (1m, good) six weeks ago, form which has been boosted; pedigree and manner of that win suggest that this step up in trip will suit him well for handicap debut; considered.

stable_tour.quote: He debuted at Doncaster and he jumped too well from the stalls and ran too gassy that day. But he was seen to much better effect on his second start at Thirsk when he got up late over a mile to win. He's been given an opening mark of 77 and will hopefully head to Ascot on Saturday for a 1m2f handicap. I'm looking forward to seeing what he can do up in trip. 06-05-26

17:00.race_name: William Hill Boosts Every Day Handicap

runners.comment: Huge player but plenty needs to go right; it didn't when 2nd of 22 over C&D eight days ago
runners.name: Leadman
runners.spotlight: Has an underwhelming strike-rate, given his ability, but he was second of 22 off a good mark over C&D eight days ago and would surely have gone very close had he not met trouble in running from well off the pace; the problems today are that he's back up 4lb, drawn even wider and has another big field to negotiate his way through; huge player but plenty needs to go right.

stable_tour.quote: New to us from Andrew Balding's, we bought him as a maiden and haven't run him, but he's still won a race since. It was a disqualification, so he's no longer a maiden. He's got ability but might have a soft temperament. 14-04-25

runners.comment: Both races were 7f novices on Newcastle AW, clearcut winner on second occasion; potential
runners.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners.spotlight: Both races were 7f novices on Newcastle AW, showing promise in September and winning in clearcut style in November; has a useful pedigree and brings clear potential but 22-runner race is something of a baptism of fire for this handicap and turf debut.

runners.comment: Disappointing at Yarmouth last time but she's from a yard which is in fine form
runners.name: Lady Mariko
runners.spotlight: Dual 7f turf winner last summer who overcame the drop back to 6f at Kempton (AW) in April; disappointing at Yarmouth three weeks later but she's from a yard which is in fine form.

runners.comment: Plenty of C&D form in big fields, including his fifth of 22 eight days ago
runners.name: Quest For Fun
runners.spotlight: Plenty of C&D form in big fields, notably wins on good to soft in 2023 and July 2025; while not so striking as Leadman, he didn't have the best of runs when fifth of 22 over C&D eight days ago, so might step up a bit today.

stable_tour.quote: He loves a bit of juice in the ground and seven furlongs or an easy mile. I think he could improve again this year, Lope De Vegas tend to do that. 23-04-24

runners.comment: Still paying for the ease of his Epsom win last August, so others are preferred
runners.name: Silver Trumpet
runners.spotlight: All his wins have been over 7f but there's been only one of those (Epsom last August) in very nearly two years now; still paying for the ease of that win in a seven-runner race, so others are preferred.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Salisbury last year but I think the handicapper got hold of him a bit - he went up 9lb for his win. He's had a wind op and I put him at Newbury on Tuesday. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Two wins and a 2nd from his four starts for new stable; could still be capable of better
runners.name: Rascal Recknell

quotes.race: Stay Golden With BetMGM Safer Gambling Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Rascal Recknell is a young schoolboy. I think seven furlongs is his trip but he's getting the idea of racing now. It wasn't the cleanest of races and I wouldn't say this was his ideal track but he knuckled down hard to the line - Benoit de la Sayette, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Two wins (one on turf at Doncaster) and a second from his four starts for new stable this season, all in 7f handicaps; failed to settle last time, yet still challenged strongly in the final 1f and left the impression he remains capable of better.

runners.comment: 0-11 on turf but has been close up; another AW win last time and he's 6lb lower today
runners.name: Beale Street
runners.spotlight: Last of 20 over 6f last May on his only race here, before finishing on the heels of the leaders twice over 7f at Doncaster; 0-11 on turf and not the most consistent but he won at Newcastle on two of his last three AW starts and the latest was over 7f; 6lb lower today and needs a close look.

runners.comment: Stays 7f; 0-13 in handicaps and others present stronger cases despite his career-low mark
runners.name: Modern Times
runners.spotlight: Won a 6f Ripon maiden last June and stays 7f; 0-13 in handicaps, however, and others present stronger cases despite his career-low mark.

runners.comment: Career-best form in two close calls on AW but this turf race surely demands better still
runners.name: Jersey Maverick
runners.owner: Tim Cottier Clark Spence And Fellowes
runners.spotlight: 15 races for one win, at Epsom (7f, good to firm; from 9lb lower) last July; faced 7f on AW for last four starts, with career-best form in two close calls, the latest under Mikkel Mortensen at Southwell late last month but today's stronger race for return to turf surely demands better still.

runners.comment: All five starts have been on AW; flop in 7f handicap last time; gelded and absent 11 weeks
runners.name: Inspired
runners.owner: Fine Claret RacingMrs Burke & C Wood

prev_owners.owner: Fine Claret RacingMrs Burke & C Wood

runners.spotlight: All five starts have been on AW, with some pretty useful form over 1m at Newcastle this winter before a flop in 7f handicap at Chelmsford; gelded and absent in the 11 weeks since; drawn wide; well bred (albeit for much longer trips) and lightly raced for his leading yard but plenty to prove today.

runners.comment: A case can be made but others have a bit less to prove in this big-field scenario
runners.name: Signcastle City
runners.spotlight: Drew a blank last year but came down the weights, won over 7f on AW in February and competitive over 1m in two recent outings; case can be made but others have a bit less to prove in this big-field scenario.

runners.comment: Made a respectable return to action one month ago and enters each-way calculations
runners.name: Highfield Viking
runners.spotlight: Gained last year's two wins over 7f on good ground in August and came second in a 15-runner race next time; made a respectable return to action one month ago and enters each-way calculations.

stable_tour.quote: He's a half-brother to Highfield Princess, who improved from three to four and beyond, and I'd like to think he'll improve further and make up into a solid handicapper. He's by Aclaim and we've found his progeny act with a bit of juice in the ground. We tried him visored on his last run as he can race lazily in the middle of a race and I'd have thought we'll continue that unless he sharpens up. 20-03-24

runners.comment: Back from longest break in two years; has to be considered, though, off last winning mark
runners.name: Feel The Need

quotes.race: Andy Thornton Hospitality Furniture 50th Anniversary Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: I saw the favourite coming on my outside and thought I'd take a soft lead. I was edging closer and closer and if it was a bit softer, Feel The Need would have won better. He's a very genuine horse. He loves this track and keeps on getting better with age - Andrea Pinna, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Most of his 14 races at York have been over 7f, including wins in this race in 2024 and another last June; absent since second on AW in January and that's the longest break he's had for two years, which asks a question, but he has to be considered off his last winning mark.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well on his return and can take a step forward from that. There are some nice races for him this month and there should be plenty of improvement to come. 04-05-23

runners.comment: He has not been far away in any of his races this year, so has place claims
runners.name: Commander Of Life

quotes.race: PPM Barnsley Handicap
quotes.quote: My plan was always to take my time as we knew there was going to be a good gallop. Commander Of Life is a horse who has got a lot of ability but he has to come with one run and you really cannot get there until the furlong pole. He did it really nicely in the end - Finley Marsh, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Not far away in one of these big-field C&D races last July; showed at Doncaster that month that he can win on turf and he's not been far away in any of his races this year, so he has place claims.

runners.comment: Just five races; 2nd three times, including on handicap debut at Nottingham (1m, good)
runners.name: Pulsar Star
runners.spotlight: Just five races, the first two for James Tate; runner-up three times, including on handicap debut in nine-runner race at Nottingham (1m, good) five weeks ago; return to 7f may well be fine and he's relatively unexposed, but taking on so many rivals from almost the widest draw asks a major question.

runners.comment: 2nd in this in 2024 but below form last week and her last two wins were in small fields
runners.name: Mereside Diva

quotes.race: Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Mereside Diva is improving all the time and thriving. She's been progressing nicely since stepping up to seven furlongs. When she was still a bit raw, you'd go for her and she'd prick her ears and have a look, but she's really game now and sticking to her task well - Callum Rodriguez, speaking to ITV Racing.

quotes.race: Pertemps Handicap
quotes.quote: We kept thinking Mereside Diva would improve for the step up to seven furlongs and she stayed the trip well. She's run a lot on bad ground, but she handles this fine and seemed to travel on it well - Nicola Barron, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Brannans Have Done The 61 Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: I had to switch Mereside Diva a couple of times because I hit a couple of wet patches that knocked her momentum, but she's tough and she dug it out well - Rossa Ryan, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Second when favourite for this race in 2024, with mixed fortunes in her five subsequent C&D appearances but she was a creditable third last June; seen in regular action this year, including when second at Wetherby last month but not so good here eight days ago; her last two wins (2024 and this February) were in small fields, so others make more appeal today.

runners.comment: Fourth and fifth in his two big-field C&D races last term; no daylight here last week
runners.name: Havana Prince

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV In Stunning HD Handicap
quotes.quote: Havana Prince is a grand little horse. He may not be the classiest, but he makes up for that by being tough and genuine. That was as quick ground as he wants and you won't be seeing him again until there's a bit of rain. He loves Redcar and Ripon, so we'll wait for the rain and won't have to go out of Yorkshire to find more winning opportunities - Tony Coyle, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Amy Washbourne Bloom Digitally Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: I would have been unlucky as I got hampered out of the gate and Havana Prince had to work hard to get into a good position. I thought we got racing plenty early and I needed the line in the last fifty yards - David Nolan, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Fourth and fifth in his two big-field C&D races last term; Newcastle win in March ensures a career-high mark today but it's hard to judge him harshly on last week's C&D result as he didn't see daylight at various stages.

runners.comment: Off since January win (yard debut); more to prove back at 7f for the first time since 2024
runners.name: Paladin

quotes.race: Free Tips Daily On attheraces.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Paladin has been disappointing since he came back from quite a long spell off. We thought a lot of him as a youngster but he's dropped a long way in class and nothing seemed to be going right for him so it's great to see him coming back to something like his old form - Mark Johnston, trainer's representative, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Free-going sort who was 4-18 for Charlie Johnston, including two 1m wins last summer, and made a winning start for new connections when 33-1 for a nine-runner race at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in January; absent since and has more to prove back at 7f for the first time since 2024.

runners.comment: Did well at 7f on AW once fitted with a visor; return to turf in March bore no comparison
runners.name: Golden Strike

quotes.race: Yorkshire Accountants Ripon Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It felt like they were going quite quick and Golden Strike was flat out after about fifty yards. I didn't want to put him on his head as he was a little bit unbalanced so I kept trying to fill him up and in the last furlong he came good. He's a lovely horse who is still a big baby and he'll improve for the run - Billy Garritty, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: First time out Golden Strike ran a good race and he's come forward from it. There was no real pace but I was able to let him lob away in front and when I asked him he's quickened up and done it nicely. I'd say he'll get further in time but for the minute he seems OK at that trip (6f). He's a big, good-looking horse and I think there's plenty to look forward with him - Oisin Orr, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Record of 122 over 7f on AW once fitted with a visor; however, despite turf achievements early in career, his return to turf at Doncaster (7f, good to soft; second favourite) in March bore no comparison.

runners.comment: Competitive mark but other cases look a bit more solid, particularly as he's drawn wide
runners.name: Follow Your Heart
runners.spotlight: Behind on his only run here (2023); Doncaster last June saw his only turf win since 2021, amidst plenty of AW success admittedly but he was out of form in February when last seen; has a competitive mark but other cases look a bit more solid, particularly as he's drawn wide.

runners.comment: 13yo who is 13lb lower than this time last year, but his last turf win was in 2022
runners.name: Documenting
runners.owner: Kevin Frost Racing Club & Mike Humphries

prev_owners.owner: Kf Racing Humphreys Orr Glover Priest
Kf Racing Club Humphreys Jones And Orr

quotes.race: Play Pick 6 At BetVictor Handicap
quotes.quote: The faster the ground, the better Documenting is. The one worry was no pace and it'd be tactical, but Jack knows him well and Able Kane gave us something to aim at. He's a tough dude and we put him in the Ayr Gold Cup because I'd love to see him in an eyeballs-out six-furlong race. I've never seen him off the bridle early in the race and it's an option if the ground's quick - Kevin Frost, trainer.

quotes.race: sunracing.co.uk Handicap
quotes.quote: I had a lovely run round the inside - it was very straightforward. Kevin [Frost] was very pleased with how Documenting was before the race - Jack Mitchell, jockey

quotes.race: Visit mymedsuk.com Maiden Stakes
quotes.quote: Documenting has got a fantastic pedigree and we bought him for just 1,000 guineas out of Juddmonte as he has obviously had problems. He can only come on for the win - Kevin Frost, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 13yo who has won on 12 occasions, the latest in December 2024 and his C&D win came before most of today's rivals were born; not disgraced on reappearance and he's now 13lb lower than this time last year, but his last turf win was in 2022; not the percentage call.

runners.comment: C&D winner; 1lb lower than when making all at Beverley last September; case can be made
runners.name: It Just Takes Time

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Training Series Final Apprentice Handicap (Part Of The Racing Excellence Series) (Div II)
quotes.quote: It Just Takes Time made it look easy and relished the ground. It slowed the others down but he's a very simple ride. I popped him out and drop the hands and that's his style. He hits a flat spot but never gives up. He's very game - Olivia Tubb, jockey.

quotes.race: Joe Rowntree Memorial Handicap
quotes.quote: It Just Takes Time is still progressing now we have found out how we can keep him settled down. He did that well enough. That was the perfect distance and a sharp 7f suits him well - Jack Garritty, jockey.

runners.spotlight: C&D winner in 2022, with no joy from nine subsequent visits but most of those were over shorter, whereas his last four wins (elsewhere) have been at about 7f; he's now 1lb lower than when making all at Beverley last September and a case can be made.

13:50.race_name: Bangor-On-Dee Ladies Day Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Useful bumper performer who was runner-up on hurdling debut at Fakenham; key player
runners.name: Ladies Day
runners.spotlight: Finished second in three of her last four bumpers including a Listed mares' event at Huntingdon in December; runner-up again on recent hurdling debut at Fakenham (2m4f, good) and that was a promising effort behind an 11-10 favourite who made all; sets a fair standard on that form and she's a big player back in trip.

runners.breeder: S C E A De La Vallee De LOrne
runners.comment: Has been progressive over hurdles and her latest third at Fontwell can be marked up
runners.name: Mega Etoile
runners.spotlight: Has improved with each of her three hurdle runs and her latest third of 14 at Fontwell (2m1f, good) can be marked up because she had traffic issues in the closing stages and got hit by a rival's whip; could continue to progress with experience and she's an interesting contender.

runners.comment: Irish point winner; flopped here in March but was reported to have an irregular heartbeat
runners.name: Double Indemnity
runners.spotlight: Bought for £30,000 after winning an Irish point; runner-up on hurdle debut at Carlisle (2m1f, good to soft) in February but he was pulled up here (2m3f, good) the following month and was reported to have an irregular heartbeat; has bit to prove after that but it's still early days and he's in good hands; stablemate of Earnest Belief.

runners.comment: Disappointing at Hexham (3-1) three weeks ago and this looks tough on the figures
runners.name: Earnest Belief
runners.spotlight: 0-6 on Flat for the Gosdens; encouraging third on hurdling/stable debut at Carlisle (2m1f, good to soft) in March but he failed to build on that when a remote fourth at Hexham (2m, good); has something to prove after that and this looks tough on the figures; equipment returns including a first-time tongue-tie.

runners.comment: 0-8 on the Flat and was well held on hurdling debut at Fontwell two weeks ago
runners.name: Chambers
runners.spotlight: Eight-race maiden on the Flat and was a well-held sixth of 14 on hurdling debut at Fontwell (2m1f, good) two weeks ago; passed over.

runners.comment: Failed to beat a rival in two bumpers and now goes hurdling after a year off; best watched
runners.name: Happy Harrison
runners.spotlight: Failed to beat a rival in two good-ground bumpers six months apart; now goes hurdling after 375 days off and he can only be watched.

stable_tour.quote: He's finished last in both his bumper starts. He had his wind done after his debut and then he fractured a joint on his second start. He's had time off and is working really nicely. I'm looking forward to getting him back on the track and he could be a dark horse. 08-04-26

runners.comment: 0-9 on the Flat and she makes no appeal now switched to hurdling after a long absence
runners.name: Winter Life
runners.spotlight: 0-9 on the Flat and was tailed off at 150-1 in both runs (1m4f/1m6f) for current yard in October 2024; makes no appeal now switched to hurdling after 576 days off.

runners.comment: Tailed off at big prices in two hurdle runs (1m7f/2m, good) this spring
runners.name: Go Try
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to the useful Perfect Myth but he's been tailed off at big prices in two hurdle runs (1m7f/2m, good) this spring.

runners.comment: Promise in bumpers early in 2025; due to make hurdling debut at Worcester on Friday night
runners.name: Kind Intention
runners.spotlight: Definite promise in all three bumpers that were won by smart horses, including Storming George and Mydaddypaddy; should have a future over hurdles but he was due to make his comeback in a Worcester maiden on Friday night (7.11).

14:25.race_name: Wrexham Lager Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Dual winner over hurdles; has fallen in two of her three runs over fences.
runners.name: Mary
runners.spotlight: Both wins over hurdles came when making all; yet to convince as a chaser, falling in two of her three starts in this sphere; a clear round would be a priority.

runners.breeder: E A R L Ecurie Des Mottes
runners.comment: Irish point winner whose best effort over fences was when second at Doncaster in February.
runners.name: Kadjar Des Mottes
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner whose best effort over fences was when second of four finishers at Doncaster (3m, soft) in February; unseated early on the following month and well beaten over hurdles since; first-time cheekpieces are now fitted; may need softer ground to be seen to advantage.

runners.comment: Point winner who got off the mark over fences at Huntingdon in March.
runners.name: Big Boy Barney
runners.spotlight: Point winner who got off the mark over fences on his second attempt, at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March; third on both starts since and first-time cheekpieces are now employed along with regular tongue-tie; should be thereabouts.

runners.comment: Finished well when third at Chepstow last month.
runners.name: Le Gentleman
runners.owner: The North West National Hunt Racing Club

prev_owners.owner: Lord Daresbury Ecurie Madame Jacques Cypres & Mme F Cypres

runners.spotlight: Formerly trained in France, he finished well when third of four finishers at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) last month on his second run in Britain; should be suited by this step up in trip but has never run on ground without soft in the description.

runners.comment: Won a maiden hurdle, but has failed to make an impact in her two starts over fences.
runners.name: Herja
runners.spotlight: Won a 2m4f Sedgefield maiden hurdle last September, but has failed to make an impact in her two starts over fences; has another go on her handicap debut but will need to improve.

runners.comment: Has a mixed hurdling record but got her second win in that sphere at this track last July.
runners.name: Wudya
runners.spotlight: Has a mixed hurdling record but landed her second win in that sphere at this track (2m3f, good) last July; catching her fresh may be the answer and she's interesting on chasing debut.

stable_tour.quote: She's just back into work now. She stopped because she wants good ground and she'll be a summer jumps type. It looks like she wants 2m-2m4f and she'll be ready in the spring. 28-01-26

runners.comment: A dual winning pointer, he was a runner-up over hurdles at Warwick and Taunton this year.
runners.name: Bobbarelli
runners.spotlight: A dual winning pointer, his only outing over fences came when pulling up in a hunter chase at Cheltenham in May 2025; a runner-up over hurdles at Warwick and Taunton this year, he should run well.

15:00.race_name: Cheshire Oaks Designer Outlet Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Returned from long absence with a second at Southwell; dangerous if he can build on that
runners.name: Copper Beach
runners.spotlight: Record of 1-18 over hurdles but he returned after 510 days off with a second at Southwell (2m4f, good) two weeks ago; that was a good effort behind an improver and he's a player if he can build on that.

runners.comment: Record of 11142132 for current yard and latest second was back over hurdles; key player
runners.name: Orange Diamond
runners.spotlight: Has record of 11142132 for his current yard, with those first three wins over hurdles at Worcester (2m4f) and his last success over fences at Market Rasen (2m7f); up another 3lb after his second over hurdles at Warwick (2m3f, good) last month, but he went down fighting after making a mistake at the last; could still have more to offer and he's a big player.

runners.comment: Flopped in final run last year but she's still lightly raced; needs a close look on return
runners.name: Back In The Bay
runners.owner: Value Racing - Back In The Bay
runners.spotlight: Made it 2-5 over hurdles when landing a mares' handicap at Stratford (2m3f, good) last July but she flopped in a three-runner race in final run last year; has bit to prove after 218 days but she has potential in this sphere and needs a close look in market.

runners.breeder: Aston Mullins Stud & S Barrow Esq
runners.comment: On reduced mark and he wasn't beaten far at Uttoxeter (2m4f) last time; in the mix
runners.name: Torrent
runners.spotlight: Got off to a flyer when winning two of his first three starts over hurdles in 2024; has drawn a blank since but he's on a reduced mark and wasn't beaten far when fourth at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) three weeks; has possibilities if he can build on that and he's in the mix.

runners.comment: Only 1lb higher than for last win but needs to rediscover her spark after six months off
runners.name: Crystal Glance
runners.spotlight: Record of 4-12 over hurdles but she was vulnerable in her final three runs last year including over C&D (good); now only 1lb higher than for her last success but she needs to rediscover her spark after six months off.

stable_tour.quote: We gave her a break over the winter because she loves good ground and she'll go on through the summer now. She pings off that type of ground and sharp tracks are right up her street. We'll aim for hurdle races over 2m and 2m4f. We might have a go over fences but she's not the biggest, so we'll see. 13-03-26

runners.comment: May have needed his reappearance run at Worcester and has claims if back near best
runners.name: Play Pretend
runners.spotlight: Won at Worcester (2m, good) last July and he ended last year with two close calls over 2m4f; well-held fifth on reappearance at Market Rasen last month but he may have needed that run and has claims if he can get back near best.

runners.comment: Dual hurdle winner but he's lost his way in last two starts and needs a big turnaround
runners.name: Magic Wave
runners.spotlight: Won off 2lb lower at Kelso (2m5f, good) last April but he's not seen much action since and has been beaten 39l in both runs this year; has some questions to answer and he needs a big turnaround.

runners.comment: Bit to prove but has possibilities if she can get back on track after wind surgery
runners.name: The Secret Pearl
runners.spotlight: Won a mares' maiden at Market Rasen (2m, good) last April; runner-up in first two handicaps during the winter but she's been disappointing in last two runs; bit to prove but mark is sliding and she's had wind surgery since her latest effort at Fontwell last month; not ruled out.

runners.comment: Won over C&D last April but he's not come close to that form in four subsequent runs
runners.name: Rock Hurley

prev_owners.owner: Mr & Mrs G Calder & P M Warren
S Dufresne B Milpied & G Luyckx

runners.spotlight: Won a C&D handicap (good to soft) last April but he's not come close to that form in four subsequent runs and latest was back here in March; has some questions to answer and he's still 3lb higher than for his last win.

runners.comment: Very lightly raced 11yo who has something to prove after another absence; cheekpieces on
runners.name: Sauce Of Life
runners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars And Miss D C Sellars

prev_owners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars & Major Philip Arkwright

quotes.race: 2025 Annual Membership Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Sauce Of Life has had his issues over the years but his owners have given him plenty of time and now they're starting to get the rewards. He just took his time to get into top gear but, once he did, he was away and gone - Danny McMenamin, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Unbeaten in bumpers (2-2) and very lightly raced for his age; won a hurdle handicap at Doncaster (2m4f, good to soft) in December 2024 but he's had only two runs since and has struggled in both of them; has something to prove after another absence and he needs first-time cheekpieces to work.

stable_tour.quote: The slow gallop didn't help him at all on his first run over hurdles at Wetherby. He jumped well, travelled strongly, but it turned into a sprint and it caught him out for a furlong until he got himself gathered up and realised he had to change a couple of gears. The race was over then, but he's come back all right and should be winning plenty of races. 22-11-21

He won both his bumper starts and then finished placed twice over hurdles, the form of which has worked out well. We'll get him back over hurdles in about a month's time. He has plenty of ability if we can keep the wheels on him. 25-10-23

15:32.race_name: F Jones Initiative Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Resumed winning ways at Chepstow last month.
runners.name: Supreme George
runners.spotlight: Has taken well to fences and completed a three-timer at Catterick in January; resumed winning ways at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) last month and this front-runner may prove hard to peg back.

runners.breeder: G F A Du Pont Rouge
runners.comment: Won over fences at Ludlow last October and has been placed on all five starts since.
runners.name: Gris Majeur
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Brian Davies

quotes.race: Great Outdoors INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: He has settled into the routine very well and his work had been very good at home. He won a point-to-point at Fairyhouse and for this time of the year he is a bit better than them. I imagine he will go on a bit softer ground - rider Jamie Codd.

runners.spotlight: Got off the mark over fences at Ludlow (2m4f, good to firm) last October and has been placed on all five starts since; drops back in trip which may not be in his favour.

runners.comment: Has five wins over fences, the latest at Sedgefield last September off 5lb lower.
runners.name: Jet Of Dreams

quotes.race: Royal Oak At Hillcommon Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was like a piece of work for Jet Of Dreams. He sometimes goes left anyway and especially when he's in front he's going to do it more so I just left him drift over that way. The things in front of me were the only things that were going to get me beat - James Bowen, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Has five wins over fences, the latest at Sedgefield last September off 5lb lower; should strip fitter for a recent fourth over hurdles but may need to come down a few pounds.

runners.comment: Won twice over fences at around this trip last spring; not so good since.
runners.name: Yes Indeed
runners.spotlight: Won twice over fences at around this trip last spring; not so good since but is 1lb lower than his last winning mark so cannot be ruled out.

stable_tour.quote: It was a respectable run in a fair race at Carlisle the other day. He jumped nicely and did everything right. Perhaps a flatter track might suit better but I wouldn't be afraid to run him anywhere and that run gives us something to build on. 14-11-23

He's a lovely big horse. He had his first run at Chepstow and just needed that. It was over hurdles and there weren't any chases for him. We're looking forward to running him back over fences and he could win a few this season. He's on a decent mark. 12-11-25

runners.comment: Dual 1m4f Flat winner (made all) and Summer Hurdle third last year; goes well fresh.
runners.name: Nibras Gold

quotes.race: Ladies Day 26th August Handicap
quotes.quote: Nibras Gold's an improving horse as well as being gelded. He thinks he's done when he hits the front but the horse who creeped up my inside made him go again. He makes hard work of it - Ray Dawson, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Dual 1m4f Flat winner (made all) and Summer Hurdle third last year, and jumped perfectly well when second on two of three chase starts in summer 2024; record of 62121 when returning from breaks of over 200 days.

runners.comment: Won five times when trained in France; first win in Britain came at Cartmel last August.
runners.name: Dexter

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late C J Leech

runners.spotlight: Won five times when trained in France; first win in Britain came at Cartmel (2m1f, good) last August; has run well when in the frame since but was beaten 30l back over hurdles when last seen in November; may be better for the run.

runners.comment: Pulled up on his chase debut at Uttoxeter three weeks ago.
runners.name: Start Again
runners.spotlight: Exeter maiden hurdle winner in October; pulled up on his chase debut at Uttoxeter three weeks ago; best watched.

runners.comment: Back to form with creditable fifth at Aintree last month; dangerous with cheekpieces added
runners.name: Cruz Control

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted to be able to get Cruz Control back on track - he'd completely lost his way. He ran ok in Punchestown, and Stan [Sheppard, jockey] just said to me afterwards, 'He's proper tired', and it's taken until now to get him really back on song. We mixed it up at home - took him to the beach, jumped the Aintree fences at Lambourn with him, and I'm so delighted for the owners, who are great supporters of mine. We've sweetened him up - did more slow work, gave him some away days, and the sun on his back - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Handicap Chase (Registered As The Freebooter Handicap Chase) (Premier Handicap) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Cruz Control missed the ditch in the home straight the second time but otherwise he jumped pretty economically, fast and effectively. It was a good performance. He was unlucky to lose at Doncaster and he got chinned at Newcastle on another occasion but otherwise he's not done a lot wrong this season. He appears to be slow but he's such a big, long-striding horse he's covering ground - he's taking one stride to other horses' two. I've been reluctant to step him up to three miles because although he's seven he's still a frame. We've given him time to mature and I think he'll just get better and better, hopefully - Tom Lacey, trainer.

quotes.race: Sportvision Stadia & Event Branding Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Cruz Control jumped much better compared to how he jumped at Ascot, where he was just running into fences. We did a load of schooling with him at home over some poles and he's tucking his front end up so much better. He's a horse that's still to do some maturing - he's got such a big frame and has been such a hollow horse - and hopefully he can go on from here. If he can jump with accuracy he could go up in trip - Tom Lacey, trainer, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cruz Control is a fine horse. Two-and-a-half miles around Cheltenham just didn't suit him and he jumped okay today, but I got a free lead. It's a cliche but we'll see the best of him over a fence - Stan Sheppard, rider.

runners.spotlight: Took big step back in right direction when fifth at Aintree (3m1f, good to soft) last month, in race he won the previous two seasons; still on a workable mark and has a fighting chance here if first-time cheekpieces have any positive effect.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big, tall, angular type who has done nothing wrong, winning his bumper and scoring twice over hurdles. However, he's always been a real chaser in the making and got off the mark on his third attempt over fences at Newcastle, where I was much happier with his jumping following plenty of schooling. He followed that up with a good second at Doncaster on Saturday and the result might have been different had he been a little bit quicker over the last few fences. He'll get better in time, is constantly filling his frame and seems to handle most ground. I think he's progressive. 20-12-23

runners.comment: Struggled in the Grand National but he's interesting back in calmer waters at this trip
runners.name: Twig

quotes.race: William Hill Half A Mill Becher Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Twig's run a blinder, Beau gave him a lovely ride and he jumped for fun. He just got lonely in front. He didn't get involved in the National, he plugged on and ran well, but you can't run like that in a National these days. He'll go up enough to get in again, so we'll see as I was thinking about the veterans final - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Oddschecker Veterans' Handicap Chase (Leg 8 Of The Stayers' Veterans' Chase Series)
quotes.quote: Twig is class; all last season was about trying to get him in the National, we got him in and he never really got into the race but finished beautifully to be tenth. We were delighted with him there and it's great to see him back. It was quite a hilarious race to watch; it changed complexion at least five times, but it's great. Hopefully, we can pop about in some of those sorts of races, maybe try him at the cross-country as well - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: This morning we were debating even running Twig, he wants better ground. But we thought we could go here and prep him for Aintree and he's run like that. I'm absolutely delighted - Beau Morgan, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: bet365 Summer Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: When I originally trained Twig for his previous owners, who bred him, he just wasn't physically ready. I didn't think he was going to be a racehorse and that's why I sent him off into the point-to-point field, and he's just improved and improved - Ben Pauling, trainer.

quotes.race: Download The BetVictor App "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Twig is very consistent at a decent level and is possibly a better chaser than he is a hurdler, but we're trying to give Beau some good experience on a nice horse. The horse is going the right way and we might chuck him in something better towards the end of the season; he's a flat track, better-ground type - Ben Pauling, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Second at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival and he started last season with two wins, including a gritty success in the Becher at Aintree (3m2f); struggled in the Grand National last month but he's now only 2lb higher than for his last win and looks interesting on this drop back in trip and class; last success was on soft but most of his wins have been on good ground.

stable_tour.quote: He's going to go for some veterans' chases and we'll possibly look at the Becher. I was delighted with his run in the National considering they went a million miles an hour from the start and he was struggling. He's not done with yet - he's got plenty to give in his own grade. 07-11-25

He joined us earlier this autumn and his three runs have been very encouraging. He finished second to Found On at Worcester first time out for us. We then went to Warwick this month where he got his head in front in a 3m novice handicap chase. He reverted to hurdles at Cheltenham on Friday and ran well to finish second to Shearer in a novice (well clear of the third). He would not want the ground too soft and I would anticipate a small break over the Christmas/New Year period. He will be an interesting runner when he returns in early spring. 26-10-22

runners.comment: Made it 5-16 over fences when scoring at Newton Abbot (2m5f); respected back up in trip
runners.name: Somespring Special

quotes.race: NAF Mares' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: That was very good. Somespring Special is better on that ground and I was really pleased with how she travelled and went like a two-miler - at Plumpton she found it all very fast. She was economical over her fences too. It was a bit of a chuckaway entry at first but when she won at Plumpton we thought she had to run. I was shocked by her price, I usually have a good idea what they'll go off, but I thought she'd be much bigger - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

runners.spotlight: 8yo who made it 5-16 over fences when bouncing back with a clearcut win at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) two weeks ago; up 6lb but she hit a personal best last time and is a big player again if her stamina holds out on this step up 3m.

stable_tour.quote: She won really nicely at Chepstow's big meeting last month and she's on her winter break now. We'll get her back for a spring campaign. She's a nice mare and will win more races. 20-11-25

She's going chasing this season and we're hoping she can progress up to competing in Listed mares' novice chases. She'll need to improve but there's some 0-120s and hopefully she'd be ready in time for those. 12-10-23

runners.comment: Back over fences after wind surgery with a second at Fakenham last month; possibilities
runners.name: Mars Harper

quotes.race: Guinness Beginners Chase
quotes.quote: This was probably the race I should have gone for in the first place but Mars Harper came out of Tuesday's race well - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

quotes.race: Armatas Fire & Security Ltd Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Mars Harper did it nicely. He had a good look when he got to the front but he won well. He got a nice run through. He has plenty of ability and I was only keeping him up to it. I still had plenty of horse from the back of the last and was always holding the second - Luke Dempsey, rider.

runners.spotlight: Left Gordon Elliott after disappointing hurdle run last autumn; well beaten again on stable debut in March but, after wind surgery, he returned to chasing with a good second at Fakenham (3m, good) 19 days ago; has possibilities if he can build on that but his last win was in 2023.

stable_tour.quote: Has won five times and the saddle slipped at Limerick the other day. Might need to come down the handicap a little but, but hopefully there is another one or two in him. Somewhere between two and a half miles and three miles is his best trip and he handles all sorts of ground. 28-10-24

runners.comment: Fair effort over hurdles latest but he's 0-12 over fences and fell on his penultimate run
runners.name: Walking On Air

prev_owners.owner: J Carthy Mrs P Shanahan & D Tabor

quotes.race: Start Your RacingTV Free Trial Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Walking On Air's dam stayed and Nico says this fella will stay. He's nice, but had some hold-ups - no big problems - and he's going to be spectacular. He'll jump a fence and might be very exciting in a year or two. Nico says he'll go two and a half, but he'll need another run before the festival. He could go somewhere with a penalty, although there is the Sidney Banks, but we've others for that - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Back over hurdles with respectable fifth of 15 in Class 2 event at Haydock (3m, good) two weeks ago; 5lb lower back over fences but he's 0-12 in this sphere and he fell at Ayr on his penultimate run; down the list.

stable_tour.quote: He's a horse I've always liked and he'll be very good one day when we can get him right, but he's had only one run over fences and this would be a tough ask. He's a very big horse, and with big horses trouble is easier to come across than with little horses, but we may try to get him out very soon with a view to the festival. 19-02-24

runners.comment: Four-time chaser winner but he looks weighted near best and is untried beyond 2m5f
runners.name: Alien Storm
runners.spotlight: Ran respectably when third of five over hurdles at regular haunt Plumpton (2m4f, good) last month; better known as a chaser these days but he looks weighted near best off this mark and is untried beyond 2m5f; has some work to do back in this sphere.

stable_tour.quote: He started the season off in style with an easy win at Plumpton in a 2m novice hurdle and was a one-length second to Attacca under a penalty at Kempton. I thought he would run well going back to Kempton at Christmas but he found the soft ground too much and could not pick up his feet in it. The experience will have taught him plenty and he will have plenty of decent opportunities in the spring when the ground dries a little. The handicapper dropped him 2lb to 123 and I think this progressive youngster is above standard and, like so many of his family, he will be better on better ground. 11-01-23

runners.comment: Well handicapped on his Huntingdon win last March but he's struggled since; down the list
runners.name: Lounge Lizard

quotes.race: Prestige Developments John Bigg "Oxo" Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Lounge Lizard was unfortunate because it absolutely bucketed it last time and he doesn't like that wet ground. I'm not sure if he didn't get a bit bored in the closing stages today. He jumped very nicely today and the plan is Aintree. We got as far as declaring him last year, but unfortunately he went lame 24 hours before because he banged himself. He ran in the Becher last term and ran well, jumped well and enjoyed it, but it was very soft ground and he never got home. We set out our stall to run in the race last year and again this year - Henry Daly, trainer.

quotes.race: John Bigg ''Oxo'' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: We'll aim at Lounge Lizard at the Topham. He ran a corker at Cheltenham in January and I don't think Huntingdon suits him all that well. Aintree will suit him better and he loved jumping around there before - Henry Daly, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Four-time chase winner at up to 3m1f; well handicapped on his Huntingdon win for Henry Daly last March but he's struggled since including in two runs for new yard this spring; ran well to a point at Ludlow last time but he was on the retreat when he fell and others preferred.

16:45.race_name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Racecourse Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Won in cheekpieces on handicap debut at Ffos Las; up 6lb but she's open to more progress
runners.name: Camshaft
runners.spotlight: Big improvement with cheekpieces added on handicap debut when beating 11 rivals at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft) last month; up 6lb but she knuckled down well last time and this unexposed mare shaped as though this new trip should be within range; strongly respected.

runners.comment: Improved form with tongue-tie added when scoring at Newton Abbot; big player again up 5lb
runners.name: Jetty May
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the fifth attempt over hurdles when keeping on well for a 16-1 win at Newton Abbot (2m6f, good) last month; up 5lb but she responded well to a tongue-tie last time and is open to more progress at this new trip; key player.

runners.breeder: Ecurie Des Vives Terres & Pa Ouvry
runners.comment: Reappeared with a good second at Ludlow (2m5f) and has claims if she can build on that
runners.name: La Cantate
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-7 but she returned after 276 days off with a promising second in a Ludlow handicap (2m5f, good) last month; nudged up 2lb but she stayed on well last time and has possibilities on this step up to 2m7f.

runners.comment: 0-12 over hurdles but she's consistent and was runner-up at Taunton latest; in the mix
runners.name: Newmill Getaway
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner who is 0-12 over hurdles but she has a solid record in handicaps for current yard and was runner-up at Taunton (3m, good) in March; should go well again off an unchanged mark and she's in the mix.

runners.comment: Showed signs of a revival when third at Uttoxeter (2m4f) last Saturday; could be dangerous
runners.name: Victoria Milano
runners.spotlight: Won two novice hurdles (2m3f/2m) for Alistair Ralph in 2023-24; struggled in first three runs for current yard but she showed signs of a revival when third of 12 at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last Saturday; was no match for the first two in that race but her mark continues to fall and she looks worth another try at this trip; could be dangerous.

stable_tour.quote: She hasn't found her form this season and she's going for a wind op as we just felt she was missing something. She ran well at Uttoxeter and then travelled very well at Bangor last time, but didn't get home. She had been very consistent, but we've been missing that Sandown form from last season. If we can get her back she's definitely one to keep on side. 19-02-25

runners.comment: Fair effort when fourth on Fontwell reappearance (3m2f) in March and she's not ruled out
runners.name: After Midnight
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Donald Smith
runners.spotlight: Ten-race maiden but she rallied on her Fontwell reappearance (3m2f, soft; cheekpieces) in March and was not beaten far in fourth; this is a deeper race but she's unexposed as a stayer and is not ruled out off 1lb lower than last time.

runners.comment: Won at Fontwell last spring but she's been disappointing since and has a lot to prove
runners.name: Pooleys Promise
runners.spotlight: Won a Fontwell handicap (3m, good) for Ryan Potter last May but she's been disappointing since including in two runs for new yard this spring; mark continues to fall but she was pulled up at Taunton last time and has a lot to prove; hood is added and tongue-tie is removed.

runners.comment: 8yo who struggled last year and needs a major revival after a break
runners.name: Faerie Cutlass
runners.spotlight: Won at Ludlow (3m, good to soft) in November 2024 but she struggled last year and was beaten 20l at Sedgefield when last seen in November; now 4lb lower than for her last success but she needs a major revival after a break.

runners.comment: Handicap newcomer but she needs a transformation on this big step up in trip
runners.name: After The Ball
runners.spotlight: 0-8 in Irish points and she hasn't shown a great deal in three hurdle runs (2m, good) this spring; now goes handicapping but this is competitive and she needs a transformation on this big step up in trip

runners.comment: 0-13 over hurdles and she struggled off a tough mark back in a handicap latest; opposable
runners.name: Porridge
runners.spotlight: 0-13 over hurdles; ran a big race at a massive price when fourth in a Fontwell maiden (2m3f, good to soft) last month but her mark shot up 41lb after that and she struggled back in a handicap at Fontwell (2m5f) last week; opposable.

17:20.race_name: Wrexham Evening On Friday 26th June Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elim') (GBB)

runners.comment: Close second on Sedgefield debut in March and she sets the standard on that form
runners.name: Bourbon Girl
runners.spotlight: 11th foal; half-sister to useful hurdler Master Malt and two bumper winners; 10-1 for a four-runner bumper at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) in March but she ran well to finish a close second; that was a promising debut and she sets the standard on that form.

runners.comment: Ex-French 4yo who won on recent stable debut at Fontwell; respected under a penalty
runners.name: Magnifix Du Moulin
runners.spotlight: Close third in a 1m4f French bumper on soft ground in October when tongue tied; weak 9-1 shot on recent stable debut at Fontwell (2m1f, good) but she overcame some traffic issues before scoring with something in hand; has a penalty but she has a useful pedigree and looks a good prospect.

runners.comment: Point winner and she's a sister to smart bumper winner; needs close look on rules debut
runners.name: Phantom Of Delight
runners.spotlight: Bought for £30,000 after winning an Irish point (soft/heavy) in January; sister to a smart bumper winner and she's also a half-sister to a useful 2m hurdler; plenty to like on pedigree and she needs a close in market on rules debut.

runners.comment: Tailed off at Doncaster in her last run in 2024 and has something to prove on comeback
runners.name: Do Wah Diddy
runners.spotlight: Second of five on Huntingdon debut (2m, good) in November 2024 but she was tailed off at Doncaster 18 days later; on the sidelines since and has something to prove back after a long absence.

runners.comment: Has several bumper winners in her pedigree and she's an interesting newcomer
runners.name: Lady Coco
runners.spotlight: Half-sister to winners Choccabloc (bumper/2m5f hurdle) and My Bobby's Lass (2m3f/2m4f hurdle); dam bumper/2m1f hurdle winner, closely related to 2m7f/3m1f hurdle winner As I See It, out of bumper/smart 2m-2m5f hurdle winner; yard has been firing in winners recently and she's an interesting newcomer.

runners.comment: Yard 3-47 in bumpers in recent years and others look more likely
runners.name: Molly Hastings
runners.spotlight: 30,000euros 3yo; fifth foal; half-sister to 2m/2m1f hurdle winner Telecon; dam placed 2m-2m2f hurdles/chase in France, sister to bumper/useful 2m-2m7f hurdle/chase winner The Polomoche, half-sister to useful 2m3f/2m6f hurdle winner Lessons In Milan; yard 3-47 in bumpers in recent years and others look more likely.

runners.comment: 6,000euros foal; yard not known for bumper winners and she could be a longer-term prospect
runners.name: Anniespatient
runners.spotlight: 6,000euros foal; first foal; dam 2m hurdle winner, out of bumper/2m-2m5f hurdle winning sister to useful bumper and 2m3f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Twelve Roses; yard not known for bumper winners and she could be a longer-term prospect.

runners.comment: Yard 0-13 in bumpers last season and she could be one for later on
runners.name: Maybellino
runners.spotlight: Eighth foal; half-sister to 2m3f hurdle winner Samtara; dam unraced sister to bumper and 2m6f-3m2f hurdle/chase winner Georgian King, half-sister to bumper/3m1f hurdle winner Madame Jasmine; yard 0-13 in bumpers last season and she could be one for later on.

runners.comment: Has fair target to aim at on debut and is best watched unless market suggests otherwise
runners.name: Liberty Leader
runners.spotlight: First foal; dam 2m4f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to smart bumper and 2m hurdle/chase winner Libberty Hunter; has fair target to aim at on debut and is best watched unless market suggests otherwise.

runners.comment: Has quite a bit of stamina in pedigree but she needs checking in market on debut
runners.name: Bonnie Lazarevic
runners.spotlight: Third foal; dam useful and prolific bumper/2m-3m1f hurdle/chase winner, closely related to winners Letterpress (2m/2m1f hurdle) and Belle Empress (2m6f hurdle/3m6f chase), half-sister to useful 2m3f-2m5f chase winner Fistral Beach; has quite a bit of stamina in pedigree and market should guide on debut.

runners.comment: Yard 21% in bumpers in recent years and she needs watching in market on debut
runners.name: Pearl Knot
runners.spotlight: Third foal; half-sister to 3m chase winner Pearl Island; dam 2m6f-3m hurdle winner, sister to 3m-3m5f chase winner Bretney, closely related to useful 2m4f-4m hurdle/chase winner Captain Cattistock, family of top 2m chaser Pearlyman; yard 21% in bumpers in recent years and she needs watching in market on debut.

13:35.race_name: Cartmel Sticky Toffee Pudding Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Runner-up in maidens at Navan and Downpatrick; can progress further; in the mix
runners.name: Loch Cuan
runners.spotlight: Has made a positive start over hurdles, runner-up in maidens at Navan (2m) in February and Downpatrick (2m6f) 15 days ago; likely to progress further so in the mix.

runners.comment: Promising hurdling debut fourth at Ffos Las; has more to offer and rates a player
runners.name: Getaway Vic
runners.spotlight: Irish point/bumper scorer who made a promising start in this sphere when fourth of five in novice at Ffos Las (2m4f, good) 18 days ago, leading long way; cheekpieces added; has more to offer and rates a player.

stable_tour.quote: He won a bumper at Worcester last summer and was then placed in another. He might have one more bumper run before the end of the season and will go novice hurdling after that. I think he should end up being a nice horse. 26-03-25

runners.comment: Shaped well on first go over hurdles when third at Downpatrick; can take a step forward
runners.name: Hawks Rock
runners.spotlight: A fairly useful bumper performer; back from six months off when shaping well on his first go over hurdles to be third of seven in a novice at Downpatrick (2m6f, good) 15 days ago; can take a step forward in retained cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Solid third in 2m Hexham novice three weeks ago; she's no forlorn hope in a refitted hood
runners.name: Lipstick Traces
runners.spotlight: Fair bumper performer who has shown similar form in this sphere, finishing third of nine in 2m Hexham novice three weeks ago; she's no forlorn hope in a refitted hood.

runners.comment: Last of eight in Kelso bumper latest; more is needed now sent hurdling
runners.name: Presentandcorrect
runners.spotlight: Fair form shown when third in Kelso bumper in February but came in last of eight in similar company there the following month; more needed now sent hurdling.

runners.comment: Failed to complete in four hurdles runs for Daisy Hitchins; more required for new yard
runners.name: Stavanger Rose
runners.spotlight: Failed to complete all four runs over hurdles for Daisy Hitchins, although she was still in third when falling at the last in 2m6f novice at Newton Abbot last month; changed hands for 2,000gns since and more required for her new handler.

runners.comment: Maiden pointer; last of three finishers in April; goes hurdling but others appeal more
runners.name: Howsmenoftomorro
runners.spotlight: Maiden pointer who came in last of three finishers in April; goes hurdling now but others appeal more.

runners.comment: Maiden pointer who came in last of four in April; much more required on her hurdling debut
runners.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners.spotlight: Maiden pointer who came in last of four in April; much more required on her hurdling debut.

runners.comment: 0-9 and pulled up in 2m Wetherby h'cap hurdle in February; it's easy to look elsewhere
runners.name: Road To Rosley
runners.spotlight: 0-9 and tried in cheekpieces when pulled up in 2m Wetherby handicap hurdle in February; it's easy to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: 0-19 and was last to finish in a 2m5f handicap at Market Rasen last month
runners.name: Raincloud
runners.spotlight: 0-19 and she was last to finish in a 2m5f handicap at Market Rasen last month; others more persuasive.

runners.breeder: E A R L Les Bordes De Mornay & M Gerard Hanquiez
runners.comment: Winning Irish pointer; has shaped well both bumper runs; interesting prospect. NON RUNNER
runners.name: Keops Des Bordes
runners.spotlight: Winning Irish pointer; shaped well on his bumper debut when second at Warwick in December 2024 and again when fourth of nine in similar company at Ayr last month, travelling smoothly for a long way on his first run for 16 months; interesting prospect now going hurdling.NON-RUNNER

stable_tour.quote: He's another nice novice hurdle prospect who finished second in his bumper last December. We thought he might win that day as he'd been doing everything well at home, but he came up against a nice horse [No Drama This End], so we weren't disappointed. He looks every inch a stayer who has a real long-term future as a chaser. I think I'll be very excited about him this time next year. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Remains winless but comes here in decent nick; place prospects back in maiden company
runners.name: Woodythewoodpecker
runners.spotlight: Remains winless but comes here in decent nick, having finished third of seven in 25.5f handicap at Hereford last month; place prospects once more back in maiden company.

runners.comment: Easily landed gamble at Newton Abbot latest; this C&D winner merits serious consideration
runners.name: Belle Le Grand
runners.spotlight: Back on the up (in first-time cheekpieces) when easily landing a gamble in 2m1f handicap at Newton Abbot 17 days ago; up 7lb but runner-up has gone in since so this C&D winner merits serious consideration in retained headgear.

stable_tour.quote: She won twice over hurdles for us earlier in the year but found the soft ground against her at Hexham on Friday and ran below par. We'll find some better ground for her through the winter and hopefully in the spring there'll be some nicer races for her. 10-11-25

runners.comment: Easy winner at Fakenham; good third at Newbury (Listed) so enters calculations after break
runners.name: Zahra Dodville
runners.spotlight: Ex-French filly; scored easily on her debut for James Owen in 2m Fakenham juvenile hurdle in October and backed it up with a good third of 12 in Listed event at Newbury (2m) the following month; off since but yard continues to go very well so she must enter calculations.

stable_tour.quote: She's come from France and will be one for those National Hunt juvenile hurdles. She shapes up well and looks like a nice addition to the yard. 24-10-25

runners.comment: Respectable fifth at Killarney (Listed) latest; remains with potential on handicap debut
runners.name: Dunsy Rock

quotes.race: Treo Eile Supporting Racehorse Aftercare Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: She was very honest, jumped great and handled the ground well. Dunsy Rock was good. On better ground she could probably go up in trip but, on that sort of ground, two miles is okay for her - Jack Kennedy, jockey.

runners.spotlight: Off the mark at just the second attempt in 2m Fairyhouse maiden in February and not disgraced when fifth in 2m1f Listed event at Killarney two weeks ago; remains with potential now going handicapping.

runners.comment: Dual C&D scorer and step back in right direction with Hexham fourth latest; possibilities
runners.name: Winds Of Winter

quotes.race: Burlington Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Pro/Am Race)
quotes.quote: We knew there was going to be plenty of pace on and that set the race up perfectly for her, because Winds Of Winter travels away really well and just needs something to aim at - Thomasina Eyston, winning jockey talking to Racing TV.

runners.spotlight: Dual C&D scorer in first half of 2025; lightly raced since but she took a step back in the right direction when fourth at Hexham (2m) three weeks ago; possibilities off a slipping mark.

runners.comment: Promising start for new yard with Aintree third (2m4f) last week; player off the same mark
runners.name: My Chiquita

quotes.race: Alfred Brown Worsted Mills Ltd Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: My Chiquita travelled a lot better today. We'll probably put her away as she wants better ground and we could wait for the mares' meeting at Cheltenham in April - Ben Brookhouse, trainer.

quotes.race: JTC Pizzalicious Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: My Chiquita is still a big baby, but it's great we could win with her as we lost her half-brother. We originally were going to put her away as we thought the ground would be wrong, but when we saw it was like it was we schooled the hell out of her - Ben Brookhouse, trainer.

runners.spotlight: A fairly useful 2m4f hurdles winner for Ben Brookhouse; made a promising start for her new yard after eight months off when third of eight over 2m4f at Aintree eight days ago; she should strip sharper here and rates a player off the same mark.

stable_tour.quote: She's 2-2 for us over hurdles and is having a break as she wants better ground. She won well at Sedgefield and Wetherby and we'll get her ready for the mares' meeting at Cheltenham in April. She'll have a couple of options there, either a handicap hurdle or Listed novice hurdle. It's all about building a pedigree with her to go on as a broodmare. 30-11-23

runners.comment: Low-mileage mare; good second at Carlisle in February; well in the mix after a break
runners.name: Kientzheim

quotes.race: 100% Racing TV Profits Back To Racing Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were very happy with Kientzheim. I think she might just be better going that way around [right-handed]. She struggled to cope at Wetherby, being a little bit free in behind, and here she was able to prick her ears in front and relax. Stepping up in trip too, everything seemed to click today. The Wetherby race had set her up nicely, although the takeaway wasn't really a lack of fitness - more that we needed to change direction and how we rode her. The way she jumps a hurdle, I wouldn't be surprised if we let her see a fence at some point. She's very straightforward and a nice horse, as they always are when JP [McManus, owner] sends one. It's great to have one from him and we're very lucky to get opportunities to train horses like that - Ben Haslam, trainer.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes "Gaffer Of All Accas" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kientzheim is related to Epatante, so it's lovely as she's a sweet filly too. She jumped really well until they really kicked on, but she's a novice. She'll have to grow up a bit more, but I'd think she can go up to some nicer races now. This was a lovely race to start in - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Has made a positive start for her current yard, scoring at Market Rasen (2m4f) in November and backing it up with a good second of 11 at Carlisle (2m1f) in February; well in the mix after a break with few miles on the clock.

stable_tour.quote: She's closely related to Epatante and is in good form ? we like her a lot. She's neat and has been running in some pretty good AQPS Flat races, but we'll find a lot more about her here. 23-12-24

runners.comment: In good form until last of ten at Sandown four weeks ago; might bounce back though
runners.name: Tour Ovalie

quotes.race: Radnor Hills Mares' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tour Ovalie just wins races. It's always tactical with her, she has to be delivered late and it's difficult to go up in class, but horses like her are hard to find - Evan Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Racing TV Club Day Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Herring Queen Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tour Ovalie is just a joy. She's progressive and enjoys racing. I think we're all guilty of not running them enough. She can only be a novice for one season, and we ran her because if you took the first two in the betting out, it was a shallow race. I think she's run to her mark. A lot of them haven't had the chance to run in handicaps, and handicappers going back into novice hurdles are just a bit hardier. I think they've probably underperformed somewhat. She's a good, tough, genuine mare, and I have a lot of time for her. I do love a trier - Evan Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Play Coral 'Racing-Super-Series' For Free Mares' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Now we know how Isabel rides Tour Ovalie, it makes it easier to watch as an owner as she leaves her late, and you've got to leave her very late, but she runs beautifully - Andrew Strong, owner.

quotes.race: EK Mowers & Machinery Mares' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tour Ovalie has been going the right way lately and that was very pleasing. She's improved with time. She used to be a bit hot but she has learned to race the right way. We've always had plenty of belief in her and she's a smashing mare for the owners as she's so consistent. Isabel gets on well with her and we'll quietly step up in grade - Evan Williams, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Resumed winning ways at Ludlow (2m) in December and in good form until finishing last of ten in 2m4f Sandown handicap four weeks ago; the sort who might bounce back though.

stable_tour.quote: She made the frame in two bumpers in the spring and is a smashing type. She'll want some give in the ground but I'm not sure whether she'll go straight over hurdles or have another bumper run. 02-11-23

A genuine mare with a habit of winning, just the kind of habit you want. She's basically a 2m hurdler and she's won six out of 20 in that discipline. I try to keep her in mares' races. She's on a mark of 118, which is just below her highest mark. I'm hoping she takes her consistency to Ludlow on Thursday. 14-01-26

runners.comment: Off for 17 months before finishing last on Newcastle AW recently; needs a big step forward
runners.name: Melinda

quotes.race: Athelstaneford Home Of The Saltire Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (Go North Grey Bomber Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I was delighted with Melinda as she got quite a good weight allowance with the mares' allowance and Alan's claim. She's always been a very natural jumper and I was very pleased with her. She's got plenty of scope and I'll imagine she'll be able to go on from there - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Made a winning start over hurdles in 2m Musselburgh juvenile in November 2024; had been off for 17 months before coming in last of five on Newcastle AW (1m4f) 22 days ago; needs to take a big step forward.

runners.comment: Back in good nick of late, third at Perth nine days ago; not out of things eased 2lb
runners.name: Magnolia
runners.spotlight: A dual 2m hurdles winner at Kelso last winter and back in good nick of late, finishing third of six at Perth (2m) nine days ago; not out of things off a 2lb lower mark.

runners.breeder: E A R L De Cordelles Et Al
runners.comment: Not at her best of late, remote Hexham second final run for Jennie Candlish; more needed
runners.name: Demoiselle Kap

quotes.race: Coming Soon betvickers.com Sports Betting Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Demoiselle Kap was pretty good on the whole even though the ground may have been a bit quick for her - Luke Scott, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Arabian Horse Bahrain Equine Products UK Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Demoiselle Kap jumped a lot better than I thought she would. She was very good at the ditch down the back then at the last down the back she came out of my hands and I knew she had loads left. We'll have to go up in grade now so we'll find out a lot more - Sean Quinlan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: Bagged a four-timer (around 2m) over hurdles/fences last winter; not at her best of late though and finished a remote second in 2m Hexham seller three weeks ago on her final run for Jennie Candlish; more needed in refitted cheekpieces for her new handler.

runners.comment: 2l third in 2025 renewal before winning a C&D Class 2 two days later; turn nearing again.
runners.name: Musique De Fee

quotes.race: Molson Coors Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Musique De Fee is so tough. I never run horses that quickly again and she looked really green on Saturday and like she was not having it, but she came out of it lively. She doesn't know how to lose, but I thought turning in we'd be second. Josh [Bryan, jockey] was tactically brilliant, and she stuck her neck out and had her head down when it really mattered - Georgina Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: DragonBet: Oncourse And Online Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I must say a big thank-you to Sean Bowen, who rode Musique De Fee six days ago. I rang him this morning and all he said was to kick on with her and he was right - Finn Lambert, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: 2l third in this race (good) last year for Georgina Nicholls when undone by two late mistakes, only to land a C&D Class 2 two days later (good to soft) off the same mark as today's; easily her best effort for new connections at Hereford latest (3m2f, good), and her turn is possibly nearing.

runners.comment: 2m6f maiden winner who didn't improve for 3m latest as expected; off since October.
runners.name: Penny Perfect
runners.spotlight: Looked like one for stayers' trips when taking a Downpatrick 2m6f maiden last summer (good), but unable to confirm that impression on her one run after; much the longest absent of these, and her mark is no gift.

runners.comment: No certainty to back up Perth near-miss; encouragement for stayers' trips on breeding.
runners.name: Tread Softly Now
runners.spotlight: Triple winner at up to 2m4f (soft and good); inconsistency tempers confidence in her backing up last month's Perth near-miss (2m4f, good; first-time visor retained), but has staying potential on breeding.

runners.breeder: Sir J Timpson & H D J Daly
runners.comment: Sharp left-handed track and good ground are positives; may stay this far.
runners.name: Keep On Cobbling
runners.spotlight: Well served by sharp left-handed tracks and good ground, winning at Stratford (2m maiden) and Sedgefield (2m5f handicap) last year; impression given when second at Warwick latest (2m5f) was that she'll stay further and that is partly backed up by pedigree.

runners.comment: Back below her last winning mark, and step up back beyond 3m looks the right move.
runners.name: Starlyte

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Go North Cab On Target Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I love racing because of the horses and Starlyte is the sort of horse I love. She's only tiny but she's so brave. You have to drop her in and let her pass horses and I'm delighted for the owners Allan and Anne Grant who've just got married - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Follow Thehawkponteland On Instagram Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Starlyte needs a fast-run two-and-a-half miles and she's the most game horse. It's her attitude that wins her races - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Few secrets left after 41 hurdles starts but back below her last winning mark again, and every outing so far this year has suggested that an extended run of races beyond 3m looks in order now; not without interest.

stable_tour.quote: She came to us from the Flat and made a flying start by winning a 2m4½f Newcastle handicap hurdle. We'll keep her to that trip with a view to going up to 3m later. She desperately needs good ground and is ready to go as soon as things dry out. 25-01-23

runners.comment: Bit better again at Ayr last time; wouldn't be convinced that Cartmel is her track.
runners.name: Pinot Rouge
runners.spotlight: Below par since last June's Hexham win off 2lb higher (3m, good to soft) until reviving, up to a point, with last month's Ayr Class 2 fourth; has to show that a sharp track is what's wanted, though.

runners.comment: Dual 2m1f novice winner here last summer; effectiveness beyond 2m3f has yet to be tested.
runners.name: Bittalemon

quotes.race: Rathbones Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's absolutely fantastic. We have a lovely local owner and Bittalemon is a tough little cookie. She'd probably be better on softer ground but we're very pleased with her. She's an absolute queen to train. She's very straightforward but it took her quite a while to learn how to jump, probably two or three months.   The owner of the horse is quite a stats man, and she's been the best jumper in every race she has run in which is why we made the running today. We've put her jumping to good use and it's all worked out - James Moffatt, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Dual 2m1f novice winner here last summer (good to soft and good); well below that level twice after, albeit once in Listed company; effectiveness beyond 2m3f has yet to be tested.

15:20.race_name: William Hill Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Pretty useful in two hurdle runs (County/Swinton) for new yard; big chance back chasing
runners.name: Tellherthename

quotes.race: Arkle Finance EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We are back on track. We turned a lot of stones to try and find out what happened at Aintree. We found a few little bits and bobs, but nothing that put us out for that long as you could see. I was just keen to get his season back on track before we dwelt on it for too long. The ground there was soft enough, and it is not the good to soft that they have advertised, but Tellherthename has handled it very well. He is an unbelievably class horse. That now gives him his fourth run so he has got the option of the Betfair Hurdle, but the ground would have to be spot on for that otherwise we will go straight to the Supreme with him. I think he is a class horse with gears galore and I sometimes think they are best fresh. They go such a gallop in that race (Supreme) and if you are anything but absolutely ready for the day then you might get flat footed - Ben Pauling, trainer.

runners.spotlight: Both wins came at Huntingdon when trained by Ben Pauling; made his stable debut in the County Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival, when not beaten far, and he wasn't disgraced when hooded and held up out the back in the Swinton at Haydock (favourite) two weeks ago; this will feel like a drop in the ocean in comparison and, although turned over at a short price last October in his only chase, he should make light work of these two rivals on his return to fences.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good horse who'll be making his debut for us, having joined us just after Christmas. He's had a bit of a chequered career but he'll go there super-fresh and his handicap mark doesn't look beyond him, although this will be a big ask. 17-02-26

runners.comment: Made a promising debut over fences when fourth at Wexford 16 days ago.
runners.name: Half A Chance

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle (IRE Incentive Race)
